ANNA is not a bank but an e-money proposition: its Mastercard and e-money services are issued by PayrNet Limited, authorised by the Financial Conduct Authority for electronic money service activities (FCA FRN 900594), and its Account Information Services are provided under agency of TrueLayer (FCA FRN 901096). Within UK Open Banking, ANNA is a consumer / third-party provider (TPP) rather than an account-holding ASPSP or a CMA9 mandated bank - it uses TrueLayer's Data and Payments APIs for external account aggregation, automatic VAT calculation, and QR-code "pay by bank" collection. ANNA publishes no public developer portal, no Open Data API, and no OBIE Read/Write (AIS/PIS/CBPII) API surface of its own; its public GitHub organisation hosts open-source engineering tooling (asyncio, aiohttp, and Postgres libraries) rather than product APIs.

providers.name: Prodigy Finance
providers.description: Prodigy Finance is a fintech lender providing collateral-free, no-cosigner postgraduate education loans to international master's students at top business, engineering, and STEM schools worldwide. Founded in 2007 and headquartered in London, it uses a borderless, forward-looking credit model based on a borrower's projected future earnings rather than local credit history, funding students from more than 150 countries. Prodigy Finance operates consumer web and mobile (iOS/Android) applications, an accounts portal, and a customer help center, but publishes no public developer API, SDKs, or developer portal at this time.

providers.name: Tranched
providers.description: Tranched is a London-based fintech building an embedded, on-chain securitisation platform that connects fintech lenders and loan originators directly to professional investors. Its "Deep Tokenisation" approach represents loans as on-chain tokens governed by Smart Loan Agreements and automated waterfall contracts, letting originators structure and launch institutional-grade asset-based financing transactions up to 90% faster and at lower cost than traditional securitisation, with automated compliance, reporting, and monitoring. Tranched connects to a lender's loan management system via API integration to retrieve the data required for assigning and monitoring loans. Founded in 2023 by Clement Larrue and Michael Elalouf, the company raised a $3.4M pre-seed round led by Speedinvest in November 2024.

providers.name: Sumary
providers.description: Sumary is a Denmark-based fintech building an AI-native workflow engine for finance and accounting teams. Its platform layers autonomous accounting agents, anomaly detection, and on-demand reporting over a company's existing accounting systems — automating reconciliations and variance explanations, validating transactions to catch errors and potential fraud, and generating management reports, margin analyses, and cost breakdowns for bookkeepers, controllers, CFOs, and finance leaders. The company raised a $4.2M (27M DKK) pre-seed round led by byFounders with participation from Partech and Tenity. No public API, developer portal, or OpenAPI surface has been located; this profile captures the company's web, trust, and domain-security surface.

providers.name: Drivio
providers.description: Drivio (Drivio Technologies Pvt Ltd) is a tech-enabled, omni-channel two-wheeler financing marketplace in India that connects motorcycle, scooter, and electric-vehicle buyers with banks and NBFCs. Founded in 2022 by Saurabh Tripathi and Ankur Bhardwaj and headquartered in the Delhi NCR region (Gurugram / New Delhi), the platform offers EMI calculators, instant eligibility checks, curated finance offers, vehicle comparison, and same-day loan approval and disbursal through lending partners including IDFC First Bank, Bajaj Auto Credit, L&T Financial Services, HDB Financial Services, Moneyplus Financial Services, and Arthmate. Drivio is an ISO/IEC 27001 certified company and is backed by 500 Global.

providers.name: Brigit
providers.description: Brigit is a consumer financial technology company whose mobile app helps people manage everyday money with instant cash advances of up to $500 with no credit check, interest, or late fees, a Credit Builder account, and a Finance Helper for budgeting, spending analysis, bill tracking, and overdraft prediction. The app also bundles identity-theft protection and a deals-and-offers marketplace, and is offered on paid monthly subscription tiers. Brigit reports more than 12 million users. This API Evangelist profile is a company lead surfaced from venture-capital portfolios (Canaan Partners, DCM Ventures, Lightspeed Venture Partners); Brigit is a direct-to-consumer app and does not currently publish a public developer API, so this record is enriched at the identity and web-property level.

providers.name: Clearco
providers.description: Clearco (formerly Clearbanc) is a Toronto-based fintech that provides non-dilutive, revenue-based working capital to ecommerce and direct-to-consumer brands. Founders connect the sales, advertising and banking platforms they already run on — Shopify, Amazon, Stripe, PayPal, Square, BigCommerce — and Clearco underwrites from that data, funding inventory and marketing spend as a cash advance or as invoice funding, in as little as 24 hours, without equity dilution. The company was founded in 2015 as Clearbanc, rebranded to Clearco in 2021, and reports having deployed more than $3.3 billion to over 10,000 businesses.

providers.name: GreenFi
providers.description: GreenFi is a climate-focused consumer financial technology company — the rebranded continuation of Aspiration's consumer banking arm. It offers a combined checking and savings account, high-yield savings with goal-based "Savings Pods", a debit card, a GreenFi Plus subscription tier, investing through its Redwood fund, and a cash-back Marketplace of sustainable brands, alongside impact programs such as Plant Your Change, tree planting and carbon offsetting. GreenFi is a financial technology company, not a bank; banking services and the debit card are provided by Coastal Community Bank, Member FDIC. Aspiration spun its consumer unit out in 2024 to Mission Financial Partners, LLC, which rebranded it GreenFi in April 2025; Coastal Financial Corporation acquired the GreenFi brand in January 2026. It is a separate company from Aspiration Partners, Inc., the enterprise carbon business that entered Chapter 11. GreenFi ships iOS, Android and web applications to end users and publishes no public developer program, API reference, or machine-readable specification.

providers.name: Model ML
providers.description: Model ML is an AI-native platform for financial services that embeds an agentic "finance agent" into the tools professionals already use — Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook, its own app, and a firm's internal systems. It automates deliverables through Workflows, runs compound-intelligence analysis via Grids, performs document review and risk assessment, captures information with a Notetaker, and answers questions through Chat and agentic dashboards backed by real-time data connections. It targets investment banking, consulting, private equity and credit, and asset and wealth management. Model ML is a fintech company backed by QED Investors. The company publishes a trust center and a security program (ISO/IEC 27001, SOC 2 Type II, GDPR) but does not currently expose a public developer API, SDK, or API documentation surface.

providers.name: Oradian
providers.description: Oradian is an AI-native, cloud-based core banking platform that helps banks, lenders, microfinance institutions, and fintechs in Asia, Africa, and Europe replace legacy core systems and launch, operate, and scale modern banking services from the cloud. Its product, Instafin, is built API-first around an open data model, an extensible architecture, and a native Model Context Protocol surface, exposing capabilities such as ledgers, transactions, deposits, cards, loans, and applications through stable, versioned APIs, webhooks, and event streams. Oradian is independently audited to SOC 2 and ISO 27001 and aligns to CBN, BSP, and OJK regulatory requirements.

providers.name: Percent
providers.description: Percent is a private credit platform that opens privately negotiated loans and debt financing from non-bank lenders to accredited and institutional investors, specialty-finance borrowers, and debt underwriters. The marketplace lets individual accredited investors access institutional-grade private credit deals (asset-backed securities and corporate loans) with entry points from $500 for direct deals, $5,000 for diversified Blended Notes, and $50,000 for Separately Managed Accounts, alongside a secondary market for eligible positions. Percent Securities, LLC is a U.S. registered broker-dealer and member of FINRA and SIPC; Percent Advisors LLC provides advisory services. Investor, borrower, and manager workflows run through authenticated portals; the public percent.com surface is marketing, education, performance, and regulatory disclosure. Percent has no public developer API — programmatic/deal-level access is not published.

providers.name: Scripbox
providers.description: Scripbox is an Indian direct-to-consumer wealth management and mutual fund investment platform operated by Scripbox Wealth Managers Private Limited. It helps families pursue financial freedom through personalized mutual fund recommendations shaped by expert advisors and data-backed algorithms, offering both regular (commission-based, zero monthly fee) and direct (advisory-fee) plans. The platform bundles portfolio construction and monitoring, financial planning, goal-based investing, tax-saving tools such as its Smart Withdraw algorithm, and multi-channel support. As of this enrichment pass, Scripbox operates purely as a consumer application and publishes no public developer API, developer portal, SDKs, or machine-readable API specifications.

providers.name: VALID8 Financial
providers.description: VALID8 Financial is a Verified Financial Intelligence (VFI) platform founded in 2017 in Seattle that turns raw banking evidence and accounting records into reconciled, evidential-grade transaction data for forensic accountants, CPA firms, law firms, bankruptcy trustees, and government investigators. The AI-powered platform automates extraction and verification of financial evidence across use cases including forensic investigations, financial crime, expert witness support, transaction advisory, bankruptcy and restructuring, and family law. A Techstars portfolio company, VALID8 is SOC 2 Type II audited, HIPAA compliant, and GDPR aligned with a Vanta-hosted trust center, but does not currently publish a developer portal or public API documentation; customers sign in through regional portals (us/ca/eu/uk/aus.valid8.io).

providers.name: Black Unicorn Factory
providers.description: Black Unicorn Factory (BUF) is a Los Angeles based pre-IPO business accelerator that prepares companies led by founders from underrepresented communities for direct listings on national stock exchanges, positioning equity rather than debt as the route to capital. Its programs run a four-step readiness pathway — foundation and readiness assessment, compliance and corporate structure, SEC filing and disclosure, and market readiness — alongside the New Black Wall Street pre-IPO program and the Follow Me For Equity (FMFE) platform, an iOS and Android application through which individuals earn stock in participating pre-IPO companies by completing verified social engagement tasks instead of investing cash. Black Unicorn Factory is a private company whose shares appear on secondary marketplaces; it publishes no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or machine-readable API contract.

providers.name: Zarna
providers.description: Zarna builds autonomous AI associates for private capital firms — private equity, growth equity, private credit, family offices, and investment banks. The platform captures deal information from CIMs, emails, meetings, CRMs, and virtual data rooms into a structured institutional memory, then runs a swarm of specialized agents (Scribe for capture and logging, Memo for screening memos and briefs, Analyst for mandate-fit scoring, and Experts for warm-intro network mapping) that deliver finished work directly into Outlook, Teams, and Slack. Zarna integrates with 30+ deal tools including DealCloud, Affinity, Salesforce, and SharePoint, deploys into VPC or on-premises single-tenant infrastructure, and is SOC 2 Type II certified. A Y Combinator Fall 2025 company founded by an ex-AEA Investors team.

providers.name: Dock
providers.description: Dock is a Latin American financial technology infrastructure provider — formerly Conductor Technology — that delivers card issuing and processing, core banking, digital accounts and wallets, Pix instant payments, bank slips, acquiring, loyalty/benefits and transactional anti-fraud from a single cloud-native platform marketed as Dock One. Dock operates in Brazil as a payment institution regulated by the Banco Central do Brasil (bank code 301) and states that it serves more than 400 companies across 11 countries, processes roughly R$1.4 trillion in annual card volume and supports around 70 million active digital accounts. Its API estate is branded Caradhras and is reached through the api.caradhras.io gateway; the developer reference at developers.dock.tech is a private ReadMe hub that redirects anonymous visitors to a login, and the previously public Caradhras reference at lighthouse.dock.tech no longer resolves.

providers.name: Ethos
providers.description: Ethos is a US digital life insurance company headquartered in San Francisco, founded in 2016, offering term life, whole life, and indexed universal life policies through an online, mostly no-medical-exam application flow. Ethos operates as a technology-driven insurance agency, distributing policies underwritten by carriers such as Ameritas, Banner Life (Legal & General America), Protective, and TruStage. Coverage is available in 49 states and Washington, D.C., with term policies offered for 10, 15, 20, 30, and 40 year durations and face amounts ranging from $15,000 to $3 million. The company has raised over $400 million from investors including Goldman Sachs, SoftBank, GV, Sequoia, and Accel, and is widely cited as one of the leading insurtech companies modernizing the life insurance buying experience. Ethos exposes a Partnership API that lets approved business partners embed quoting, identity validation, instant underwriting, application capture, billing, and signed policy issuance directly into their own products. The Partnership API uses bearer-token authentication tied to a partner API key and per-applicant session, and consolidates steps such as identity validation and quoting into combined endpoints to enable instant decisioning. There is no public, self-serve OpenAPI specification, SDK, or developer signup; access requires a partnership agreement with Ethos. Ethos's only material open-source footprint is the ethos-design-system React component library on GitHub.

providers.name: Fintor
providers.description: Fintor is an enterprise software company that provides an agentic AI workforce for mortgage lending operations. Its purpose-built, autonomous AI agents execute mortgage workflows end to end - from application through closing - with human-in-the-loop oversight, integrating with existing loan origination systems (LOS), CRMs, and contact centers rather than replacing them. Product modules include a Loan Officer Assistant (document intake, borrower communication, gap analysis), a Processor Assistant (third-party orders, condition tracking, disclosures), Predictive Conditioning, a Closing Agent, and a Manager Assistant for forecasting and reporting. Fintor ships pre-built connectors for Encompass, Salesforce, Five9, Polly, and Blend, exposes documented API integrations, and is SOC 2 Type II certified with encryption, RBAC, approval chains, and audit logging.

providers.name: Precium
providers.description: Precium is a South African fintech that provides local payment infrastructure for global merchants expanding into Africa. Its enterprise-grade platform handles payment processing across cards, instant EFT, mobile wallets and debit orders, plus intelligent smart routing, network tokenization, automated reconciliation, cross-border settlement, and payment recovery through retries and mandates. Precium exposes a public API and a mandates API (per its status dashboard) and integrates via server-to-server, redirect, and orchestrator paths with webhook status updates, though it does not publish a public API reference or OpenAPI. Backed by Partech, QED Investors, and Speedinvest.

providers.name: Dave
providers.description: Dave is a U.S. consumer financial-technology company (Nasdaq: DAVE), founded in 2016 and headquartered in Los Angeles, that operates a mobile banking app serving roughly 14 million members. Its products include ExtraCash short-term cash advances of up to $500 (underwritten with its CashAI cash-flow model rather than credit scores), an FDIC-insured Dave Checking account with early direct deposit and Round-Up savings, and a Goals savings account. Banking services are provided through partner banks such as Coastal Community Bank. Dave is a consumer app and does not publish a first-party public developer API, SDKs, or a developer portal: there is no developer.dave.com / docs.dave.com, and api.dave.com is the app's private, undocumented mobile backend. Programmatic access to Dave-held consumer data is aggregator-mediated — Dave both consumes Plaid (to let members link external accounts) and is reachable as a supported institution through open-finance aggregators. This profile captures its public identity, aggregator-only open-finance posture, commercial link surface, and domain-security posture.

providers.name: Harness Wealth
providers.description: Harness — the company that launched as Harness Wealth, and today a wholly owned business of Multiplier, Inc. — is a New York City firm that runs an advisory platform for tax and wealth practices. It operates three connected surfaces: a marketplace that matches individuals with complex financial situations (equity compensation, liquidity events, business owners, real estate, high net worth) to vetted tax advisors; a client portal and workflow platform that tax firms run their engagements, documents, questionnaires and e-file on; and Harness Wealth Advisers, LLC, an SEC-registered investment adviser that recommends third-party advisers. Harness publishes no public developer program — there is no developer portal, API reference, OpenAPI/GraphQL/AsyncAPI specification, SDK, CLI or webhook documentation on any Harness host, and the product is delivered entirely as an end-user web application at app.harness.co.

providers.name: InvestaX
providers.description: InvestaX is a Singapore-based, MAS-licensed tokenization platform for real-world assets (RWAs), operated by IC SG Pte. Ltd. under a Capital Markets Services license (CMS100635) and a Recognised Market Operator license from the Monetary Authority of Singapore. The platform provides end-to-end infrastructure for the issuance, distribution, secondary trading, and custody of security tokens and tokenized securities, plus a Tokenization SaaS product for institutional issuers and RWA investment products such as tokenized money market funds and private credit. It supports multiple blockchain protocols including Ethereum, Polygon, BASE, Algorand, Tezos, and Hedera. Backed by 500 Global.

providers.name: TIFIN
providers.description: TIFIN is a Boulder, Colorado based fintech company founded in 2018 by Dr. Vinay Nair that builds AI-driven wealth technology for financial advisors, RIAs, broker-dealers, asset managers and insurance firms. Its platforms span TIFIN.AI (an agentic operating system consolidating the group's AI businesses for wealth and asset management workflows), TIFIN Wealth (investment proposal, risk-capacity and client-personalization tooling that integrates with Fidelity, BNY Pershing, Black Diamond, Salesforce, Wealthbox, Redtail, Orion and iRebal), TIFIN AMP/AG for asset-manager distribution intelligence, TIFIN Give for charitable giving accounts, TIFIN @Work for workplace financial wellness, and Magnifi, an AI investing assistant. TIFIN incubated 55ip (sold to J.P. Morgan) and Paralel, and announced a joint venture, TIFIN.AI, with J.P. Morgan Asset Management. The company states its AI capabilities are available as APIs that plug into existing wealthtech stacks, but publishes no public developer portal, API reference, or machine-readable contract; access is gated behind a "Get access" request form.

providers.name: Vested
providers.description: Vested Finance is an investment platform that enables Indian residents to build globally diversified portfolios by investing in US markets. It provides access to 10,000+ US stocks and 2,000+ ETFs, professionally managed portfolios (Vests), global mutual funds spanning 50+ countries, and private-market opportunities, alongside INR-to-USD remittance handling and US tax-reporting tools for Indian investors. Vested also operates a login-gated Partner API developer portal at developer.vestedfinance.com that exposes its brokerage and investing capabilities to partners. The company was originally surfaced as a portfolio company of Techstars and is profiled in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: APAC Financial Services
providers.description: APAC Financial Services (Apacfin) is a Mumbai-based, Reserve Bank of India registered Non-Banking Financial Company (NBFC) that provides customized MSME business loans to underbanked and underserved micro, small, and medium enterprises across India. APAC offers tech-enabled, largely paperless digital onboarding, quick disbursal with minimal documentation, and a mobile app (APACM) for loan tracking, EMI payments, and service requests. The lender reports roughly Rs 2,479 Crore of assets under management across 226 branches in six states, serving more than 52,000 customers, and carries an ICRA A (Stable) credit rating. APAC is a portfolio company of Norwest Venture Partners. No public developer API, OpenAPI specification, or developer portal is published; customer and partner interaction is via the mobile app and hosted customer/complaint portals.

providers.name: Corgi
providers.description: Corgi is an AI-native, full-stack business insurance platform for startups, offering modular coverage (Commercial General Liability, Directors & Officers, Tech Errors & Omissions, Cyber, EPLI, and fiduciary) quoted in minutes. Founded in 2024 and based in San Francisco, Corgi is a licensed insurance carrier rather than a broker, underwriting and issuing policies directly with pricing tailored to a startup's stage (pre-seed, Series A, growth). Backed by Kindred Ventures and TCV, the company was reported as an AI insurance unicorn in 2026. This API Evangelist profile was seeded from Kindred Ventures' portfolio; Corgi does not currently publish a public API or developer portal.

providers.name: HiJoJo Partners
providers.description: HiJoJo Partners Inc. (HiJoJo Partners株式会社) is a Tokyo-based independent asset management and fintech group, established in November 2017 and registered with the Director of the Kanto Local Finance Bureau (No. 3065) for Type II Financial Instruments Business, Investment Management Business, and Investment Advisory and Agency Business. The firm forms, sells and manages funds that give Japanese institutional and individual investors access to late-stage private and pre-IPO companies, and works to develop Japan's secondary market for unlisted shares. It operates three lines: HiJoJo Prime (in-person advisory for investors with 100M JPY or more in investable assets), HiJoJo.com (an online fund platform for individual investors with 30M JPY or more), and HiJoJo Private Market Solution for institutional investors and startups. HiJoJo joined the Nasdaq Private Market investor consortium in 2024 to expand secondary-market access in Japan. Its investor-facing platform is delivered as an authenticated member web application; the company publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK or machine-readable specification of any kind.

providers.name: LeaseLock
providers.description: LeaseLock is an insurtech platform for rental housing that replaces the traditional cash security deposit with lease insurance. Its Zero Deposit program embeds coverage into the lease through a signed addendum, removing thousands of dollars of move-in cost for residents while protecting owners and operators against unpaid rent and damage. LeaseLock Shield applies AI to ledger data, market trends and lease profiles to underwrite risk, and LeaseLock Central gives property teams a portal for claims, support tickets and training. Founded in 2016 and headquartered in Dallas, Texas, the company says it integrates with all major property management systems, but publishes no public developer API, developer portal, API reference or client SDKs — integration is arranged as a managed engagement. Its public engineering output is two open-source PostgreSQL extensions, pgasync and pgflow.

providers.name: Octane Lending
providers.description: Octane (Octane Lending, Inc.) is a New York City fintech founded in 2014 that makes powersports, outdoor power equipment and recreational-vehicle financing as simple as paying cash. It runs an end-to-end digital lending platform — instant soft-pull prequalification for consumers, real-time credit decisioning and eContracting through its in-house lender Roadrunner Financial, Inc., and loan servicing — connecting more than 4,000 dealer partners and 30-plus OEMs with prime through non-prime buyers. Its Dealer Portal 2.0 and dealer-management-system integrations (AppOne, Ekho and similar DMS platforms) submit credit applications and return decisions over a partner API whose credentials are coordinated privately by Octane account managers; Octane publishes no public developer portal, API documentation or machine-readable specification.

providers.name: Renew Financial
providers.description: Renew Financial (Renew Financial Group LLC) is a specialty consumer finance company founded in 2008 and headquartered in Oakland, California that pioneered and administers Property Assessed Clean Energy (PACE) financing for residential energy efficiency, renewable energy, water efficiency and resiliency home improvements. It administers the CaliforniaFIRST program in California and RenewPACE in Florida, funding solar, HVAC, roofing, windows, landscaping, hurricane and seismic projects through a voluntary property tax assessment repaid over terms up to 30 years. The company is licensed by the California Department of Financial Protection and Innovation as a PACE Program Administrator (#60DBO-90653) and carries NMLS ID 1788120. Renew Financial runs a contractor technology platform and an online homeowner application, but publishes no public developer program, API documentation, SDK or machine-readable API contract.

providers.name: Geocomply
providers.description: GeoComply is a geolocation compliance, digital identity, and fraud-prevention company that provides the location-verification and anti-fraud intelligence layer behind many of the world's most regulated digital platforms. Its product suite spans GeoComply Core (location-based fraud detection and geolocation compliance), IDComply (KYC and AML identity verification), GeoGuard (VPN and proxy/spoofing detection), PinPoint (on-property geofencing), the Chargeback Integrator (GCI), and the OneComply licensing-management platform, serving the iGaming, financial services, media/entertainment, and cryptocurrency industries. GeoComply's integrations are enterprise, sales-led engagements rather than a public self-serve developer portal; this profile was surfaced as a Norwest Venture Partners portfolio company and has been enriched from GeoComply's public security, trust, and discovery surface.

providers.name: nsKnox
providers.description: nsKnox is an Israeli fintech-security company that protects business-to-business payments against fraud and misdirection for corporations and banks. Founded and led by Alon Cohen, the founder and former CEO of CyberArk, nsKnox built its platform on a patented Cooperative Cyber Security (CCS) architecture in which payment and bank-account data is shredded and distributed across multiple independent "Knoxer" systems so that no single breach reveals anything. Its PaymentKnox product line covers outgoing payments (accounts payable), incoming payments (accounts receivable), Bank Account Certificates, Master Data Guard, Payment Check, and an Adaptive Payment Security service that validates payee bank accounts worldwide using Quick Check in-network lookups and Knox Verify out-of-network mini-transactions against the banking system. Customers connect through a hosted portal, scheduled file transfer, or a direct ERP API integration with systems such as SAP and Oracle. nsKnox publishes no public developer portal, API reference, or machine-readable specification; the API surface is documented to onboarded customers only.

providers.name: Salient
providers.description: Salient (Skwid Inc.) is an AI-native loan servicing and collections platform for consumer lenders — banks, credit unions, captive lenders, and specialty finance companies. It builds compliance-first AI voice and chat agents that automate servicing, collections, audit, insurance claims, chargebacks, and chargeoff workflows with native FDCPA, TCPA, and CFPB compliance. Its named agent products include Taylor (omnichannel servicing and collections), Marshall (automated audit), Flyn (total-loss insurance claims), Alex (chargebacks and disputes), and Melanie (chargeoffs). Founded in 2023 and backed by Andreessen Horowitz, Matrix Partners, and Y Combinator, Salient exposes a partner integration and onboarding API behind an authenticated developer portal. This profile was enriched from public web surfaces; the API reference is gated behind login so no public machine-readable specification was harvested.

providers.name: SRS Acquiom
providers.description: SRS Acquiom provides deal management solutions for mergers & acquisitions and loan agency transactions, operating across the entire deal lifecycle. Its services span pre-closing tax and accounting advisory, closing-phase escrow, payment disbursement and shareholder solicitation, and post-closing shareholder representation, alongside loan agency roles (administrative, collateral, and facility agent). SRS Acquiom delivers these through digital dashboards and platforms for deal transparency, backed by affiliate broker-dealer Acquiom Financial LLC (FINRA/SIPC). The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of Norwest Venture Partners. No public developer API, SDK, or developer portal is currently exposed.

providers.name: Trust & Will
providers.description: Trust & Will is a digital estate planning platform, headquartered in San Diego, California and founded in 2017, that lets individuals and families create legally valid, state-specific estate planning documents entirely online. Members build will-based or trust-based estate plans and related documents such as guardianship designations, powers of attorney, and advance healthcare directives, and the company also offers probate support and nationwide notarization. Trust & Will distributes through direct-to-consumer subscriptions as well as B2B partnerships with financial advisors, wealth managers, and employers offering it as a benefit. The platform is SOC 2 and HIPAA compliant. It was surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a Techstars portfolio company; this enrichment pass found no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal, but did confirm a live security program and trust posture.

providers.name: Arta
providers.description: Arta Finance (Arta Finance Wealth Management LLC) is a global digital wealth management platform that gives accredited investors and professionals from leading technology companies access to sophisticated investment strategies historically reserved for the ultra-wealthy and institutions. Its products include a High-Yield Cash Reserve (an automated U.S. Treasuries portfolio), curated private-market funds spanning private equity, private credit, real estate, venture capital and hedge funds, bespoke structured investments, private placement life insurance, and AI-assisted portfolio tools (AI for Wealth). Founded by former Google executives and backed by Ribbit Capital and other venture investors, Arta is an SEC-registered investment adviser (with a Singapore entity regulated by the Monetary Authority of Singapore), with clearing and custody provided by Pershing LLC. Arta operates as a consumer/member wealth application and does not publish a public developer API, SDKs, or MCP surface.

providers.name: Brightside
providers.description: Brightside (Brightside Benefit, Inc.) is an employer-sponsored financial care benefit that helps working families reduce everyday money stress. Delivered as an employee benefit through employers, Brightside pairs each employee with a human Financial Assistant and a mobile/web app offering emergency cash and loans, debt management and credit-score improvement, savings and early wage access, bill negotiation, crisis support (eviction, utilities, food), and guidance through major life events. The company is backed by a16z, Obvious Ventures, and Trinity Ventures. Brightside is a consumer-facing benefits platform and does not currently publish a public developer API or documentation.

providers.name: EverBank
providers.description: EverBank, N.A. is a Jacksonville, Florida based national bank (Member FDIC) focused on high-yield consumer deposits, business and treasury banking, and commercial lending, serving customers nationwide online plus a small network of financial centers in Florida, California and New York. The bank operated as TIAA Bank from 2017 until 2023, when it was acquired by an investor group and reverted to the EverBank brand as an independent institution. Like most US banks, EverBank publishes NO first-party public developer API or developer portal; there is no documented open-banking, FDX, or CFPB Section 1033 data-access API exposed directly. Consumer-permissioned account data is reached only through third-party aggregators (e.g. Plaid, MX, Finicity), which is the honest, non-fabricated posture recorded here.

providers.name: Julaya
providers.description: Julaya is a West African B2B fintech, founded in 2018 and headquartered in Abidjan, Cote d'Ivoire, that digitizes corporate financial operations across the UEMOA zone (Cote d'Ivoire, Senegal, Benin and Togo). Its pro account lets businesses send mobile money and bank transfers, collect cash and mobile-money deposits, pay suppliers and run payroll, and receive UEMOA-wide transfers via a Julaya IBAN, with multi-company sub-wallets, approval and signature workflows, real-time transaction tracking and accounting exports. Julaya is licensed as a payment establishment in Cote d'Ivoire and connects businesses to mobile-money rails including Orange Money, Wave, MTN MoMo, Moov and Wizall. A partner integration API (api.julaya.co) exposes disbursement and collection programmatically for enterprise customers.

providers.name: Lendorse
providers.description: Lendorse GmbH is a Berlin-based education-finance company that funds international master's students studying in Europe through Income Share Agreements (ISAs) instead of traditional credit-scored loans. Students receive between EUR 3,000 and EUR 20,000 toward tuition, visa deposits, relocation and living costs, then repay a fixed 6-12% share of gross monthly income for 12 to 60 months once they earn above a EUR 2,500 monthly salary floor, with total repayment capped at 2.3x the funded amount. No collateral, co-signer, parental guarantor or credit check is required, which opens funding to students from developing and emerging markets who are normally excluded. Lendorse also provides mentorship, CV review, mock interviews and industry introductions. It covers universities in Austria, Belgium, France, Germany, Italy, Spain, Sweden and Switzerland, went through the Techstars and ABN AMRO Future of Finance Accelerator, and raised EUR 1.75M co-led by LUMO Labs and Soulmates Ventures. Lendorse publishes no public API, SDKs or developer portal as of July 2026; this profile is a company record rather than an API profile.

providers.name: Pintarnya
providers.description: Pintarnya is an Indonesian technology startup, launched in May 2022, that operates an employment and financial-services super-app for the country's blue-collar and entry-level workforce (education levels from elementary school through bachelor's degree, "SD-S1"). The platform aggregates tens of thousands of daily-updated job listings across 300+ Indonesian cities and pairs job search with Cari Cuan side-income tasks, Siap Kerja skill-building video courses, a CV builder, and an employer/recruiter posting product used by tens of thousands of companies. Pintarnya reports more than 10 million registered job seekers and is registered with Indonesia's Ministry of Labor (KEMNAKER). It is a consumer web and mobile product; no public developer API, OpenAPI description, or developer portal is published as of this profile.

providers.name: Sellersfi
providers.description: SellersFi is a financial technology company providing working capital and inventory financing to e-commerce merchants, including sellers on Amazon and direct-to-consumer channels. It offers flexible funding lines with approvals in as fast as 48 hours, helping online businesses manage cash flow, purchase inventory, and scale operations. Backed by Northzone, SellersFi operates a lending platform and applicant portal rather than a public developer API; this profile captures its identity and domain-security posture for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Siepe
providers.description: Siepe is a Dallas, Texas fintech providing cloud-based software and technology-enabled services for private credit, CLO and alternative investment managers. Its front-to-back platform spans portfolio management, operations and accounting, collateral administration, compliance and legal, middle-office services, data extraction and a centralized data-management warehouse that normalizes borrower, lender, agent-bank and investor feeds into one real-time view. Siepe also operates managed technology and public-cloud services for asset managers. The company raised a $30M Series B led by WestCap in 2024 and holds SOC 2 Type II certification. Siepe publishes no public developer program: connectivity is delivered as bilateral, managed integrations (for example its 2026 Order Management System integration with Octaura for syndicated loan and CLO trading) rather than as a self-serve, documented public API.

providers.name: Titan
providers.description: Titan (Titan Global Capital Management USA LLC) is a New York City wealth-management firm founded in 2017 that offers app-based investing and advisory services to high-performing professionals and emerging high-net-worth individuals. Its product suite spans actively managed Flagship, Smart Treasury and Opportunities funds, direct indexing, automated stocks and bonds, venture-fund access, credit and real-estate strategies, crypto, and dedicated CFP-led wealth advisory, managing over $1.2 billion for 10,000+ clients. Titan is a consumer fintech application delivered via web and mobile apps; it does not publish a public developer API, developer portal, or API documentation. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of a16z, accel, and general-catalyst.

providers.name: City National Bank
providers.description: City National Bank is a national bank chartered in the United States and a wholly owned subsidiary of Royal Bank of Canada (RBC) since 2015, headquartered in Los Angeles, California and known historically as "the bank to the stars" for its deep roots in the entertainment industry. With roughly $98 billion in assets, it is an FDIC-insured, super-regional institution offering personal, business, and private banking, wealth management, treasury management, and capital markets services, with industry expertise across entertainment, healthcare, real estate, technology, and law. City National operates as CN Bank in Florida. It runs NO first-party public developer portal or documented public API: developer.cnb.com and developers.cnb.com do not resolve and api.cnb.com returns 404. Consistent with the voluntary, fragmented US open-finance model, consumer-permissioned account data is reached through third-party aggregators (Plaid, MX, Finicity, Akoya) rather than a direct City National API. As a covered depository institution it falls under the emerging CFPB Section 1033 Personal Financial Data Rights rule, but no City-National-specific 1033 or FDX participation posture is publicly documented. Its Canadian parent RBC runs a separate developer portal (developer.rbc.com) under a different charter that does not expose City National Bank APIs.

providers.name: Lendable
providers.description: Lendable Ltd is a UK consumer lending fintech founded in 2014 and headquartered in London, offering unsecured personal loans directly to borrowers through a fully digital application. The company underwrites with technology and data analytics rather than relying on a credit score alone, describing its approach as looking at all of an applicant's data together to produce a personalised quote in minutes without paper forms or branch visits. Lendable distributes through the major UK price-comparison platforms including ClearScore, Compare the Market, MoneySuperMarket, Experian, TotallyMoney, TransUnion and Go.Compare. It is authorised and regulated by the Financial Conduct Authority (FCA reference 720261, company number 08828186) and is a CIFAS member. Lendable publishes no public developer API or developer portal — its public technical surface is an RFC 9116 security.txt, an llms.txt, and a set of first-party open source PHP/Symfony engineering libraries on Packagist and GitHub.

providers.name: Solar Mosaic
providers.description: Solar Mosaic, Inc. (trading as Mosaic) was a residential clean-energy lender founded in Oakland, California in 2010, originally as a solar crowdfunding platform and from 2014 as a point-of-sale financing platform for residential solar, battery storage and other sustainable home improvements funded through third-party capital partners. Mosaic originated loans through a dealer/installer channel and backed more than $15 billion in home energy loans across roughly 360,000 households. Its integration surface for installer and capital partners was the Mosaic Financing API, documented on a password-protected ReadMe developer portal at developer.joinmosaic.com. Solar Mosaic filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in the Southern District of Texas on 2025-06-09 and its loan portfolio was acquired in September 2025 by Solar Servicing LLC, which stated it would not originate new solar loans. As of this profile the joinmosaic.com website 301-redirects to solarservicingllc.com, the api.joinmosaic.com host returns HTTP 503, and the Mosaic status page reports "Page Inactive".

providers.name: Kafene
providers.description: Kafene is a New York-based point-of-sale financing platform that lets retailers offer transparent lease-to-own (LTO) purchase options to prime and non-prime consumers. Founded in 2019 by Neal Desai and James Schuler, the company underwrites shoppers with an AI-driven risk model that pulls 20,000+ data points to return an approval — up to $5,000 — in seconds, then pays the merchant directly on delivery confirmation while the customer pays weekly or biweekly until ownership. Merchants originate applications from their in-store POS or by sending a text-to-apply link; consumers manage leases and payments in a self-service dashboard. Kafene raised a ~$31M Series B and reaches merchants through financing-waterfall networks such as Versatile Credit and LendPro. As of the 2026-08-01 enrichment probe Kafene publishes no public developer program, no OpenAPI/GraphQL/MCP contract, no SDKs, and no /.well-known discovery surface; its merchant and consumer surfaces are authenticated single-page web applications and integration is arranged through Kafene's partner team, not self-serve documentation.

providers.name: Lentra
providers.description: Lentra is a Pune, India based cloud-native digital lending platform for banks and non-banking financial companies. Built on a microservices architecture with customisable customer journeys, the platform spans loan origination (GoNoGo), loan management (1LMS), data and machine learning operations (Lentra MLOps), and data transfer (TransferX), alongside standalone modules for MultiBureau credit bureau access, identity and video KYC verification, collateral management, document management, co-lending and bank reconciliation. Lentra packages these into pre-built retail, business and agriculture lending journeys - home, personal, education, vehicle, consumer durable and credit card loans, equipment finance, working capital, supply chain finance and agri/KCC lending - delivered SaaS on a per-user or per-transaction basis to institutions including HDFC Bank, State Bank of India, IDFC and TVS Credit. The company is an Open Credit Enablement Network (OCEN) participant and maintains a public trust center covering SOC 2 Type II, SOC 3, ISO 27001:2022, ISO 27017, ISO 27018, ISO 27701, ISO 22301:2019 and CSA STAR. Lentra sells to enterprises directly; it does not operate a public self-service developer portal or publish an open API reference.

providers.name: Perfios
providers.description: Perfios is a Bangalore, India-headquartered financial technology (SaaS) company providing an AI-driven operating system for banks, NBFCs, fintechs, and insurers, serving over 1,000 financial institutions globally. Its platform spans four product families: Perfios Analyse (bank statement, ITR, GST, payslip, credit-card and financial-statement analysers), Perfios Verify (KYC/KYB, video KYC, liveness detection, OCR, digital signature and onboarding via OneSDK), Perfios Lens (portfolio monitoring, PFM, credit assessment memos, due diligence), and Perfios Protect (document tamper detection, deepfake detection, and insurance fraud detection). Perfios also runs a digital public infrastructure (DPI) stack for Account Aggregator FIU/FIP roles. Its data-aggregation, decisioning, and verification capabilities are delivered to partners programmatically; public developer documentation is gated behind partner access. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Bessemer Venture Partners.

providers.name: Rain Financial
providers.description: Rain is a Middle East and North Africa (MENA) cryptocurrency exchange and digital-asset platform, operated through Rain Financial Inc. and its Bahrain entity Rain Management W.L.L. Founded in 2017 by Abdullah Almoaiqel, AJ Nelson, Joseph Dallago, and Yehia Badawy, Rain became the first crypto-asset company accepted into the Central Bank of Bahrain (CBB) regulatory sandbox and, in 2019, the first CBB-licensed crypto-asset service provider in the region. Rain Trading Limited later received approval from Abu Dhabi Global Market's Financial Services Regulatory Authority (FSRA) to expand across the UAE. Rain lets retail and institutional customers buy, sell, store, and manage Bitcoin, Ethereum, and other cryptocurrencies against multiple fiat currencies, with a Rain Pro offering for advanced traders and the majority of customer assets held in multi-signature cold storage. The company raised seed, Series A, and a $110M Series B (Paradigm, Kleiner Perkins), and is a portfolio company of 500 Global.

providers.name: Savvy
providers.description: Savvy (Savvy Advisors, Inc.) is a technology-driven, SEC-registered investment advisory firm founded in 2021 and headquartered in New York, NY. It combines licensed fiduciary financial advisors with proprietary technology — including Savvy Intelligence, an AI workspace for advisors — to deliver personalized wealth management for high-net-worth individuals and independent financial advisors. Savvy manages $5B+ in assets across 100+ advisors in 30+ U.S. locations, custodying at Fidelity and Charles Schwab. The firm serves two audiences: clients seeking wealth management (financial planning, investment management, direct indexing, tax optimization, retirement, trust and estate planning) and advisors looking to join or build a practice on its platform. Savvy publishes no public developer API; this profile captures its identity, domain security posture, and the verbatim /llms.txt it exposes for agents.

providers.name: ChangEd
providers.description: ChangEd (Changed) is a consumer financial-technology company whose mobile app helps people pay off debt faster by automatically rounding up everyday purchases to the nearest dollar and directing those micro-savings toward student loans, credit cards, mortgages, personal loans, and auto loans. Founded by brothers Dan Stelmach and Nick Sky, the app launched in 2017, appeared on Shark Tank and took investment from Mark Cuban, and is a Techstars portfolio company. It links to a user's bank account, tracks spending, automates extra debt payments, supports savings goals, and visualizes payoff progress for a $4/month subscription, with banking services provided by nbkc bank (Member FDIC). ChangEd is a consumer mobile product and does not publish a public API, developer portal, or SDK; this profile is maintained as a company record in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Cicada
providers.description: Cicada Securities, LLC is a financial technology company revolutionizing the bond markets in Emerging Markets. It operates an Alternative Trading System (ATS) focused on local-currency-denominated government bonds in Mexico (M Bonos, UDI Bonos, and Cetes), enhancing liquidity and facilitating all-to-all access in an anonymous trading environment through central limit orderbook and request-for-quote protocols. Cicada Securities, LLC is an SEC-registered broker-dealer and FINRA member, and Cicada SEF, LLC is an applicant for swap execution facility registration with the CFTC. The company offers a trading platform, live pricing data, and a programmatic API for direct access to LatAm local-currency rates market liquidity, backed by 500 Global.

providers.name: Clerkie
providers.description: Clerkie, operated by Henry Labs Inc. and founded in San Francisco in 2016, is an AI-powered debt management and loan-recovery platform serving both consumers and institutional lenders. The consumer side offers a conversational financial assistant for budgeting, debt negotiation, and personalized repayment planning, while the B2B side — marketed as Fiber, launched in 2021 and now sold on its own domain getfiber.ai — gives lenders, banks, credit unions, and collection agencies an AI-driven recovery suite spanning CRM, an inventory management system (IMS), an AI agent, omnichannel communications, borrower scoring, a self-service payment portal, and workflow automation. Clerkie markets a RESTful API and multi-currency payment processing for lenders to integrate loan portfolios, real-time reporting, and automated repayment arrangements, but publishes no public developer documentation, machine-readable API contract, or self-serve developer portal — integration is arranged through a sales conversation. The company has raised over $41M from Left Lane Capital, Flourish Ventures, Vestigo Ventures, and Citibank.

providers.name: F.N.B. Corporation
providers.description: F.N.B. Corporation (NYSE: FNB) is a diversified financial services holding company headquartered in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, and the parent of First National Bank of Pennsylvania, an FDIC-insured, state-chartered commercial bank. With roughly $50 billion in total assets at year-end 2025, FNB is a regional super-community bank operating around 350 branches across seven states and Washington, D.C. (Pennsylvania, Ohio, Maryland, West Virginia, North Carolina, South Carolina and Virginia), offering commercial banking, consumer banking and wealth management through its eStore digital platform. On open finance, FNB exposes NO first-party public developer portal or documented API: the developer/api subdomains of fnb-online.com redirect to the marketing homepage and no developer documentation is published. Consumer-permissioned account and transaction data is reachable only through third-party aggregators (notably Plaid), not a first-party FNB API. No direct Financial Data Exchange (FDX) membership or public CFPB Section 1033 posture is documented by the institution as of this profile.

providers.name: iTrustCapital
providers.description: iTrustCapital (legal entity ITC2.0, Inc.) is a US fintech software platform for alternative assets, offering 24/7 self-directed access to dozens of cryptocurrencies and physical precious metals through three account types: tax-advantaged self-directed Crypto IRAs for retirement savings, Premium Custody Accounts (PCA) for everyday non-retirement investing, and Treasury Accounts for businesses, trusts, non-profits and other entities. The platform charges a 1% cryptocurrency transaction fee with no monthly, annual, startup, exit, storage or transfer fees, and runs a closed-loop system backed by third-party US banks, custodians (iTrust Custodial Services, Fortis Bank) and institutional storage providers. iTrustCapital is not an exchange, custodian, trust company, broker-dealer or investment adviser; all transactions on the platform are self-directed. As of this profiling pass the company publishes NO public developer API — its own help center states that it "does not offer any API integration to any third-party applications, including self-trading bots and coin trackers." Access is via the web app and the iOS/Android mobile apps only.

providers.name: LIQUiDITY Group
providers.description: LIQUiDITY Group (branded simply "Liquidity") is an AI-native private credit lender and alternative asset manager founded in 2018, headquartered in New York with offices in Tel Aviv, London, Singapore, Tokyo and Abu Dhabi. It underwrites and deploys non-dilutive debt and growth capital — typically $10M to $200M — to late-stage technology and mid-market companies across 35+ countries, using its proprietary DYNAMiCs decision-science platform to compress due diligence from months to days. The firm manages several billion dollars across multiple debt and equity funds, including Mars Growth Capital, a joint venture with MUFG Bank, and is backed by MUFG, Apollo Asset Management, Spark Capital and Meitav Dash. Liquidity is a lender that runs on software rather than a software vendor: its DYNAMiCs platform is operated for its own analysts, borrowers and fund investors at app.liquiditygroup.com and is not offered as a public developer product. No public developer portal, API reference, OpenAPI/GraphQL schema, SDK or machine-readable contract is published on any host the company controls.

providers.name: Vastu Housing Finance Corporation
providers.description: Vastu Housing Finance Corporation Limited (Vastu HFC) is an Indian, technology-enabled affordable housing finance company backed by Norwest Venture Partners. It provides home purchase, construction, extension, and improvement loans, plot-plus-construction loans, commercial property loans, and loans against property through 200+ branches across 17 states, serving 1.6+ million customers, and participates in government subsidy schemes such as Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana Urban 2.0. Vehicle, business, and construction-equipment lending is offered through its subsidiary Vastu Finserve. The company operates as a digital-first lender with a customer mobile app, but publishes no public developer portal or API surface.

providers.name: Long-Term Stock Exchange
providers.description: The Long-Term Stock Exchange (LTSE) is a U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission-registered national securities exchange headquartered in New York, built to support companies and investors committed to long-term value creation. LTSE operates a principles-based equities trading platform that accepts order entry over the MEMO FIX and MEMO SBE (Simple Binary Encoding) protocols and distributes real-time market data - depth of book, top of book, and last sale - via the MEMOIR multicast feed. Beyond the exchange it offers private-markets and cap-table software plus long-term listing standards. LTSE does not publish a public REST/OpenAPI developer API; participant connectivity (Direct, Extranet, Telco via NY4) and technical specifications are provided through its Market Operations team.

providers.name: Mutual of Omaha
providers.description: Mutual of Omaha is a Fortune 500 mutual insurance and financial services company headquartered in Omaha, Nebraska, providing life, disability, dental, vision, critical illness, accident and long-term care insurance, Medicare supplement and Medicare Advantage plans, annuities, retirement services, mortgage lending and investment products to individuals, employers and groups across the United States. Its Workplace Solutions unit runs an API integration program for group and voluntary benefits — Plan Setup, Evidence of Insurability and Enrollment — but those APIs are delivered through benefits administration platform partners such as ADP Workforce Now, bswift, Employee Navigator and PlanSource rather than through a public developer portal, and no machine-readable contract is published.

providers.name: Taptap Send
providers.description: Taptap Send is a mobile money-transfer (remittance) application that lets people send money from Europe, the UK, the US, and Canada to family and businesses across Africa, Asia, and Latin America. The service supports bank deposits, mobile-money wallets, and cash pickups in 100+ receiving countries with competitive exchange rates and low fees, and operates as a licensed and regulated money transmitter (FCA regulated, SOC 2 and PCI DSS attested) with bank-level encryption. Taptap Send is a consumer-facing app and does not currently publish a public developer API, developer portal, or API documentation; this profile captures its company identity, security posture, and compliance program.

providers.name: Farther
providers.description: Farther is a technology-driven wealth management and registered investment advisory (RIA) firm that pairs human financial advisors with a proprietary "Intelligent Wealth Platform." The firm has recruited more than $23 billion in client assets and positions itself among the fastest-growing US financial services firms (Inc. Magazine, Deloitte Technology Fast 500). Services span financial and retirement planning, investment and portfolio management, tax-intelligent optimization, trust and estate planning, generational wealth, small-business services, Farther Asset Management, and institutional offerings. The client experience runs through a single-page web/mobile application at app.farther.com and integrates account aggregation via Plaid. Farther does not publish a public developer API, OpenAPI/AsyncAPI specification, SDKs, or a developer portal; this profile captures the firm's public web, security, and identity surface. Backed by Bessemer Venture Partners and Lightspeed Venture Partners.

providers.name: Raymond James Bank
providers.description: Raymond James Bank is a Florida-chartered state member bank headquartered in St. Petersburg, Florida, and a wholly owned subsidiary of Raymond James Financial, Inc. (NYSE: RJF), a diversified financial services holding company founded in 1962. Supervised by the Federal Reserve and the Florida Office of Financial Regulation, the bank provides securities-based lending, residential mortgages, commercial and industrial and commercial real estate loans, tax-exempt loans, and deposit products (including its Enhanced Savings Program) primarily to Raymond James wealth-management and institutional clients. On open finance, the bank runs no first-party public developer portal and publishes no downloadable API specifications; consumer-permissioned account data is reachable only indirectly through third-party aggregators such as Plaid. No FDX participation or CFPB Section 1033 data-access posture is publicly documented for this institution as of this record.

providers.name: Swypex
providers.description: Swypex is an Egyptian fintech, founded in 2022 and headquartered at Smart Village in Cairo, that provides an all-in-one financial management platform for businesses. The platform bundles corporate cards, payments, invoice management, and working capital financing into one system, giving finance teams real-time visibility and control over company spend. Swypex launched Egypt's first approval-based corporate card, where each transaction's limit unlocks only after real-time review and approval by the company's finance team, and offers e-invoicing (with an Odoo integration) and Swypextend working-capital financing. Swypex is licensed by the Central Bank of Egypt and operates its card program in partnership with Visa and Mashreq Bank. It raised a $4M seed round led by Accel (Accel's first fintech investment in MENA), with Foundation Ventures and Raba Partnership. Swypex does not publish a public developer API; its products are delivered through web and mobile apps plus a small set of native integrations (Odoo, e-invoicing, Just2Pay).

providers.name: Vancity Community Investment Bank
providers.description: Vancity Community Investment Bank (VCIB) is a federally regulated Schedule I chartered bank headquartered in Toronto, Ontario, and a wholly owned subsidiary of Vancouver City Savings Credit Union (Vancity), Canada's largest community credit union. Established to carry the cooperative "community-first" finance model into the national banking system, VCIB is a values-driven, Certified B Corporation and CDIC member that provides impact-focused commercial banking - commercial real estate and affordable-housing lending, clean-energy and green-building finance, social-enterprise banking, Impact GICs, high-interest savings, and business Visa products - to organizations driving social, economic, and environmental change. As a small impact/commercial bank rather than one of the Big Six, VCIB operates no public developer portal, exposes no first-party developer API, and publishes no downloadable API specifications. Canada's Consumer-Driven Banking (open banking) framework, legislated in Budget 2024 and the 2024 Fall Economic Statement under the Financial Consumer Agency of Canada, is not yet operational, so any third-party access to VCIB customer data today would be voluntary and aggregator-mediated rather than via a documented open API.

providers.name: Bhub
providers.description: BHub (bhub.com) is a Brazilian accounting and financial back-office company serving small and medium-sized businesses across Brazil. It combines bookkeeping and tax accounting (contabilidade), financial business-process outsourcing (BPO financeiro) covering accounts payable/receivable and reconciliation, tax consulting (consultoria tributaria), and corporate/legal structuring (societario), delivered through its online client hub at app.bhub.ai. Specialized divisions Agrocontar (agribusiness) and Quality Associados (nonprofit/third sector) extend its sector coverage. Backed by QED Investors, BHub reports processing tens of millions of invoices and reconciling billions of reais annually. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a fintech portfolio lead; BHub currently exposes an internal application backend (api.bhub.com) but publishes no public developer API, SDKs, or API documentation.

providers.name: Blend Financial
providers.description: Blend Financial Inc., doing business as Origin Financial (useorigin.com), is a consumer wealth management and personal finance platform that unifies income, net worth, spending, investments, assets, and liabilities into a single application. Origin pairs AI-powered budgeting and spend tracking with investment tools, estate and tax planning, and access to CFP professional advice; investment advisory services are provided through Origin Investment Advisory LLC, a subsidiary of Blend Financial Inc. The company is a consumer (B2C) product backed by 500 Global, Felicis Ventures, Founders Fund, and other investors, and also offers employer-sponsored financial wellness. As surfaced in the API Evangelist network it is a company profile; Origin publishes no public developer API, developer portal, or API documentation at this time.

providers.name: Brightmoney
providers.description: Bright Money (Bright) is a San Francisco-based financial technology company that describes itself as the world's first AI Loan Assistant. Its consumer mobile app helps people pay off credit-card debt faster, build credit history, and access affordable credit through products including Bright Builder (a secured 0% APR credit line reported to the major bureaus), Bright Plan debt-payoff and budgeting, Smart Round-Ups automated savings, rent reporting, personal loans up to $10,000 through network partners, and cash advances up to $750 for all credit scores. Bright is a consumer-facing product and does not currently publish a public developer API or documentation.

providers.name: BrightPlan
providers.description: BrightPlan is a San Jose, California based financial wellness company that sells a Total Financial Wellness platform to enterprise HR and benefits teams, combining a self-service digital financial planning application, an AI-powered financial wellness coach, and access to human CFP fiduciary advisors. BrightPlan LLC is an SEC-registered investment adviser, and the product is delivered to employees as an employer-sponsored benefit rather than as a self-serve consumer subscription. The employee experience runs at my.brightplan.com and web.brightplan.com with iOS and Android apps; employer value is framed around benefits engagement, retention, and measurable financial wellbeing. BrightPlan markets HRIS and benefits-system integration to employers but publishes no public developer program, API reference, or machine-readable specification of any kind.

providers.name: Drip Capital
providers.description: Drip Capital is a digital trade finance and working capital company founded in 2016, headquartered in Palo Alto, California, with operations in Mumbai, India and Mexico City, Mexico. It provides collateral-free post-shipment finance to small and medium-sized exporters and importers through data-driven underwriting, offering invoice factoring, export finance, an importer credit program, supply chain and vendor financing, receivables financing, and revolving lines of credit. The company has financed over $9 billion in trade transactions for 11,000+ businesses worldwide. Drip Capital does not currently publish a public developer API; this profile captures its identity and public web properties. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Accel, Initialized Capital, Wing Venture Capital, and Y Combinator.

providers.name: Heard
providers.description: Heard (Heard Technologies, Inc.) is the financial management platform built specifically for therapists and wellness practitioners in private practice. Founded in 2019 and based in Seattle, Washington, Heard pairs easy-to-use software with a dedicated human team to handle bookkeeping, taxes, payroll, and business banking in a single subscription, so licensed mental health and allied health clinicians can focus on their clients. Heard serves solo and single-owner group practices across the United States, from newer sole proprietors to established S corporations, and connects with tools practices already use such as SimplePractice, TherapyNotes, Headway, Jane App, Stripe, and Square. Heard exposes no public developer API; this API Evangelist profile captures the company identity, its public web properties, and the published llms.txt.

providers.name: OnDeck Capital
providers.description: OnDeck Capital (ODK Capital, LLC) is one of the largest online small business lenders in the United States, providing term loans and business lines of credit to small and medium-sized businesses. Founded in 2007 and headquartered in New York, OnDeck uses data-driven underwriting and cash-flow analytics to deliver fast funding decisions, and has delivered more than $13 billion in financing to over 100,000 businesses across the U.S. OnDeck operates as a subsidiary of Enova International and also markets under the Headway Capital brand. It surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of IVP; OnDeck publishes a public marketing site and an llms.txt resource index but does not currently expose a public developer or partner API.

providers.name: Ummeed Housing Finance
providers.description: Ummeed Housing Finance Pvt. Ltd. is an Indian affordable-housing finance company registered with the National Housing Bank (NHB), providing home loans, loans against property, business loans, and MSME business loans to low- and middle-income households. Headquartered in Gurgaon, Haryana, it operates 130+ branches across 9 states and has served 45,000+ families. Backed by Norwest Venture Partners. Ummeed publishes no public developer portal or API surface; its digital channels are the customer website and a customer mobile app.

providers.name: Axial Networks
providers.description: Axial Networks operates Axial (axial.net), a private deal network for mergers, acquisitions and capital raising in the North American lower middle market. Founded in 2010 and based in New York, the platform connects business owners, M&A advisors, private equity buyers, strategic acquirers and lenders around live sell-side and buy-side transactions, and publishes a public member directory, the Middle Market Review editorial forum, industry deal-activity dashboards and business valuation calculators. The member product runs at network.axial.net and product help documentation at guide.axial.net. Axial publishes an llms.txt orientation file for language models and a public status page, but ships no public API, SDK, webhook surface or developer program — the platform is delivered as an authenticated end-user application only.

providers.name: Commerce Bank
providers.description: Commerce Bank is the principal banking subsidiary of Commerce Bancshares, Inc. (NASDAQ CBSH), a Missouri-based regional bank holding company with roughly $32 billion in assets and dual headquarters in Kansas City and St. Louis. Commerce Bank is a Missouri state-chartered bank and Federal Reserve member, founded in 1865, offering personal, business, commercial, and wealth-management services across the U.S. Midwest. Its API posture is corporate/embedded-banking oriented rather than a fully open public program: it runs a registration-gated external developer portal (developers.commercebank.com) and a CommercePayments developer platform, and delivers ERP-embedded banking via Commerce Connections Direct. Consumer-permissioned data sharing is largely intermediated through aggregators such as Plaid and platforms like Modern Treasury rather than a documented first-party, self-serve open-banking API. No public FDX or CFPB Section 1033 data-access posture is documented, and no downloadable OpenAPI/Swagger is publicly available.

providers.name: Plural Ai
providers.description: Plural is an AI platform built for private markets professionals across private debt, private equity, and banking. Its AI agents ingest and analyze complex financial documents and data-room sources (documents, SharePoint, data rooms) to generate auditable, fully-referenced outputs — deal screeners, investment committee (IC) memos, term-sheet drafts, portfolio reports, and compliance documentation. Plural emphasizes EU data residency, end-to-end encryption, ISO 27001-aligned controls, and GDPR/DORA readiness, with no training on customer data. The company is backed by Speedinvest, Creative Destruction Lab, AI SEED, Innovate UK, and the European Commission. As of this enrichment pass no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface is published; the product references MCP and agent integrations for private-markets workflows.

providers.name: UBS Bank USA
providers.description: UBS Bank USA (BUSA) is a Utah state-chartered industrial bank and FDIC-insured depository institution headquartered in Salt Lake City, Utah, established in 2003 and reporting roughly $122 billion in total assets. It is the primary US banking vehicle of UBS Wealth Management Americas, providing FDIC-insured deposit sweep programs, securities-based lending, mortgages, and credit cards almost exclusively to the high-net-worth and ultra-high-net-worth advisory clients of parent UBS Group AG. It is supervised by the FDIC, the Utah Department of Financial Institutions, and the CFPB. Unlike a fintech or a Banking-as-a-Service provider, UBS Bank USA exposes no first-party public developer API surface of its own; its services are delivered through UBS Financial Advisors rather than self-serve APIs. The only live UBS developer portal (developer.ubs.com) belongs to UBS Switzerland and serves Swiss and EU products (key4 mortgages, QR-bill, PSD2, TWINT, bLink, KeyPort/EBICS), not this US entity. US consumer-permissioned data access, where available, is mediated by third-party aggregators rather than a documented BUSA API.

providers.name: Umony
providers.description: Umony is a London-based communications compliance platform, founded in 2017 and backed by Seedcamp, that captures, records, and archives employee voice calls, SMS, WhatsApp, and Microsoft Teams conversations at the telecom-network level for banks and other regulated financial institutions. Its platform spans the Umony App (BYOD softphone), Umony Mobile (eSIM carrier-level capture), and Umony Archive with AI risk scoring, and the company holds BSI-certified ISO 27001:2022, ISO 42001:2023, and ISO 22301:2019 certifications. Umony publishes no public developer API surface today.

providers.name: America First Credit Union
providers.description: America First Credit Union is a federally chartered, NCUA-insured credit union headquartered in Riverdale, Utah, founded in 1939. With roughly $19 billion in assets, more than one million members, and about 124 branches across seven western states (Utah, Idaho, Oregon, New Mexico, Arizona, Nevada, and California), it is one of the largest credit unions in the United States. Like the vast majority of US credit unions, America First operates no public first-party developer portal and publishes no downloadable OpenAPI/Swagger specifications. It provides no self-serve, publicly documented API surface; consumer-permissioned account data access is handled through third-party data aggregators and its core banking provider rather than a direct first-party API. No public FDX participation or CFPB Section 1033 data-access posture is documented on its public website as of this bootstrap. This record is an honest identity profile with no fabricated API surface.

providers.name: Endowus
providers.description: Endowus is a Singapore- and Hong Kong-based digital wealth management platform founded in 2017 by Gregory Van and Samuel Rhee. It gives retail, accredited, and private-wealth clients access to low-fee institutional share-class funds, advised and self-directed portfolios, and private-market and alternatives strategies across Cash, CPF (Central Provident Fund), and SRS (Supplementary Retirement Scheme) accounts. Its conflict-free model rebates 100% of trailer fees and fund-manager commissions to clients. Endowus is licensed by the Monetary Authority of Singapore (CMS License 101051), serves 300,000+ clients, and manages over US$10 billion in assets. It was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-company lead; the company operates consumer apps but publishes no public developer API or documentation at this time.

providers.name: First American Financial
providers.description: First American Financial is a leading provider of title insurance, settlement services, and risk solutions for real estate transactions, as well as related products and services. First American operates a developer portal exposing APIs for office lookup, order management, document exchange, messaging, and webhook notifications.

providers.name: Nitra
providers.description: Nitra is an integrated financial and operational platform — an "operating system" — for independent medical practices, unifying business banking, spend management, payments, accounting, capital, and front-desk automation in one system. Its core products include the Nitra Card (a Visa business card with cashback and vendor pricing), NitraMart (a medical-supplies marketplace), BillPay payment processing, accounting integrations (QuickBooks, Nextech), Trina (an AI assistant for phone reception and invoice matching), and capital products such as lending, equipment financing, and insurance factoring. Nitra primarily serves eye care, aesthetics, dental specialty, and fertility practices as well as multi-site groups. The company is SOC 2 Type II certified and HIPAA-aware, holds funds at FDIC-insured banks, and is backed by a16z and Pantera Capital. Nitra publishes no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal as of this enrichment pass.

providers.name: GraniteShares
providers.description: GraniteShares is an independent exchange-traded fund (ETF) issuer that builds alternative, single-stock and thematic investment products for investors who want differentiated exposure. Its lineup spans 2x leveraged and inverse single-stock ETFs (such as NVDL for NVIDIA and TSLR for Tesla), YieldBOOST options-income ETFs, autocallable ETFs, physically-backed gold and broad commodity ETFs, and diversified income and equity strategies across U.S. and European markets. GraniteShares publishes no public developer or data API program; this API Evangelist profile catalogs the company's public web surface and the machine-readable discovery documents (OpenID Connect / OAuth 2.0 member authentication for its Umbraco-powered site) that were probed from its domain. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Bain Capital Ventures.

providers.name: Splitero
providers.description: Splitero is a San Diego, California fintech founded in 2021 by Michael Gifford and David Zvaifler that originates Home Equity Investments (HEIs) — a lump sum of cash, up to $500,000, paid to a homeowner today in exchange for a share of the home's future value, with no monthly payments, no income requirement, credit scores accepted from 500, and terms of up to 30 years. The company operates a consumer application and servicing portal at my.splitero.com, funds its originations through institutional capital commitments (including a $350M facility led by Blue Owl Capital), and has expanded into a licensed residential brokerage, Splitero Homes. Splitero is an end-user consumer finance product: it publishes no developer portal, no public API, no SDKs and no machine-readable contract of any kind.

providers.name: Stifel Financial
providers.description: Stifel Financial is a financial services holding company whose subsidiaries provide securities brokerage, investment banking, trading, investment advisory, and related financial services to individual investors, corporations, and government entities. Stifel bank accounts are accessible via open banking data aggregators including Plaid and Finicity (Mastercard) for third-party financial applications.

providers.name: MANTL
