providers.description: MANTL is an account and deposit origination software company for banks and credit unions. Its omnichannel platform lets financial institutions open consumer and business deposit and loan accounts across online and in-branch channels, integrating with existing core banking systems to modernize onboarding and accelerate deposit growth. More than 100 institutions raise over $1 billion in deposits monthly through the platform. MANTL was surfaced as a Techstars portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network. It publishes no public API or developer portal — this profile captures its public web, legal, support, and system-status surfaces.

providers.name: Selective Insurance Group
providers.description: Selective Insurance Group, Inc. (NASDAQ: SIGI) is a Branchville, New Jersey holding company whose insurance subsidiaries underwrite standard commercial lines, standard personal lines, and excess and surplus lines property and casualty insurance, plus flood insurance written through the National Flood Insurance Program's Write Your Own program. Coverage is distributed exclusively through independent insurance agents and brokers across the Eastern and Midwestern United States. Selective operates customer and agent self-service portals (MySelective, and the agent portal at customer1.selectiveinsurance.com) and supports policy, billing and claims download into agency management systems, but publishes no public developer program, API documentation, or machine-readable API contract as of this profile.

providers.name: SequoiaDB
providers.description: SequoiaDB (巨杉数据库) is a distributed, document-oriented NoSQL database built for financial-grade workloads and widely deployed across banking, insurance, securities, and government systems in China — running in production at more than 100 banks. A single cluster scales to 500 physical servers, 3.0 PB of storage, and 1.4 trillion rows, with remote disaster recovery targeting RPO=0 and RTO under 15 seconds. The platform is multi-model: a native distributed storage engine with full ACID transactions, a MongoDB-protocol-compatible document store (dds) with built-in vector indexing for AI workloads, a MySQL-compatible SQL engine (SequoiaSQL-MySQL), and an S3-compatible object interface (SequoiaCM). The core engine is open source under Apache-2.0, and access is provided through native client drivers for Java, Python, C, C++, PHP, and C#/.NET rather than a public HTTP REST API. SequoiaDB is backed by DCM Ventures and Qiming Venture Partners.

providers.name: Apis Partners
providers.description: Apis Partners is a London-headquartered private equity asset manager investing in tech-enabled financial infrastructure and financial services businesses across Europe and Growth Markets. With additional offices in Dubai and Singapore, the firm backs companies in payments, digital banking, insurance technology and lending, taking minority positions with governance rights. Apis manages approximately $2.3 billion in assets under management and reports over $1 billion in portfolio realizations, with portfolio companies reaching more than 244 million people. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Anthemis and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment; the firm is an investor rather than an API producer, so it exposes no public developer API surface.

providers.name: Erebor
providers.description: Erebor is a digital-first, FDIC-insured national bank built for the innovation economy — technology startups, cryptocurrency and stablecoin businesses, and AI and defense companies that traditional banks have historically underserved. Co-founded by Palmer Luckey (Anduril) and Joe Lonsdale (8VC) and backed by Founders Fund, Lux Capital, Haun Ventures, and 8VC, Erebor received OCC preliminary conditional approval in October 2025, FDIC deposit-insurance approval in December 2025, and launched in February 2026. It offers deposit accounts, wires and money movement, and stablecoin operations. Erebor exposes a developer API at api.erebor.bank secured with API keys, an Auth0-authenticated developer dashboard at developer.erebor.bank, and Fern-based developer documentation at docs.erebor.bank. The public developer docs are login-gated, so the machine-readable surface captured here is limited to what is observable without credentials.

providers.name: Murphy
providers.description: Murphy is a Barcelona-based fintech building AI voice and omnichannel agents that automate debt collection and servicing for banks, fintechs, utilities, telecoms and debt collection agencies. Founded in 2024 by Borja Sole and Marc Sanchez, the platform runs 24/7 AI agents across voice, SMS and email in 15+ languages, handling inbound and outbound recovery with human escalation, behavioural personalisation and fully audited, compliance-bounded interactions (ISO 27001, GDPR and EU AI Act aligned). Murphy claims materially higher recovery rates and 50-70% lower operational cost. It raised roughly $15M (seed + pre-seed) led by Northzone with ElevenLabs, Lakestar, Seedcamp and Enzo Ventures. Added to the API Evangelist network as a company profile; no public developer API, SDK or documentation surface is currently published.

providers.name: Papernest
providers.description: Papernest is a French technology company, founded in 2015 and headquartered in Paris, that provides a digital platform for managing, switching, and cancelling household subscriptions — energy, telecom and internet, mobile plans, and home insurance — through a single interface. Built around the moment people move home, the service is free to end users and monetized through commissions from supplier partners across France, Spain, Italy, and the UK, having helped more than 3 million customers. Papernest does not publish a public developer API; it runs a private B2B partner integration program and maintains an official GitHub organization of archived open-source utilities.

providers.name: Highbeam
providers.description: Highbeam is a business banking and finance platform built for modern consumer brands (direct-to-consumer and e-commerce). It brings together operating and high-yield accounts, a charge card that pays cashback on advertising spend, working capital and credit lines, automated bill pay, and spend intelligence, alongside Luma, an applied-AI finance assistant. Banking services are delivered through partner banks (Thread Bank, member FDIC) and Airwallex. Highbeam is based in New York City. As of this profile it publishes no public developer API, developer portal, or machine-readable API specification; this entry captures the company identity, its public web properties, and a live domain-security probe.

providers.name: defi SOLUTIONS
providers.description: defi SOLUTIONS is an auto and consumer lending technology company founded in 2012 and headquartered in Westlake, Texas. It provides cloud-native, API-enabled loan origination software (defi ORIGINATIONS), a servicing platform for account, collateral, and default management, digital borrower acquisition and self-service portals, and outsourced (BPO) managed servicing. The platform serves captive auto finance companies, banks, credit unions, and consumer finance companies, and ships 135+ pre-built partner integrations (Dealertrack, RouteOne, TransUnion, Equifax, LexisNexis, Experian, Black Book, J.D. Power, Zest AI, and more). APIs move borrower and loan data between origination and servicing but are exposed to enterprise customers and integration partners rather than through a public developer portal.

providers.name: Desjardins Group
providers.description: Desjardins Group (Mouvement Desjardins) is the largest cooperative financial group in North America, founded in 1900 in Lévis, Quebec by Alphonse Desjardins. It is a federation of caisses populaires (member-owned credit unions) rather than a share-capital chartered bank, comprising the Fédération des caisses Desjardins du Québec and its subsidiaries, the caisses in Quebec and the Caisse Desjardins Ontario Credit Union, regulated in Quebec by the Autorité des marchés financiers (AMF). It holds roughly CAD $470 billion in assets and serves more than 7.8 million members and clients with personal, business, wealth-management and insurance products. On open finance, Desjardins publishes no first-party public developer portal or downloadable API specification; developer.desjardins.com and other API-portal subdomains do not resolve, and consumer financial-data access is delivered today through third-party aggregators (Flinks, Plaid, Finicity, Tink) via screen-scraping/aggregator connectivity rather than a documented Desjardins API. Canada's Consumer-Driven Banking (open-banking) framework is legislated (Budget 2024/2025, overseen by the FCAC) but not yet operational; as a cooperative outside the Big Six, Desjardins may opt in to Phase 1 rather than being mandated.

providers.name: EquityBee
providers.description: EquityBee is a fintech marketplace that helps startup employees fund the exercise of their stock options before those options expire, giving them the cash needed to purchase their equity while the company is still private. On the other side of the marketplace, EquityBee connects accredited investors with the opportunity to invest in pre-IPO companies by funding those employee option exercises in exchange for a share of the future proceeds. Founded in 2018, the company operates a two-sided platform spanning startup employees, accredited investors, and the private companies whose equity underlies each funded position. EquityBee publishes a public marketing and account website but exposes no public developer API, SDK, or machine-readable API discovery surface at this time.

providers.name: Halogen Capital
providers.description: Halogen Capital is Malaysia's first and only licensed digital asset fund manager, regulated by the Securities Commission Malaysia (License eCMSL/A0388/2023) and headquartered in Kuala Lumpur. The firm gives high-net-worth individuals, family offices, corporates, and institutional investors regulated access to cryptocurrency and traditional assets through unit trust structures, offering Shariah-compliant Bitcoin, Ethereum, and Crypto Titans basket funds alongside a MYR liquid fund, a ringgit income fund, and an enhanced income fund, all secured with multi-signature custody. Backed by Kenanga Investment Bank and 500 Global, Halogen manages roughly RM400 million in assets under management and is expanding into real-world asset (RWA) tokenization. This API Evangelist profile currently tracks the company's public web presence and domain-security posture; no public developer API surface was found during enrichment.

providers.name: Hum Capital
providers.description: Hum Capital operates an AI-powered funding marketplace that connects growth companies with the right institutional capital. Through its Intelligent Capital Market platform, companies share their financial and operating data once and are matched to a network of 900+ lenders and investors for non-dilutive and structured financing (typically $1M-$50M), while investors receive curated, data-driven deal flow. Hum reports more than $700M in capital deployed across 6,000+ companies. Headquartered in New York, the company operates in the financial services, capital markets, and alternative-financing sector. This API Evangelist profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Partech and enriched from the company's public web surface; Hum publishes no public developer API, so this entry is identity- and security-focused.

providers.name: INBOTIQA
providers.description: INBOTIQA is a UK-based fintech whose flagship product, YUDOmail, is an Intelligent Business Email and shared-mailbox management platform for high-volume group inboxes at banks, BPOs and financial-services operations teams. YUDOmail layers over Microsoft 365 and Google Workspace to turn incoming emails into assigned, trackable tasks with ownership, due dates, SLA tracking, machine-learning triage and sentiment analysis, audit trails and analytics, without replacing the underlying email platform. It deploys in the cloud or on-premises, integrates with Symphony chat and Microsoft Teams, and is used across KYC, FX, collateral, settlements and trade-support functions. INBOTIQA was a 2019 Barclays Accelerator (powered by Techstars) company.

providers.name: Possible Finance
providers.description: Possible Finance is a consumer fintech company offering small-dollar installment loans and credit-building products through a mobile app. Its core products are the Possible Loan (up to $500 with flexible repayment schedules), the Possible Advance (up to $300 drawn against a future paycheck), and Bill & Rent Reporting that builds credit history by reporting on-time payments to the credit bureaus. The company charges no late fees or penalty charges and uses AI-driven underwriting based on real banking activity rather than FICO scores, serving borrowers who are underserved by traditional credit. Possible Finance operates as a Delaware Public Benefit Corporation and is backed by Union Square Ventures. It is a mobile-app, consumer-facing product with no public developer API surface; this profile captures its identity and domain-security posture for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Aboon
providers.description: Aboon is a digital 401(k) retirement-plan platform and third-party administrator (TPA) that helps financial advisors and employers design, launch, and manage workplace retirement plans. It pairs AI-powered workflows with dedicated human plan consultants to generate customized 401(k) proposals in minutes, streamline recordkeeper onboarding, handle digital plan contracting and census intake, and run ongoing compliance testing and Form 3(16) administration. Aboon markets partnerships with major recordkeepers (American Funds, Empower, John Hancock, and others) and serves a network of advisors nationwide. It is a fintech company backed by Bain Capital Ventures. No public developer/API surface has been identified.

providers.name: Aura Finance
providers.description: Aura Finance is an employer-sponsored financial wellness platform that blends behavioral psychology with money management to help employees reach financial stability and peace of mind. The San Francisco fintech — a Techstars Economic Mobility 2023 company and an SEC-registered investment adviser (CRD 318940) — delivers goal-based automated investing, one-on-one financial coaching over chat, budgeting and saving tools, financial-literacy workshops, mindfulness exercises to reduce money stress, and a money-personality quiz, offered through a B2B2C model to organizations and their workforces. The company publishes no public developer program, API, or SDKs; its member application lives at web.aurafi.io.

providers.name: Bank of Hawaii
providers.description: Bank of Hawaii is a state-chartered commercial bank organized under the laws of the State of Hawaii in 1897, a member of the Federal Reserve System and FDIC-insured. It is the principal banking subsidiary of Bank of Hawaii Corporation (NYSE: BOH), a Honolulu-headquartered regional financial services company serving Hawaii, Guam, and other Pacific islands with consumer, commercial, and wealth-management banking. As a regional US institution, Bank of Hawaii publishes no first-party public developer portal and exposes no documented public API surface; probes of developer.boh.com and developers.boh.com do not resolve. US open finance is voluntary and fragmented, and consumer-permissioned data access to Bank of Hawaii accounts is available in practice only through third-party aggregators (for example Plaid), not through a direct bank-operated API. No Financial Data Exchange (FDX) membership and no published CFPB Section 1033 data-access posture were found at the time of this record.

providers.name: Motilal Oswal
providers.description: Motilal Oswal Financial Services Limited (MOFSL) is a diversified Indian financial services company offering equity and derivatives broking, wealth management, asset management, mutual funds, IPO access, investment banking, private equity, and home finance. Surfaced as a portfolio company of bessemer-venture-partners and profiled in the API Evangelist network. The public surface is a consumer/corporate investing website built on Adobe Experience Manager Edge Delivery Services; no public developer API or OpenAPI is published (algorithmic/partner trading access sits behind a partner login).

providers.name: dopay
providers.description: dopay is a digital payroll platform operating in Egypt that lets employers register employees and disburse salaries in minutes through a single system, including permanent, temporary, and seasonal workers across construction, agriculture, hospitality, retail, healthcare, education, and manufacturing. Supervised by a bank and regulated by the Central Bank of Egypt, dopay digitizes cash-based wage payments and pairs core Salary Disbursement with an Early Pay earned-wage-access product that lets employees withdraw part of their salary before payday. Originally a Techstars-backed fintech focused on banking the unbanked, dopay is added to the API Evangelist network as a company profile; it publishes a business web app and login but no public developer API, portal, or documentation at this time.

providers.name: Epsor
providers.description: Epsor is a French fintech, founded in 2017, that manages employee savings and retirement plans (épargne salariale et retraite) for companies and helps them turn that benefit into an HR lever. A certified B Corp and mission-driven company, Epsor ranks among the top 10 employee-savings and retirement providers in France and serves more than 2,500 corporate clients. It targets HR, Compensation & Benefits, and Finance teams at mid-size and large French firms, combining a pedagogical, personalized saver experience, an open-architecture fund range (40+ funds from 15+ asset managers, with a strong ESG/SRI focus), and year-round support to run and promote the plan. Epsor is neither an asset manager nor a bank: it is the single point of contact for companies and their employees, and delegates account-keeping to Société Générale Securities Services (SGSS). Products span PEE, PER Collectif (PERECO), PER Obligatoire, intéressement, participation, abondement, and employee share ownership. Epsor exposes no public developer API; this profile captures its public identity and security posture for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: First Hawaiian Bank
providers.description: First Hawaiian Bank is Hawaii's oldest and largest financial institution, founded in 1858 and headquartered at First Hawaiian Center in Honolulu. It is a Hawaii state-chartered commercial bank and member FDIC, operating as the principal subsidiary of First Hawaiian, Inc. (NASDAQ ticker FHB), a publicly traded bank holding company. The bank serves consumer and commercial customers through roughly 57 branches in Hawaii plus locations in Guam and Saipan, offering deposit accounts, lending, wealth management, treasury/cash management, and merchant services. On the open-finance front, First Hawaiian operates no public first-party developer portal and publishes no downloadable OpenAPI/Swagger specifications; probes of developer.fhb.com, api.fhb.com, and fhb.com/en/developers returned no host or HTTP 404. Consumer-permissioned account data is reachable only through third-party aggregators (notably Plaid), not a direct bank API. No documented Financial Data Exchange (FDX) participation or published CFPB Section 1033 data-access posture was found as of this record. Its commercial online banking product (FHB Commercial Online, formerly OBC) is a traditional web application rather than a developer-facing API surface.

providers.name: Greenboard
providers.description: Greenboard is an AI-native compliance software platform for SEC- and FINRA-regulated financial institutions, consolidating communications archiving, employee compliance monitoring, marketing/advertising review, firm-wide compliance management, and third-party (vendor) compliance into a single system of action. It serves independent advisors, RIAs, hedge funds, private funds, and broker-dealers, automating regulatory workflows and reducing review times. Greenboard is a General Catalyst portfolio company. Its product is delivered as a hosted SaaS application; no public developer API, OpenAPI specification, or developer portal is published at this time, so this profile captures corporate identity, trust/compliance posture (SOC 2 Type II), and domain security rather than API artifacts.

providers.name: iCapital Network
providers.description: iCapital (Institutional Capital Network, Inc.) is a New York-headquartered financial technology company, founded in 2013, that operates the alternative investments marketplace and the operating infrastructure behind it. Its platform lets wealth managers, RIAs, family offices and institutional investors research, subscribe to, service and report on private markets funds, hedge funds, structured investments, annuities, model portfolios and separately managed accounts, while asset managers use it to distribute those products into the wealth channel. iCapital Marketplace advertises access to funds from 700+ asset managers and reports $945B+ in global platform assets. Around the marketplace sit Architect (portfolio construction and analytics), Data Solutions (alternative data management and consolidated reporting), Identity Solutions (KYC/AML), and iCapital DLT, an API-first distributed ledger platform built on the Canton Network. Integration with custodians, fund administrators, transfer agents and advisor platforms (BNY, Fidelity, Envestnet, Orion, Morningstar, Vestmark, TradePMR, GeoWealth, Ultimus, UMB) happens through SSO, embedded workflows and partner data integrations. As of the 2026-08-01 enrichment pass iCapital publishes no public developer portal, API reference, machine-readable API contract or client SDKs; API documentation is described as available to integration partners only, through the sales and technical-support organization.

providers.name: OpenFX
providers.description: OpenFX is a cross-border payment infrastructure provider delivering real-time foreign exchange liquidity and settlement for institutional clients across emerging markets. Backed by Accel and Northzone, it pairs traditional-finance reliability with blockchain-rail speed to settle fiat and stablecoin payments in minutes across 40+ currency pairs and 25+ local payment rails, and exposes a programmatic Trading API (REST, FIX and Streaming) to automate quotes, trades, deposits and withdrawals. Serves remittance companies, FX on/off ramps, payment service providers and stablecoin infrastructure providers.

providers.name: RCS Capital
providers.description: RCS Capital Corporation (RCAP) was a publicly traded holding company focused on the financial services industry, founded by Nicholas Schorsch and taken public in June 2013. The firm owned a diversified group of businesses including independent broker-dealers, investment banking, capital markets, and transaction management services. It assembled Cetera Financial Group to become the second largest network of independent broker-dealers in the United States, with approximately 9,100 financial advisors managing $220 billion in assets under administration for 2.5 million clients. RCS Capital filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection in January 2016, citing $1.39 billion in debts, and emerged in May 2016 as Aretec Group, Inc., the holding company of Cetera Financial Group. No public developer APIs were offered under the RCS Capital brand.

providers.name: Securian Financial
providers.description: Securian Financial Group is a Saint Paul, Minnesota-based mutual holding company offering life insurance, annuities, institutional retirement solutions, trust services, investment management and group workplace benefits to individuals, employers, financial institutions and institutional clients across the United States and Canada. Its operating companies include Minnesota Life Insurance Company, Securian Life Insurance Company, Securian Asset Management and Securian Canada. Securian does not run a public developer program: its integration surfaces are partner-facing and sales-gated. Securian Platform Connect exchanges benefits data with employer benefits-administration platforms using LIMRA LDEx standards (Evidence of Insurability and Benefits Enrollment Management) plus SSO, API notifications and file feeds, and FlexTech - launched March 2026 with Walnut - embeds payment protection into digital lending journeys through API-based integration. Neither publishes a machine-readable contract, developer portal or self-service onboarding.

providers.name: Brinks
providers.description: Brink's is a global leader in secure cash management, armored transport, ATM services, and financial security solutions. The company serves retail, restaurant, financial institutions, and entertainment businesses with its Total Cash Management platform, combining hardware, software, and logistics services. Brink's digital customer portal 24SEVEN ACCESS enables businesses to track cash deposits, order change, and manage operations via mobile and desktop interfaces. Additional products include the Brink's Armored Account payment processing service, Brink's Money paycard for employee payments, and RetailBox point-of-sale cash management.

providers.name: Freddie Mac
providers.description: Freddie Mac (Federal Home Loan Mortgage Corporation) provides liquidity, stability, and affordability to the U.S. housing market. Its Single-Family API solutions span origination, selling and delivery, and servicing, delivering data and decisioning at each stage of the mortgage lifecycle.

providers.name: Funding Societies | Modalku
providers.description: Funding Societies (known as Modalku in Indonesia) is Southeast Asia's largest SME digital financing and investment platform, connecting small and medium enterprises seeking working capital with individual and institutional investors. Operating across Singapore, Indonesia, Malaysia, Thailand, Vietnam and Hong Kong, the platform offers micro loans, business term loans, invoice and accounts-payable/receivable financing, startup financing and property-backed secured lending, alongside investment products for lenders. It is licensed and regulated (Capital Markets Services License, Monetary Authority of Singapore) and was surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network. No public developer API, documentation, or developer portal is currently published.

providers.name: LedgiFi
providers.description: LedgiFi (formerly Krypto Ledgers) is a Latin American cryptocurrency tax and portfolio-tracking platform founded in 2020 and headquartered in Antofagasta, Chile. The product syncs a user's transaction history from exchanges and wallets — Binance, Coinbase, Kraken and MetaMask among them — normalizes it across more than 25,000 assets, and computes realized capital gains using the valuation methods and monetary-correction adjustments each jurisdiction requires, so investors can file a compliant return. Its Chilean profile applies the SII's specific rules (IPC indexation and dollar-variation adjustments, Impuesto de Primera Categoría and Impuesto Global Complementario), and the platform has since expanded to Mexico, Spain, Colombia and Argentina. Alongside tax reporting it offers a portfolio view spanning crypto, stocks and ETFs, with per-asset performance and allocation. LedgiFi is a 500 Global (500 LatAm B18) portfolio company. It runs a monitored production API at api.ledgifi.com that backs its own web and mobile apps, but publishes no developer portal, no API specification and no self-service API program.

providers.name: Splash Financial
providers.description: Splash Financial is a Cleveland, Ohio financial technology company and online lending marketplace, founded in 2013, that matches consumers with loan offers from a network of partner banks and credit unions rather than lending directly itself. The platform uses automated underwriting to prequalify borrowers and present competing offers across student loan refinancing, personal loans, debt consolidation, home equity lines of credit, in-school private student loans, and medical school loan refinancing. The company reports having helped more than 125,000 people refinance over $6 billion in loans. Splash also sells its origination technology to credit unions and community banks as a partner channel, but that integration is arranged through a business development contact form and no public developer portal, API reference, or machine-readable specification is published.

providers.name: Wintrust Financial
providers.description: Wintrust Financial Corporation is a Rosemont, Illinois-based financial holding company operating a network of chartered community banks (Wintrust Bank, N.A. and its affiliates) primarily across Illinois, Wisconsin, Indiana and Florida, plus specialty lending, wealth management and mortgage businesses. Wintrust does not publish a first-party public developer portal or downloadable API specifications; its programmatic surface is delivered through commercial treasury management. Wintrust describes "API banking" that connects businesses directly to its secure file transfer protocol (SFTP) for account balance and activity reporting, payment files (Positive Pay, ACH, wires, EDI, lockbox) and data-format translation (NACHA, EDI 820, BAI2). Consumer and small-business account data is reachable to third parties through open-banking aggregators — Plaid is the confirmed aggregator supporting Wintrust / iBusinessBanking access.

providers.name: Asaak
providers.description: Asaak is an East African fintech company, headquartered in Kampala, Uganda, that provides asset financing and working capital to small businesses and individual entrepreneurs who are underserved by traditional banks. Its core products are loans for boda boda motorcycles, fuel, and smartphones, delivered through a mobile-first application with a simple four-step flow of apply, qualify, receive financing, and repay to build credit. Asaak operates branches across Uganda (Kampala, Jinja, Mukono, Matugga, Nabbingo, Fort Portal, Gulu, and Soroti) and is a 500 Global portfolio company. It runs a backend admin platform at api.asaak.net and a Wix-hosted marketing site that exposes a live Model Context Protocol (MCP) endpoint for agentic access to public site content. Asaak does not currently publish a public developer API or OpenAPI.

providers.name: Associated Bank
providers.description: Associated Bank, N.A. is the primary banking subsidiary of Associated Banc-Corp (NYSE ASB), a nationally chartered commercial bank and the largest bank holding company headquartered in Wisconsin, based in Green Bay. With roughly $50 billion in total assets following the April 2026 acquisition of American National Corporation, Associated operates a full-service Midwest banking franchise of more than 200 locations across Wisconsin, Illinois, Iowa, Minnesota, Missouri and Nebraska, offering consumer, business, commercial and wealth-management services. Associated does not publish a first-party public developer portal or downloadable OpenAPI/Swagger specifications. Its digital banking runs on a core-provider stack (Jack Henry), and consumer-permissioned data access is delivered through third-party aggregators (Plaid, Tink/TrueLayer) rather than a direct first-party API. Its commercial treasury customers use the login-gated Associated Connect platform. No FDX participation or CFPB Section 1033 data-access posture is publicly documented as of this review.

providers.name: Blnk Finance
providers.description: Open-source double-entry ledger for financial products (wallets, loans, payouts, escrow, cards). Available as self-hosted Blnk Core (OSS engine) and Blnk Cloud (managed), plus Blnk Watch for transaction monitoring. Exposes REST APIs with a public OpenAPI spec, hosted MCP servers, llms.txt, and installable agent skills.

providers.name: Calastone
providers.description: Calastone operates the world's largest global funds network, connecting asset managers, distributors, custodians and platforms to automate and digitalize the investment funds marketplace. Founded in 2007 and headquartered in London, it provides order routing, settlements, share-class conversions, dividends, transfers, reporting, money market services and tokenized fund distribution. More than 4,500 clients across 58 countries and territories use the network, processing over £300 billion of investment value each month. API and messaging connectivity is delivered through client onboarding rather than a public self-service developer portal. Calastone is a wholly owned subsidiary of SS&C Technologies Holdings, Inc. (Nasdaq: SSNC).

providers.name: Exactera
providers.description: Exactera is a corporate tax technology and advisory company that pairs AI-powered software with expert tax professionals to help multinational corporations manage the full corporate tax lifecycle. Its SaaS platform and services span transfer pricing compliance and benchmarking, R&D tax credits, fixed-asset depreciation, indirect (sales and use) tax advisory, tax provision, and the RoyaltyStat royalty-rate and transfer-pricing data platform. Exactera automates documentation, benchmarking studies, and regulatory reporting so tax and finance teams can reduce audit exposure and meet global compliance requirements. Backed by Insight Partners, the company serves enterprise tax departments and advisory firms worldwide.

providers.name: FlyHomes
providers.description: Flyhomes is a Bellevue, Washington-based real estate and mortgage financial technology company whose Buy Before You Sell platform lets homebuyers purchase a new home before selling their existing one. Its products—Flyhomes Cash Offer, Instant Equity, and Guaranteed Backup Contract—turn financing into competitive cash-like offers, unlock home equity without requiring a prior sale, and reduce a buyer's debt-to-income ratio so they can qualify for larger loans and move only once. Flyhomes reaches homebuyers through a network of in-network loan officers and real estate agents and also operates an AI-powered home search portal. Flyhomes does not currently publish a public developer API; this profile captures its identity, discovery surface (llms.txt), and domain-security posture.

providers.name: Good Driver
providers.description: Good Driver Club (formerly Good Driver Mutuality) is an insurtech company backed by Ribbit Capital and Hedosophia. It runs a membership-based, cost-sharing alternative to traditional collision and comprehensive auto coverage: members pay weekly pledges into a shared community pool that covers vehicle damage from accidents, weather, theft, and other qualifying events across 5,000+ partner repair shops nationwide, and accident-free members keep their unused pledge balances as savings. It is explicitly not insurance. The product is delivered through a consumer mobile app (Good Driver Club on Google Play); the company publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI, or documentation surface at this time.

providers.name: Exporo
providers.description: Exporo is a Hamburg, Germany-based digital investment platform for real estate and renewable-energy infrastructure, operating as a regulated European Crowdfunding Service Provider (ECSP). The platform lets private investors participate in residential and commercial property development as well as clean-energy projects such as solar, with typical terms of 12-36 months. Exporo has mediated over EUR 1.17 billion of capital across more than 600 financed projects, and also offers Club Deals for larger qualified investors. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Partech and added to the API Evangelist network. No public developer API or developer portal is currently published; this profile is maintained as a company lead and will be enriched if a developer surface appears.

providers.name: Provide
providers.description: Provide is a financial services division of Fifth Third Bank offering banking and financing built specifically for owners of professional practices — dental, medical, veterinary, optometry, childcare, financial advisory, funeral, and insurance businesses. The company provides conventional and SBA loans to start, acquire, or expand a practice, alongside a full suite of customized banking products. Provide was acquired by Fifth Third Bank and operates as a specialty lending and banking brand. Surfaced as a portfolio company of QED Investors; it publishes no public developer API, documentation, or developer portal at this time.

providers.name: Tangerine
providers.description: Tangerine is a Canadian direct (branchless) bank headquartered in Toronto, Ontario, and a federally regulated Schedule I bank chartered as Tangerine Bank (institution number 614). Founded in 1997 as ING Direct Canada, it was acquired by Scotiabank in 2012 and rebranded as Tangerine in 2014; it remains a separate legal entity operating as Scotiabank's digital-banking arm, serving roughly two million clients with no-fee chequing and savings accounts, GICs, mortgages, mutual funds, and a cash-back Mastercard delivered entirely through mobile and web. On API and open-finance posture, Tangerine publishes no first-party public developer portal or downloadable API specifications; Canada has no operational consumer-driven-banking mandate yet (the federal framework is legislated but not live), so third-party access to Tangerine account and transaction data today is aggregator-based via Plaid and Finicity (Mastercard) rather than through a documented first-party API.

providers.name: Ares Management
providers.description: Ares Management is a major US corporation and Fortune 1000 company. The Ares Management API provides programmatic access to its platform services, data, and integrations for enterprise customers and partners.

providers.name: Avantos
providers.description: Avantos is an AI-native operating system for client management in financial services, built for wealth management and advisory firms. The platform unifies client data, products, teams, and workflows into a knowledge graph that powers agentic onboarding, relationship intelligence, and an AI-powered servicing workspace where agents anticipate client needs and streamline operations. It integrates with existing CRMs, custodians, and core systems, and is SOC 2 compliant with enterprise-grade architecture. Avantos raised a $35M Series A led by Bessemer Venture Partners, announced February 2026.

providers.name: BNP Paribas
providers.description: BNP Paribas is a leading international banking group providing a wide range of financial services to individuals, businesses, and institutions worldwide. The company offers APIs through its CIB Developer Portal covering capital markets, payment services, securities services, and open banking integrations for corporate and institutional clients.

providers.name: Halo Investing
providers.description: Halo Investing is a Chicago-based financial technology company that operates a marketplace for "protective investments" — structured notes, multi-manager structured note SMAs, buffered ETFs, annuities and insurance — connecting financial advisors, RIAs and financial institutions with more than 40 global banking and insurance issuers. Founded in 2015 by Biju Kulathakal and Jason Barsema, the platform lets advisors analyze, customize, price, execute and then monitor outcome-based products from a single dashboard, with tools such as the Aura portfolio simulator and an asset allocation framework for structured notes. Halo reports more than $45.5B in transactions since 2015 and employs 100+ people. Its affiliate Halo Securities LLC is an SEC-registered broker-dealer and a member of FINRA/SIPC, acting as distributor and selling agent for structured note products. The advisor platform at notes.haloinvesting.com is entirely authenticated behind a login. As of this profiling pass Halo Investing publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, OpenAPI/AsyncAPI/GraphQL contract, SDK, CLI, MCP server or A2A agent card; advisor-side API integration is offered through the third-party Schwab OpenView Gateway rather than a Halo-published API.

providers.name: M&T Bank
providers.description: M&T Bank is a US super-regional bank holding company (M&T Bank Corporation, NYSE: MTB) headquartered in Buffalo, New York, operating through its national bank subsidiary Manufacturers and Traders Trust Company. With roughly $200 billion in assets it is one of the twenty largest US commercial banks, serving consumers, businesses, and institutional clients across the eastern United States, and it owns Wilmington Trust, its custody, fund-administration, and wealth arm. Unlike UK/AU open banking there is no single mandated contract in the US, so M&T's public API posture is split: it runs a real first-party Developer Portal / "API Store" at developer.mtb.com for institutional and wholesale clients (Banking & Treasury plus Wilmington Trust Custody APIs), gated behind Microsoft Entra login and Azure API Management subscription keys with per-product OpenAPI reference available only after authentication. Consumer-permissioned account data is shared through aggregators (Plaid) rather than a public first-party consumer API. No public FDX conformance or CFPB Section 1033 data-access API is documented on the portal at review time.

providers.name: Avant
providers.description: Avant is a Chicago-based financial technology company that provides consumer credit products to middle-income U.S. consumers, primarily unsecured personal loans of roughly $2,000-$35,000 (9.95%-35.99% APR, 24-60 month terms) for debt consolidation, emergencies, home improvement, and other needs, alongside the Avant Credit Card issued through WebBank. Founded in 2012 and backed by investors including QED Investors and 500 Global, Avant operates a mobile-first lending and card-servicing platform with a customer help center, personal-finance blog, and SCRA support for military members. Avant is a consumer-facing product company and does not publish a public developer API or portal; this profile captures its public web, security, and support surfaces.

providers.name: Curve
providers.description: Curve is a London-based fintech, founded in 2015 by Shachar Bialick, that consolidates multiple debit and credit cards into a single smart card and mobile wallet. Its "over-the-top" banking platform lets customers spend from any linked Mastercard or Visa card, switch the funding source of a past purchase up to 120 days later with "Go Back in Time", avoid foreign-exchange fees, earn cashback, and pay in instalments with Curve Flex. Premium tiers (Curve Pay X / Pro / Pro+) add insurance, lounge access, and richer rewards. Curve is backed by Seedcamp and Speedinvest among others. Curve does not publish a public developer API — it acts as an open-banking consumer to aggregate customer account balances rather than exposing a provider API.

providers.name: First Horizon
providers.description: First Horizon Corporation is a Fortune 500 financial services holding company headquartered in Memphis, Tennessee. Through First Horizon Bank it provides commercial, private, consumer, and mortgage banking, wealth management, and capital markets services across the southern United States. First Horizon operates a real API Banking developer portal for Treasury Management clients, exposing RESTful products for money movement, ACH origination, real-time account information, and routing-number lookups, secured with OAuth 2.0 and a sandbox for build-and-test integration. Onboarding is partner/relationship gated and no OpenAPI/Swagger specifications are publicly downloadable — this repository captures the documented API surface honestly, humanURL-only.

providers.name: Kiavi
providers.description: Kiavi (formerly LendingHome) is a technology-driven private lender for residential real estate investors, providing fix-and-flip bridge loans, new-construction financing, and DSCR rental loans across 49 states plus Washington, D.C. The company has originated more than $30 billion in loans and funded over 100,000 investment properties, pairing a digital application and portfolio-management experience with institutional capital. Kiavi is backed by Cowboy Ventures and Ribbit Capital. As of this enrichment pass Kiavi publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI, or developer portal; its public surface is a marketing site, a real-estate-investing blog, legal/policy pages, and a HackerOne-based security vulnerability disclosure program.

providers.name: MidFirst Bank
providers.description: MidFirst Bank is a federally chartered savings association (thrift) headquartered in Oklahoma City, Oklahoma, and owned by Midland Financial Co. Founded in 1982 with roots in Midland Mortgage from the early 1950s, it is the largest privately owned bank in the United States, with roughly $42 billion in assets and retail banking, private banking, commercial real estate lending, and nationwide mortgage servicing operations across Oklahoma, Arizona, California, Colorado, Nevada, Texas, and Utah. MidFirst does not operate a first-party public developer portal or publish downloadable OpenAPI/Swagger specifications. Its open-finance posture is aggregator-mediated: through its "Open Access" program, MidFirst adds direct API connections between its Business Online Banking platforms and consumer-permissioned data aggregators (Plaid, MX, Stripe, Intuit, Mastercard/Finicity, Envestnet Yodlee, and Morningstar), replacing screen scraping. There is no publicly documented first-party API surface, and no FDX participation or CFPB Section 1033 data-access posture is published on its site as of this review.

providers.name: Albo
providers.description: Albo (albo.com, formerly albo.mx) is a Mexican digital financial services company founded in 2016 and operating since 2022 as an Institución de Fondos de Pago Electrónico (IFPE) authorized by the Comisión Nacional Bancaria y de Valores (CNBV) and regulated by Banco de México. Albo ships a mobile-first personal account with a Mastercard debit card — SPEI transfers, bill payments, cash deposit and withdrawal at partner locations, and real-time notifications — alongside "albo empresa", a business account for payroll, employee cards, and bulk dispersion of up to 3,000 transactions at a time. Adjacent credit (abea, by Aureo Lab) and crypto (albit, by Indigo DeFi) products are offered by independent partners. Albo publishes no public developer program: no developer portal, API reference, OpenAPI/AsyncAPI specification, SDK, webhook catalog, or sandbox was found on any albo.com, albo.mx or albo.live host.

providers.name: Crabi
providers.description: Crabi is a Mexican digital auto-insurance company (insurtech) offering fully online vehicle policies purchasable in about fifteen minutes from a mobile device. Coverage spans material damage, theft, third-party civil liability, medical expenses, and roadside and legal assistance across 27 Mexican states, sold and serviced through its mobile apps, online quoter (cotizador), and customer login portal. The company is regulated in Mexico by the CNSF and CONDUSEF and is a portfolio company of 500 Global. Crabi publishes no public developer API, documentation, or SDKs; this profile captures its identity and public web surface.

providers.name: Earnix
providers.description: Earnix provides an AI orchestration system (Earnix AIOS) purpose-built for insurance and banking decisioning. The platform unifies pricing, an enterprise rating engine, automated underwriting, and real-time customer engagement so insurers and financial institutions can price smarter, underwrite faster, and engage customers better. Earnix serves 100+ leading insurers worldwide, processing billions of transactions annually and compressing rate creation from months to days. Earnix is a portfolio company of Insight Partners. This profile was enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline; Earnix is an enterprise B2B vendor with no public self-serve developer portal or API documentation.

providers.name: Fabric Technologies
providers.description: Fabric Technologies operates Fabric by Gerber Life, a direct-to-consumer financial services platform built for parents and families. The company offers term life insurance with an instant online quote and application flow, UGMA custodial investment accounts and 529 college-savings plans for children, and digital estate-planning tools including free wills. Fabric is backed by Gerber Life, part of Western & Southern Financial Group, and was originally venture-funded by Bessemer Venture Partners. The platform emphasizes fast, accessible, mobile-first family financial planning spanning protection, wealth-building, and legacy planning. Fabric is a consumer-facing service and does not currently publish a public developer API or portal.

providers.name: Marcus by Goldman Sachs
providers.description: Marcus by Goldman Sachs is the U.S. consumer banking brand of The Goldman Sachs Group, launched in 2016 to offer no-fee high-yield Online Savings Accounts and Certificates of Deposit (CDs) directly to retail customers online. Deposits are held at Goldman Sachs Bank USA, a New York State-chartered bank and member of the Federal Reserve System, insured by the FDIC. After Goldman's broad retreat from consumer lending, Marcus no longer originates personal loans and now centers on digital deposit products. Marcus operates NO public first-party consumer developer API and runs no self-serve developer portal for its retail banking products; the Goldman Sachs Developer platform (developer.gs.com) serves institutional Transaction Banking and Marquee offerings, not Marcus consumer banking. Consumer-permissioned account data (balances, transactions, account/holder info) is reachable only through third-party open-finance aggregators such as Plaid, Flinks, and MX, not a documented Marcus API. As a bank chartered in the U.S., Goldman Sachs Bank USA is subject to the emerging CFPB Section 1033 personal financial data rights framework, but no first-party FDX-conformant Marcus developer interface is publicly documented as of this record.

providers.name: Orus
providers.description: Orus is a French online insurance broker ("l'assurance professionnelle en ligne") offering professional-liability and business insurance to independent professionals and small businesses across France. Products include RC Pro (professional liability), Multirisque Professionnelle, Assurance Décennale (ten-year construction liability), Assurance Bureau (office insurance), Mutuelle Santé TNS (self-employed health), and Prévoyance TNS (income protection), serving sectors from consultants and construction to hospitality, retail, and wellness. Backed by Partech and Speedinvest, Orus operates a self-service quote-and-buy app (app.orus.eu) but publishes no public developer API, SDK, or integration surface at this time. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead and enriched via public web and domain probes.

providers.name: SEI Investments
providers.description: SEI Investments Company (NASDAQ: SEIC) is a publicly traded financial services and technology provider founded in 1968 and headquartered in Oaks, Pennsylvania. SEI delivers end-to-end technology, operations, and asset management solutions to asset managers, banks and wealth managers, financial advisors, and institutional investors. Marquee platforms include the SEI Wealth Platform (front-to-back wealth management technology and outsourced operations), SEI Data Cloud (managed near-real-time data platform), SEI Sphere (managed IT, cybersecurity, cloud, and network operations), and SEI Novus (institutional portfolio analytics). SEI does not run a public developer portal — partner and client integrations are delivered through contractual onboarding to the SEI Wealth Platform, SEI Connect advisor channels, and managed-service engagements rather than self-serve OpenAPI or SDK distribution.

providers.name: Teamshares Inc
providers.description: Teamshares is a tech-enabled acquirer of small businesses that offers a permanent home for companies whose owners are retiring. It programmatically buys profitable companies with $0.5-5 million of EBITDA from retiring owners, integrates them onto the Teamshares operating platform of financial products, software, and education, and helps employees earn company stock through employee ownership. Backed by QED Investors and other fintech investors, Teamshares runs a login-gated operating platform (os.teamshares.com) for its portfolio companies plus an investor portal. As of this profile Teamshares publishes no public developer API, developer portal, or API documentation.

providers.name: TRDATA
providers.description: TRDATA (TRDATA Technology Limited) is a real-time financial information and communication platform for professional traders, aggregating over-the-counter (OTC) quotes, prices, news, and analytics from market makers across fragmented fixed-income and emerging-market instruments. It covers Ukrainian, CEEMEA, and global bonds, currencies, commodities, and derivatives from local and international data providers, and bundles analytics tools such as a Bond Calculator, Bond Calendar, Swap Curves, real-time asset charts, and a TRDATA Excel add-in. More than 800 institutions -- including Societe Generale, UniCredit, Raiffeisen, BNP Paribas, Barclays, Deutsche Bank, and Commerzbank -- use the platform to read and exchange market information. TRDATA is backed by 500 Global. As of this profile the company publishes no public developer API, SDKs, or documentation surface; access is via registration and the hosted platform.

bands.label: Minimal
bands.blurb: Index entry only; little beyond a description and a link.

providers.name: Aviva
providers.description: Aviva (Aviva Financial, S.A. de C.V., SOFOM E.N.R.) is a Mexican fintech lender operating under the tagline "Tu historia importa." It offers quick, secured personal and business loans originated in person through a network of 100+ physical kiosks across central Mexico (Puebla, Hidalgo, Estado de Mexico, Morelos, Queretaro, Tlaxcala and Veracruz), using a video-call onboarding flow (the Aviva Onboarding System, AOS) with same-day or 24-hour direct-deposit disbursement. Products include Aviva Contigo (everyday expenses, up to $15,000), Aviva tu Negocio (business owners, up to $20,000), Aviva tu Compra (appliances at Bodega Aurrera), and Aviva tu Casa (construction materials via Construrama). Borrowers manage payments through the Aviva mobile app. Aviva was surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass Aviva publishes no public developer portal, API, SDKs, or OpenAPI - it exposes a consumer web/app and kiosk surface only.

providers.name: Clark
providers.description: Clark ("Dein Versicherungsmanager") is a Germany-based digital insurance manager that lets consumers view, compare, optimize, and manage all of their insurance policies in one mobile app and web platform. Founded in Frankfurt in 2015, Clark pairs a licensed insurance brokerage with automated tariff comparison across more than 180 insurance providers and free expert consultation, covering health, liability, property, life, mobility, and retirement products. The company operates across Germany, Switzerland, France, and the UK, serves over 700,000 customers, and is backed by venture investors including Lightspeed Venture Partners. Clark exposes no public developer API or developer portal; it is a consumer-facing insurtech rather than an API producer.

providers.name: Data Sutram
providers.description: Data Sutram is an enterprise AI trust platform for the financial services sector, using external and alternative data intelligence plus agentic workflows to power fraud detection, identity and address verification, credit assessment, and collections. Its products - Trust (fraud and trust scoring), Auth (authentication and verification), and Echo (collections intelligence) - are applied across the customer lifecycle from acquisition and onboarding through portfolio monitoring and debt recovery. Data Sutram serves leading Indian banks and fintechs including HDFC, Axis, ICICI, Kotak, IndusInd, Jupiter, Navi, and Fibe, and maintains ISO 27001, ISO 27018, and SOC 2 certifications along with DPDP compliance. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of Lightspeed Venture Partners and is also backed by B Capital.

providers.name: LendUp
providers.description: LendUp was a San Francisco consumer-lending fintech founded in 2011 and backed by GV and QED Investors, offering single-payment and installment loans to subprime borrowers alongside a gamified "LendUp Ladder" program that promised cheaper credit and credit-bureau reporting as borrowers repaid. LendUp Loans LLC ceased lending operations in January 2022 following Consumer Financial Protection Bureau enforcement actions over misleading marketing and pricing claims. The lendup.com domain is now operated by an unrelated company, LendUp LLC of Dover, Delaware, which runs a consumer loan-matching and financial-education site connecting borrowers to licensed lenders for a referral fee; it states it has no corporate, ownership, or operational relationship to the former lender and no access to its customer data. Neither entity publishes a public API, developer portal, SDKs, or any machine-readable discovery surface.

providers.name: Rogo
providers.description: Rogo is a New York-based artificial intelligence company building an AI platform purpose-built for the world's leading financial institutions. Founded by Gabriel Stengel, John Willett, and Tumas Rackaitis, Rogo serves 300+ institutions and 35,000+ bankers and investors with AI agents that execute end-to-end financial workflows — producing institutional-grade Excel models, investment memos, diligence materials, and slide decks. Its platform (including the Felix assistant) integrates with firm systems (SharePoint, CRM) and financial data providers (LSEG, FactSet, Capital IQ, PitchBook, Preqin, Dow Jones, SEC filings) and is custom-deployed with enterprise-grade, single-tenant security. Customers include Truist Securities, Nomura, and Baird. Rogo raised a $160M Series D led by Kleiner Perkins. Rogo publishes no public developer API, SDKs, or API documentation; this profile captures its identity and published security/compliance posture.

providers.name: Tangelo
providers.description: Tangelo is a Latin American fintech company, surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of QED Investors (a fintech-focused venture firm). Tangelo runs an API-first developer program: it publishes API documentation through a Stoplight-hosted developer portal at docs.tangelolatam.com (workspace "Tangelo Latam Docs") and operates a branded Atlassian status page at status.tangelolatam.com. Its marketing site runs on Webflow. This profile was enriched by live probing of Tangelo's public surfaces; the underlying OpenAPI definition is served behind the Stoplight single-page app and was not machine-extractable in this pass, so spec-derived artifacts (packages, scopes, errors, authentication) remain open for a follow-up once the specification URL is captured.

providers.name: Clearcover
providers.description: Clearcover is a digital-first auto insurance company that offers customizable, affordable car insurance backed by AI-assisted claims that can resolve eligible claims in minutes rather than days. Customers buy and manage policies through a mobile app, file claims by photographing damage, and track claim status in real time, with coverage spanning liability, comprehensive and collision, medical payments, uninsured/underinsured motorist protection, roadside assistance, and alternate transportation. Clearcover operates across multiple US states through several underwriting entities, distributes through both direct and independent-agent channels, and runs a developer portal for partner and embedded insurance integrations. It was surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of 500 Global and enriched from its public web surface.

providers.name: Creditas
providers.description: Creditas is a Brazilian digital lending fintech founded in 2012 and headquartered in Sao Paulo, operating in Brazil and Mexico. It provides secured consumer credit - loans backed by real estate (home equity) and vehicles, plus private payroll (consignado privado) loans - alongside auto insurance, multi-bank real estate and vehicle financing, and a corporate benefits platform (salary advance, flexible-benefits cards, and financial education). Regulated by the Banco Central do Brasil, Creditas has originated over R$12 billion in credit. It is backed by QED Investors and the SoftBank Vision Fund. No public developer API program or OpenAPI has been identified; this profile captures the company public identity, its published llms.txt, and its domain security posture.

providers.name: Eisen
providers.description: Eisen is an AI-enabled compliance operations platform for financial institutions and digital asset companies, managing escheatment (unclaimed property), disbursement, customer outreach, and 1099 tax reporting across all account types. Its product suite includes an Escheatment Manager that tracks state compliance deadlines and dormancy rules, a Disbursement Manager that automates personalized customer payments, an Outreach Manager that re-engages dormant account holders, and a 1099 Reporting Manager for tax reporting. Eisen handles dormant accounts, stale checks, account wind-downs, and forced closures, and is backed by Cowboy Ventures, Homebrew, and Index Ventures. As of this profile Eisen exposes no public developer API, portal, or documentation; this record captures its identity and public web surface.

providers.name: Mr. Cooper Group
providers.description: Mr. Cooper Group (formerly Nationstar Mortgage, NASDAQ: COOP) was a Coppell, Texas-based mortgage servicer with roughly $1.5T in unpaid principal balance under servicing and more than 4 million customers. It was acquired by Rocket Companies (NYSE: RKT) in an all-stock transaction announced March 31, 2025 (initial value $9.4B) and closed October 1, 2025 (final value approximately $14.2B). Mr. Cooper now operates as a Rocket Companies subsidiary; the corporate site mrcoopergroup.com redirects to rocketcompanies.com and the COOP ticker has been delisted. The consumer brand Mr. Cooper continues at mrcooper.com as one of seven Rocket Companies operating businesses (Rocket Mortgage, Redfin, Mr. Cooper, Rocket Homes, Rocket Close, Rocket Money, Rocket Loans). Mr. Cooper does not publish a public developer API or developer portal.

providers.name: National Bank of Canada
providers.description: National Bank of Canada (Banque Nationale du Canada, TSX: NA) is a Schedule I chartered bank headquartered in Montreal, Quebec, founded in 1859. It is the sixth-largest of Canada's Big Six banks and the leading bank in Quebec, serving personal, commercial, wealth-management, and financial-markets clients. On open finance, National Bank is a notable first-mover: it was the first major Canadian bank to launch a secure, consent-based data-sharing API for retail customers, but it does NOT operate a public self-serve first-party developer portal. Programmatic access to customer financial data is delivered through aggregators rather than a downloadable public API — principally Flinks, the Montreal aggregator in which National Bank holds an ~80% stake, via its Open Banking Environment (OBE), and also through Plaid. National Bank and Flinks are founding participants of the FDX Canada working group, aligning their data-sharing on the FDX technical standard, and the bank is positioning ahead of Canada's forthcoming, legislated-but-not-yet-operational Consumer-Driven Banking framework (Budget 2024 / FCAC oversight). Today access is voluntary and aggregator-mediated; there is no operational open-banking mandate and no public first-party API surface.

providers.name: Clearscore
providers.description: ClearScore is a London-founded fintech (2015) that gives consumers free access to their credit score and report and matches them to financial products — credit cards, loans, car finance, insurance and more — through a personalised financial marketplace. It also runs ClearScore Protect (dark-web identity monitoring), DriveScore (driving-behaviour scoring) and Open Banking features, and operates across the UK, South Africa, Australia, Canada and New Zealand. Its B2B arm, ClearScore Connect, exposes credit-data and eligibility services to partner lenders through a partner-gated developer portal (docs.clearscore.com). Backed by QED Investors. This profile was surfaced as a QED portfolio company and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline; ClearScore's developer API is documented behind a password-gated ReadMe.io portal, so no public OpenAPI or machine-readable spec could be captured.

providers.name: Conexus Credit Union
providers.description: Conexus Credit Union is Saskatchewan's largest credit union, a member-owned cooperative financial institution headquartered in Regina with over $10 billion in consolidated assets under management, more than 140,000 members, roughly 30 branches, and over 800 employees across the province. As a provincially regulated Saskatchewan credit union it operates under a cooperative charter, with member deposits guaranteed by the Credit Union Deposit Guarantee Corporation (CUDGC). In November 2024 Conexus announced its intent to explore a merger with Cornerstone and Synergy credit unions. Conexus does not publish a first-party public developer API or a developer portal; developer.conexus.ca does not resolve, and /developer and /api on the corporate site return 404. Consumer financial-data access is provided through third-party aggregators (notably Plaid in Canada) via screen-scraping and connection-based data sharing rather than a first-party API. Digital and online banking are delivered through core-banking and fintech partners (banking.online.conexus.ca), and investing runs through the credit-union system's Aviso Wealth / Qtrade and Thrive Wealth partners. Canada's federal Consumer-Driven Banking (open banking) framework, overseen by the Financial Consumer Agency of Canada (FCAC), is legislated but not yet operational, so Conexus's open-finance access remains voluntary and aggregator-mediated today.

providers.name: FundMiner
providers.description: FundMiner is a fund management and donor stewardship platform for mission-driven organizations, giving universities, healthcare systems, and community foundations one place to manage the full fund lifecycle. It combines fund management with compliance monitoring, impact and donor reporting, and a branded donor portal that gives donors real-time visibility into how their gifts are used. The platform integrates with existing financial systems and offers role-based dashboards and access controls. FundMiner is a Techstars-backed company; it exposes no public developer API, SDK, or API reference at this time, so this profile captures its public identity and web presence.

providers.name: Mission Lane
providers.description: Mission Lane is a consumer fintech founded in 2018 that offers the Mission Lane Visa credit card (issued by WebBank) to help millions of Americans with limited or rebuilding credit gain access to transparent, fair credit. Operating as a remote-first company backed by QED Investors, it combines modern data science and machine-learning underwriting with the discipline of an established financial institution, and partners with Plaid for open-finance connectivity. Mission Lane provides a mobile app and a web account dashboard for cardholders but does not publish a public developer API, OpenAPI specification, or partner API program; its engineering surface (BentoML model services, MLOps tooling) is internal.

providers.name: Pine
providers.description: Pine is a Canadian digital-first mortgage lender and real estate brokerage (Pine Canada Financial Corporation / Pine Real Estate Brokerage) that makes home buying more accessible for Canadians through an online platform offering low interest rates, fast pre-approvals, and zero hidden fees. Backed by Greylock, Pine pairs mortgage origination with a REALTOR-affiliated brokerage licensed across multiple provinces (ON, AB, SK, NS, NB, NL), and reports more than $2B in mortgages funded and 100,000+ clients served. Pine is a consumer fintech product with no public developer API; its backend at api.pine.ca is a private, authenticated service.

providers.name: QPLIX
providers.description: QPLIX GmbH is a Munich-based wealth management software company offering QPLIX-Q, an all-in-one SaaS platform for professional investors, family offices, asset managers, and banks to consolidate, manage, and report on multi-asset-class portfolios. The platform automates portfolio management, trading and rebalancing, accounting, tax, and client reporting, integrating direct data feeds from 150+ custodian banks (UBS, Julius Baer, Deutsche Bank, and others) and leading market-data providers (LSEG, Moody's, S&P Dow Jones Indices, ISS ESG). QPLIX runs a self-hosted, API-based infrastructure on ISO 27001-certified European data centers, holds an ISAE 3402 attestation, and is registered with Germany's BaFin as an account information service provider (AISP). The company does not publish a public developer API or portal; integrations are delivered as managed add-ons and there is no OpenAPI, SDK, or developer documentation surface.

providers.name: Auquan
providers.description: Auquan builds production-grade, autonomous AI agents for institutional finance — agentic systems that convert messy, global, unstructured data (earnings calls, ESG disclosures, filings, news across 2M+ sources in 76 languages) into auditable, decision-ready intelligence and fully-formed deliverables such as credit memos, IC memos, portfolio-monitoring alerts, sustainability reports and LP reporting. Its RAG-powered agents cover 550,000+ companies and entities and complete end-to-end workflows autonomously for banks, asset managers, private credit, insurers and other institutional clients. Founded by Chandini Jain (CEO) and Shub Jain (CTO) with offices in New York and London, Auquan is used by 40% of the top 50 financial institutions (MetLife, T. Rowe Price, BC Partners) and was named a Gartner 2025 Cool Vendor in Agentic AI. The platform is demo/sales-gated and publishes no public self-service API or developer portal.

providers.name: BlockFi
providers.description: BlockFi was a Jersey City, New Jersey crypto-financial-services company founded in 2017 by Zac Prince and Flori Marquez that offered retail and institutional clients interest-bearing crypto accounts (the BlockFi Interest Account), USD loans collateralized by bitcoin and other digital assets, spot trading, and a bitcoin-rewards credit card, growing on a USD 350 million Series D in March 2021 that valued it at roughly USD 3 billion. The company filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection in November 2022 in the wake of the FTX and Alameda Research collapse, and emerged in October 2023 not as an operating business but as a wind-down estate. Its customer web platform and mobile apps have been shut down, in-kind crypto distributions are administered through Coinbase and cash distributions through Kroll Restructuring Administration and Digital Disbursements, and blockfi.com is now a WordPress notice site carrying noindex/nofollow and dated estate updates rather than a product. There is no operating developer program: api.blockfi.com and every other developer, docs and app subdomain no longer resolve in DNS, the company GitHub organization holds zero public repositories, and no OpenAPI, GraphQL, AsyncAPI, MCP or agent-card document is served from any surviving BlockFi host.

providers.name: Equitable
providers.description: Equitable Holdings, Inc. is a financial services holding company offering individual retirement, group retirement, life insurance, and employee benefits solutions. In 2025, Equitable launched API capabilities for benefits plan setup integration, partnering with platforms such as Employee Navigator to streamline broker workflows.

providers.name: Finova Capital
providers.description: Finova Capital is a non-banking financial company (NBFC) licensed by the Reserve Bank of India, founded in 2015 by Mohit Sahney and Sunita Sahney and headquartered in Jaipur, Rajasthan. It provides secured lending to micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) and self-employed customers across India, including MSME business loans, home loans, working capital and machinery loans, and personal loans, all secured against immovable property. Operating across 17 states through 450+ branches, Finova Capital is backed by investors including Peak XV Partners, Norwest Venture Partners, Faering Capital, Maj Invest, Sofina Ventures, Avataar Ventures and Madison India Capital. The company holds a Certificate of Registration issued by the RBI under Section 45-IA of the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934. This is a financial-services provider with a public marketing and investor-relations website; it does not currently expose a public developer API surface.

providers.name: H&R Block
providers.description: H&R Block is a major US corporation and Fortune 1000 company. The H&R Block API provides programmatic access to its platform services, data, and integrations for enterprise customers and partners.

providers.name: HomeFirst
providers.description: HomeFirst (Home First Finance Company India Limited) is an affordable-housing finance company headquartered in Mumbai, India, that provides home loans, self-construction and resale loans, loans against property, shop loans, and renovation/top-up loans to first-time and lower- to middle-income home buyers across India, marketing itself as "India's Home Loan Expert" with approval within 48 hours. It is a technology-led lender operating consumer-facing customer and connector portals and mobile apps, and is a publicly listed company backed by Bessemer Venture Partners. It was surfaced as a Bessemer portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network; it publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, or machine-readable API artifacts at this time, so this profile captures its public web/identity and domain-security posture only.

providers.name: Jacobi
providers.description: Jacobi (Jacobi, Inc.) builds a cloud-native, API-first technology platform for multi-asset portfolio design, analytics and client engagement, used by asset managers, wealth managers and RIAs, asset owners and pension funds, and investment consultants and OCIOs. The platform spans portfolio construction and asset-allocation modeling, risk analysis, a Model Portfolio Management Solution (MPMS) covering the model portfolio lifecycle, custom portfolio solutions, an OCIO solution, and the Jacobi Data Engine, which unifies fragmented investment datasets and automates integration, construction, risk and reporting workflows. Jacobi markets an open-architecture API layer and a Python-based Software Development Kit that let analysts and developers build custom models, automate data processes and connect proprietary systems, market data providers, custodians and risk engines. Each client runs on its own private deployment with data segregation, encryption in transit and at rest, fine-grained permissions, enterprise IAM integration, audit logging and continuous monitoring — so the API and SDK surface is provisioned per tenant and is not publicly documented or self-serve. Founded by investment professionals and technologists, headquartered in San Francisco with offices in London and Brisbane; raised a Series A led by QIC in 2022.

providers.name: Kingsware
providers.description: Kingsware (Zhuhai Kingsware Artificial Intelligence Co., Ltd. / 珠海金智维人工智能股份有限公司) is a leading Chinese enterprise AI and RPA solutions provider that builds "AI digital employees" and enterprise-grade agent platforms by fusing large language models, AI algorithms, and robotic process automation with vertical industry workflows. Its core products are the K-APA intelligent process automation (RPA) platform and the Ki-Agent enterprise agent platform (built around a "Supervised Agent" model with task planning, tool calling, multi-agent collaboration, and result verification), exposed through the Kingsware AI Open Platform (ai.kingsware.cn). The company serves finance, government, manufacturing, energy, telecom, education, HR, and finance/operations use cases; it has been recognized by IDC as the number-one China RPA+AI solution vendor by market share, counts all six major state-owned banks and 1,300+ enterprise/government customers, has deployed over 1.8 million AI digital employees, and is a national-level "little giant" (专精特新) enterprise. Added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of the venture firm Qiming and enriched by the pipeline.

providers.name: Nibbles PBC
providers.description: Nibbles PBC is a public benefit company building consumer financial and insurance products that make pet ownership easier. Its flagship product is the Nibbles credit card, a Mastercard that bundles built-in pet insurance and pet- focused rewards for cardholders. The company operates a consumer web application and account portal at nibbles.com (formerly reached via the nibbl.es short domain) covering sign-up, sign-in, card management, insurance policies, and rewards. Nibbles PBC was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes no developer API, SDK, OpenAPI specification, or developer portal; its public surface is a consumer product site, help center, and legal agreements. This profile therefore captures verified company identity and domain-security posture only.

providers.name: OnCorps AI
providers.description: OnCorps AI is an agentic AI platform for fund operations at financial institutions, automating complex middle- and back-office tasks through AI agents that predict root causes and reduce time and cost. Its products span NAV oversight, investment operations, reconciliation, financial report review, performance verification, security attribution, cash and positions validation, accounting controls, OTC confirmations, and FX/share-class hedging, plus Deep Industry Research Agents (DIRA) for financial transaction analysis. OnCorps serves asset managers and fund administrators including PIMCO and Natixis, and is SOC 1 and ISO 27001 certified. No public API or developer program is currently published; this profile is maintained as a company record in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Paperstack
providers.description: Paperstack is a Canadian fintech operating a private-credit / working-capital financing platform for direct-to-consumer (DTC), e-commerce, and retail consumer brands. It provides non-dilutive, revenue-based funding of up to $5,000,000 that brands can use without restrictions to purchase inventory, invest in advertising, and finance payroll, with transparent flat fees (typically 4-10%) and no origination or late fees. Paperstack couples a network of lending partners with proprietary AI/ML underwriting software that integrates directly into a brand's financial and e-commerce data to assess creditworthiness and project future performance in real time.
