Founded by Assel Beglinova (CEO) and Vadim Lidich (CTO) and backed by Techstars, the company has processed over 1,500 funding applications. As of this enrichment pass Paperstack publishes a customer-facing product and marketing site only; it exposes no public developer API, SDKs, or developer documentation.

providers.name: QueroQuitar
providers.description: QueroQuitar is a Brazilian fintech platform that helps consumers and businesses renegotiate and settle overdue debts online. Through its web and mobile apps it connects users with 50+ creditors (including Santander, Claro, Sky, BV, Inter and Carrefour) to arrange discounted, installment-based payoffs, and participates in Brazil's Desenrola Brasil program. It also offers QueroCredito credit products and QueroSaude health services. It is a portfolio company of 500 Global. As of this enrichment pass QueroQuitar exposes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface.

providers.name: Setpoint.io
providers.description: Setpoint is a capital markets operating system for asset-backed finance. It embeds with borrowers and lenders to manage debt facilities — warehouse facilities, forward flow agreements, securitization, and fund/leverage finance — automating collateral verification, data standardization, and reporting across ABS and ABF markets. The platform (Capital OS and Data OS, plus PledgeCheck collateral certification and Setpoint Analytics) manages over $50 billion in financed assets annually. Setpoint is not currently a public API provider; this profile captures the company's identity and public web surface for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Silent Eight
providers.description: Silent Eight is an AI-driven financial crime compliance (FCC) technology company founded in Singapore in 2015 and operating globally. Its flagship platform, Iris 7, delivers policy-bound agentic AI that replicates the investigative judgement of experienced compliance analysts, executing explainable, auditable decisions across sanctions screening, anti-money laundering, transaction monitoring, fraud, trade surveillance and complex customer due diligence. Iris 7 is composed of AI Agents by capability (Customer Screening, Payment Screening, Transaction Monitoring, Risk Data Manager, Adverse Media, Case Manager) plus pre-built and custom agents, and is deployed as a governed decision layer on top of existing screening and monitoring systems via managed service, customer cloud, hybrid or on-premise infrastructure. In production with Tier 1 institutions since 2018, including HSBC, Standard Chartered, Emirates NBD and First Abu Dhabi Bank. Silent Eight publishes no public developer program: the platform is delivered under enterprise contract and integrated into each institution's tenant, so no machine-readable API contract is published to the open web.

providers.name: SmartAsset
providers.description: SmartAsset is a financial technology company that runs the largest online marketplace connecting consumers with fiduciary financial advisors. Its SmartAdvisor matching service pairs more than 50,000 retail investors each month with up to three vetted advisors based on geography, investable assets, and preferences, while the SmartAsset Advisor Marketing Platform (AMP) delivers advisors a subscription stream of qualified referrals plus lead automation that syncs into their CRMs (Salesforce, HubSpot, Wealthbox, Redtail, Zoho, Pipedrive, SmartOffice). SmartAsset also publishes a large library of consumer personal-finance calculators and editorial content across taxes, retirement, mortgages, investing, and banking. Backed by a16z and Y Combinator, SmartAsset is a lead-generation and media business and does not currently expose a public developer API.

providers.name: T2P
providers.description: T2P Co., Ltd. (DeepPocket) is a Bangkok, Thailand fintech founded in 2011 that provides comprehensive payment solutions for enterprises of all sizes. Its products include a payment gateway (cards, mobile wallets, in-store), a white-label digital wallet platform, corporate and prepaid card issuance, spend management with real-time controls, business escrow, the DeepBlok loyalty program, and the DeepPocket consumer e-wallet app for top-ups, payments, and global money transfers. T2P is backed by 500 Global, Benchachinda Holding, DTAC Accelerate, and J Ventures, and reports serving 10M+ customers and 30+ corporate clients. T2P holds PCI DSS compliance but publishes no public developer API surface; integrations are arranged directly with the company.

providers.name: Truehold
providers.description: Truehold is a St. Louis, Missouri-founded residential real estate company that buys homes from owners and rents them back to those same owners through a residential sale-leaseback, letting a homeowner convert home equity into cash without moving. Launched in 2021, the company expanded across the Midwest and into the South and Southwest, and in 2025 added Truehold Financial, a Jacksonville, Florida-based lending arm offering DSCR loans, fix-and-flip financing and other investor lending products. Truehold also transacts portfolio sales and multifamily sales with real estate investors. Its public surface is a marketing and lead-generation website plus two authenticated web applications for customers and borrowers; it publishes no developer program, no API documentation and no machine-readable API contract.

providers.name: TrustIQ
providers.description: TrustIQ (operating as Trusting Social) is a Singapore-headquartered AI fintech that provides alternative-data credit scoring, fraud detection, and digital identity verification for lenders and consumer platforms across emerging Asian markets including India, Indonesia, Vietnam, and the Philippines. Its products — Trust Scores (AI credit and fraud scoring built from telco and alternative data), Trust Vision (facial-recognition digital onboarding and KYC), and Smart Customer Acquisition — help financial institutions extend credit to underbanked, new-to-credit consumers. Engagement is sales-led; the company publishes no public self-service API, SDK, or developer portal.

providers.name: Webster Bank
providers.description: Webster Bank, N.A. is a nationally chartered commercial bank (National Association) and the principal banking subsidiary of Webster Financial Corporation (NYSE: WBS), a Delaware-incorporated bank and financial holding company headquartered in Stamford, Connecticut. A values-based super-regional institution with roughly $84 billion in assets, Webster serves businesses, individuals, and families across the Northeast from the New York City metro area through Connecticut, Rhode Island, and Massachusetts, and operates the HSA Bank division, a leading national provider of health savings accounts and consumer-directed benefit administration in all 50 states. Webster does not publish a first-party public developer portal or downloadable API specifications. Its open-finance posture is consumer- and commercial-permissioned data sharing delivered through aggregators rather than a direct API: in June 2026 Webster went live on Prolific Banking's FI-Streams Connector using Plaid's FDX-aligned Core Exchange specification to give commercial clients secure, tokenized connectivity to the Plaid network, and consumer account data is also reachable via Plaid and Finicity. There is no publicly documented first-party REST API, OpenAPI/Swagger definition, or self-serve developer program.

providers.name: Kickpay
providers.description: Kickpay is an intelligent finance platform for e-commerce and hardware brands that unlocks capital tied up in inventory. It plugs into a company's data sources — fulfillment centers, e-commerce sales channels, and bank accounts — to see historic sales, then finances the manufacturing cost of each SKU it estimates will sell within a reasonable window (typically around 16 weeks). Kickpay can fund the brand directly or pay the manufacturer to purchase more inventory, and the brand only pays Kickpay back as units ship: when a unit ships from the fulfillment center, Kickpay activates an ACH payment for the manufacturing price plus a fixed fee. It provides smart daily servicing and reporting, distinguishes customer shipments from internal stock movements, and uses prediction tooling to forecast future sales and cash flow so it can underwrite startups with as little as three months of sales history. Kickpay was backed by Canaan Partners and DCVC. This profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network; Kickpay publishes no public developer API, documentation, or SDKs, and the enrichment pipeline found no machine-readable API surface.

providers.name: Mooncard
providers.description: Mooncard is a French corporate expense-management platform that pairs a smart payment card, a mobile app, and accounting-automation software so finance teams can handle business spending end to end without manual data entry. It automates expense reports, VAT recovery, and mileage and per-diem calculations, then syncs transactions into accounting systems such as Sage, Cegid, SAP, Microsoft Dynamics, Exact Online, and Agicap. Mooncard also runs a developer program that offers API access plus a sandbox environment, though the API reference and OpenAPI are gated behind a developer-portal login and are not publicly discoverable.

providers.name: SunGard Data Systems
providers.description: SunGard Data Systems was a software and technology services company that provided software and processing solutions to financial services, education, and the public sector. In November 2015, SunGard was acquired by Fidelity National Information Services (FIS) for approximately $9.1 billion. Key product lines included SunGard Financial Systems (trading, treasury, risk management, capital markets), SunGard AvantGard (cash and liquidity management), SunGard K-12 (student information systems), and SunGard Higher Education (ERP for universities). Post-acquisition, these products were integrated into the FIS portfolio.

providers.name: Can Capital
providers.description: CAN Capital is a small business financing company that provides short-term working capital loans, equipment financing, and ecommerce loans to small business owners across the United States. One of the earliest alternative small-business lenders, the company has facilitated more than 190,000 funding transactions totaling over $8 billion in working capital, underwriting on business performance and daily/weekly revenue rather than traditional credit criteria. Borrowers apply online, receive fast funding decisions, and manage their accounts through a self-service client portal. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Accel and profiled in the API Evangelist network; CAN Capital publishes a marketing site, application flow, and customer portal but no public developer API or discovery surface at this time.

providers.name: EDUFI PTE. LTD
providers.description: EduFi (EDUFI PTE. LTD) is a Singapore-incorporated education-financing fintech operating Pakistan's first Study Now, Pay Later (SNPL) digital platform, with expansion into Saudi Arabia and Oman. The Shariah-approved platform lets parents and students finance private schooling, higher education, and international student loans through quick, collateral-free approvals with direct disbursement to educational institutes and convenient monthly installments. EduFi also provides partner educational institutes a free ERP system and subsidized SNPL for their students, and works with financial institutions to fund receivables. Backed by 500 Global. This profile is maintained by API Evangelist; EduFi publishes a consumer marketing and application surface but no public developer/API program.

providers.name: Evertas
providers.description: Evertas is a digital-asset insurance underwriter and the first company dedicated exclusively to crypto insurance. Founded in 2017 as BlockRe by J. Gdanski and Raymond Zenkich and rebranded to Evertas in 2020, it underwrites cryptocurrency mining and AI-infrastructure hardware property, platform failure, crime/theft/loss, insider theft/loss, digital property, and directors-and-officers risk. Products are underwritten by certain underwriters at Lloyd's of London and other insurers, carry AM Best and Standard & Poor's creditworthiness ratings, and offer coverage limits up to $600 million per declaration. Policies are distributed exclusively through appointed brokers. Evertas operates a marketing and content site plus an email-gated broker document-upload portal; it publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK, or machine-readable specification.

providers.name: Getsafe
providers.description: Getsafe (Getsafe Digital GmbH) is a Heidelberg, Germany-based digital insurance company (insurtech) that lets consumers buy, manage, and file claims for insurance entirely through a mobile app. Getsafe operates as a licensed insurance carrier and offers 15+ products across liability and legal protection, health (public, private, dental, and travel), living (contents and drone), pet (pet health and dog liability), and protection and finance (income protection, term life, private pension, and children's savings). It serves 500k+ customers in Germany and Austria with English-language, app-based support. In 2018 Getsafe launched an early-access P&C and health insurance API and embeddable widget for partner distribution; that partner API is no longer offered as a public self-service developer program, so this profile is maintained as a company record. Backed by earlybird and partech.

providers.name: Gojo & Company
providers.description: Gojo & Company, Inc. is a Tokyo-headquartered financial inclusion holding company founded on 4 July 2014 by Taejun Shin and Sanjay Gandhi, with the stated ambition of becoming a "private-sector World Bank". Gojo raises capital from mission-aligned investors and deploys it into microfinance institutions and inclusive financial service providers across South Asia, Southeast Asia, Central Asia, the Caucasus and Africa, supplying not only equity and debt but also management, governance, risk and technology support to its group companies. It runs a Financial Diaries research programme on low-income household cashflows, the Pasio digital financial inclusion initiative, and a non-profit arm, the Gojo Foundation. Gojo is a certified B Corporation and reports under J-GAAP. It is a private company; its equity trades on secondary marketplaces such as Hiive. Gojo publishes no public developer program, API documentation, or machine-readable API contract — its digital financial infrastructure and cloud core banking work is internal to the group and its partner institutions.

providers.name: Noodle
providers.description: Noodle is a Brazilian fintech building financial infrastructure for the creator economy. It provides automated payouts to creators, influencers, and vendors; FastPay early access to future earnings; noodleOS, a unified platform for campaigns, creator data, payments, and asset tracking; global payouts powered by Ebanx; foreign-exchange settlement; and credit and capital products underwritten in part on a creator's social presence. Backed by QED Investors, Noodle serves media companies, agencies, and platforms that pay content creators. The company references API-based integrations but publishes no public developer portal or API documentation.

providers.name: Onafriq
providers.description: Onafriq (formerly MFS Africa) is a pan-African digital payments network headquartered in London with operating entities across Mauritius, Ghana, Nigeria, Tanzania, Rwanda, Uganda, the DRC, and the UK. Founded by CEO Dare Okoudjou, Onafriq operates what it calls "Africa's largest digital payments gateway" — a network of networks connecting roughly one billion mobile money wallets and 500 million bank accounts across 40+ African countries through 2,000+ cross-border corridors. The platform exposes a REST API surface for partners including Money Transfer Organizations (MTOs), Mobile Network Operators (MNOs), banks, NGOs, governments, and enterprises. Core developer products include Async Payouts (the recommended path for MTOs and bulk disbursement partners, with webhook-based status updates), Sync Payouts (custom-built for MNOs requiring synchronous responses), Sync Bank Transfers, Collections APIs (Payins) for receiving funds from cards, cash agents, and mobile wallets, a Contacts API for managing payer/payee records, a Get Rates API for daily foreign exchange rates, and Async Webhooks for Instant Payment Notifications. Two distinct portal endpoints serve domestic (api.mfsafrica.com/api) and cross-border (mfsafrica.beyonicpartners.com/api) workloads. Beyond cross-border remittance and disbursement, Onafriq operates Baxi — a Nigerian agent banking network of 460,000+ agents across all 36 states with its own Virtual Account, Fingerprint, and Account Debit APIs — plus card issuance and processing for physical/virtual prepaid programs and multi-currency treasury services. Onafriq has raised $200M+ in Series C funding from Vitruvian Partners, AXA Investment Managers, and Goodwell, and holds 16 payment licenses including FSC (Mauritius) and FCA (UK) authorization. The legacy MFS Africa developer hub (developer.mfsafrica.com) remains the canonical reference documentation, with a newer developers.onafriq.com portal reflecting the post-rebrand identity.

providers.name: StanCorp Financial Group
providers.description: StanCorp Financial Group, Inc. (doing business as The Standard) is an insurance and financial services company headquartered in Portland, Oregon, and a wholly-owned subsidiary of Meiji Yasuda Life Insurance Company since 2016. Founded in 1906, The Standard offers group and individual disability insurance, group life and accidental death and dismemberment insurance, group dental and group vision insurance, absence management services, retirement plans, individual annuities, and commercial mortgage loan origination. The Standard does not offer a public developer API. Employer and benefits administrator integrations are managed through EDI and proprietary data exchange channels.

providers.name: UBS
providers.description: A Swiss multinational investment bank and financial services company and the world's largest wealth manager. UBS exposes a multi-ecosystem developer platform at developer.ubs.com covering retail banking, mortgages, QR billing, EU PSD2 open banking, Swiss TWINT payments, corporate bLink connectivity, and the enterprise UBS Partner / KeyPort offering.

providers.name: Atlantic Union Bank
providers.description: Atlantic Union Bank is a Virginia state-chartered commercial bank with roots going back to 1902, and the principal banking subsidiary of Atlantic Union Bankshares Corporation (NYSE: AUB), a Richmond, Virginia bank holding company regulated under the Bank Holding Company Act of 1956. It is the largest regional bank headquartered in Virginia, with roughly $37 billion in assets and a branch network across Virginia, Maryland, and North Carolina, offering consumer and business checking, savings, lending, mortgages, credit cards, and wealth management. Like most US regional banks, Atlantic Union Bank operates under the voluntary, fragmented US open-finance landscape rather than a mandated open-banking regime: it publishes no first-party public developer portal or documented public API. Consumer-permissioned account and transaction data is reached indirectly through third-party data aggregators (Plaid, Finicity by Mastercard, MX, Teller) as surfaced by aggregator coverage directories, and no direct FDX-conformant data-access endpoint, Akoya participation, or published CFPB Section 1033 posture was found. This is an identity-only, aggregator-only record with no first-party API surface.

providers.name: Zeta
providers.description: Zeta is a next-generation banking and payment card processing platform for banks and financial institutions, offering a cloud-native omnistack to launch and manage credit, debit, prepaid, BNPL, and fleet card programs alongside loans and deposits. Its product suite spans Tachyon (core processing and real-time APIs and events), Neutrino (digital app experiences), Elena (conversational AI), Saturn (servicing and back-office operations), Luminos (engagement and rewards), and Zeus (data and analytics). Founded by Bhavin Turakhia and Ramki Gaddipati and backed by SoftBank Vision Fund, Zeta processes 25+ million cards across seven countries for institutions including HDFC Bank, Pluxee, and Sparrow. Zeta's platform is delivered to enterprise banking partners; its APIs are partner-gated rather than published on a public developer portal.

providers.name: Capitolis
providers.description: Capitolis is a financial technology company for the capital markets that helps banks and institutional investors optimize how capital is used across their trading portfolios. Its two flagship offerings are a Capital Marketplace that connects banks with origination capabilities to institutional providers of capital, and a Portfolio Optimization service that offsets redundant and offsetting derivatives positions to reduce capital requirements, counterparty exposure, and systemic risk. By combining technology with financial expertise, Capitolis aims to create a safer, more efficient financial system and broaden access to more diversified pools of capital. The platform is delivered as a secure, login-gated web application to regulated financial institutions rather than as a public developer API.

providers.name: CIBC
providers.description: Canadian Imperial Bank of Commerce (CIBC) is a Schedule I domestic chartered bank and one of Canada's Big Six, formed in 1961 through the merger of the Canadian Bank of Commerce and the Imperial Bank of Canada and headquartered in Toronto, Ontario. Serving roughly eleven million personal, business, commercial, wealth, and capital-markets clients across Personal & Business Banking, Wealth Management, and Capital Markets, CIBC is a participant in the shared Canadian rails, including Interac e-Transfer and Payments Canada settlement systems. Canada has no operational open-banking mandate today: the federal Consumer-Driven Banking framework legislated in Budget 2024 and the 2024 Fall Economic Statement, overseen by the Financial Consumer Agency of Canada (FCAC), is not yet live, so access remains voluntary and fragmented. CIBC runs no first-party public developer portal (developer.cibc.com does not resolve) and publishes no downloadable OpenAPI or Swagger specifications. Consumer-permissioned data access is aggregator-mediated: CIBC signed a tokenized data-access agreement with U.S. aggregator MX (announced August 2022, MX's first in Canada) to let clients share financial data with third-party apps without exposing banking credentials, and its accounts are also reachable through Plaid (Assets, Auth, Balance). Corporate connectivity is offered through CIBC SWIFT Corporate Access (SCA) file exchange rather than a public REST API, so CIBC's honest public API surface today is aggregator-mediated only, pending the coming Consumer-Driven Banking regime.

providers.name: Clair
providers.description: Clair Inc is a New York-based financial technology company that provides free, compliant On-Demand Pay (earned wage access) as an embedded service inside the payroll, time-and-attendance and workforce-management platforms employees already use. Rather than selling a consumer app, Clair partners with platforms — Gusto Embedded Payroll, Check, 7shifts and others — and connects to them over a partner REST API that transmits employee, employment and attendance data, which Clair's underwriting engine uses to originate 0% APR earned wage advances through its FDIC-insured partner bank, Pathward N.A. Partners embed a Clair-hosted user experience (a WebView component, distributed for iOS as Swift packages) so employees can take an advance, review history and handle loan servicing without a separate login. Clair has raised roughly $218M in total capital, including a $23.2M Series B in May 2025.

providers.name: Finda
providers.description: Finda (핀다) is a South Korean fintech company founded in 2015 and headquartered in Seoul that operates a licensed online loan-comparison and financial-product marketplace. Through its mobile app and website, Finda lets consumers compare loan products from 76+ financial institutions and 400+ products in about a minute, refinance existing loans ("갈아타기"), aggregate accounts and cards for asset management, run financial calculators (interest, DSR, year-end tax, mortgage eligibility), and monitor and manage their credit. Registered as a loan-brokerage/loan-collection corporation under Korea's Financial Services Act, Finda earns commissions from partner financial institutions rather than charging consumers. It reports 3.47M+ cumulative members and 256T+ won in managed loan assets, and is backed by 500 Global. Finda is a consumer B2C platform and does not publish a public developer API.

providers.name: Flow48
providers.description: Flow48 is an SME financing platform founded in March 2022 and backed by Speedinvest that provides non-dilutive, collateral-free capital to small and medium businesses across the GCC and wider MENA region, with a focus on the e-commerce and food & beverage sectors. Its two core products are revenue-based financing, which converts a business's future revenues into upfront capital repaid as a share of sales, and invoice financing, which accelerates cash locked in unpaid invoices. Flow48 markets funding decisions and disbursement within 24 to 48 hours with flexible repayment and no equity surrender. The company operates a self-service borrower onboarding portal but does not currently publish a public developer program, API reference, or SDKs.

providers.name: GrowXCD
providers.description: GrowXCD (GrowXCD Finance Private Limited) is an RBI-registered Non-Banking Financial Company (NBFC) headquartered in Chennai, India, focused on accelerating business growth for the small businesses and self-employed customers that form the backbone of India's economy. Its lending products include Grow Shubam small-ticket mortgage loans, Loan Against Property (LAP) secured lending, and unsecured loans up to Rs 25 lakh with tenures of 12 to 60 months, delivered through a minimal-documentation digital process with swift approvals and repayment via eMandate or NACH auto-debit. GrowXCD is a portfolio company of Prosus Ventures. It publishes a consumer website and statutory policy documents but does not currently expose a public developer portal, API, or SDKs.

providers.name: Kennek
providers.description: Kennek (Kennek Solutions Ltd) is a UK-based fintech providing all-in-one loan management software built for specialist bridge and development lenders. The platform lets lenders originate, manage, and service loans while monitoring funding lines in one place, automating manual workflows, covenant and eligibility calculations, portfolio risk visibility, and investor reporting so lending teams can scale without adding headcount. Founded by former lenders and backed by HV Capital, Kennek is surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a fintech portfolio-company profile; it publishes a marketing site and legal pages but no public developer portal, API documentation, or SDKs at this time.

providers.name: Noble
providers.description: Noble (operated by Benga Inc.) is a no-code risk and credit decisioning platform that provides risk infrastructure for the full customer lifecycle. Fintech companies, lenders, and banks use Noble to verify customer identity, aggregate and assess credit and financial-health data from multiple sources, build and launch automated underwriting and decisioning workflows with a no-code Workflow Builder, and monitor customer behavior and creditworthiness over time. Noble exposes this capability as a SaaS platform, an API, and an embeddable widget, plus pre-built data-partner integrations, so teams can build, launch, and scale digital financial products faster. Founded in 2021 and based in San Mateo, California, Noble is a Y Combinator company backed by Insight Partners, Paradigm, and Polychain.

providers.name: Rupeek
providers.description: Rupeek is an asset-backed online gold loan company operating across India, enabling customers to borrow money by pledging gold jewelry as collateral. Its products include gold loans (from around 30,000 up to 1.5 crore rupees), gold loan balance transfers, the Rupeek Gold Card, part/full gold release, and an online repayment portal. The company partners with banks such as Federal Bank, Indian Bank, and South Indian Bank, offers 100% insurance coverage via New India Assurance, and delivers its consumer experience primarily through its website and highly-rated mobile app. It is ISO 27001 certified. Rupeek is a consumer fintech surfaced as a portfolio company of Accel and GGV Capital; it publishes no public developer API surface, so this profile is an identity-only company record.

providers.name: Bridgewater Bank
providers.description: Bridgewater Bank is a Canadian Schedule I chartered bank, a wholly-owned subsidiary of the Alberta Motor Association (AMA), headquartered in Calgary, Alberta and established in 1997. It is a member of the Canada Deposit Insurance Corporation (CDIC) and operates a broker-distributed, deposit-and-lending model rather than a direct-to-consumer retail branch network — residential mortgages, Guaranteed Investment Certificates (GICs), and high-interest savings accounts sold through a select network of trusted mortgage and deposit brokers, with roughly $3.3 billion in mortgages and deposits across approximately 53,000 customer accounts nationwide. Bridgewater Bank exposes NO public first-party developer API or developer portal. Its only dedicated digital surface beyond the corporate site is a partner-gated broker information portal (bwbbrokerinfo.ca). Canada's Consumer-Driven Banking (open-banking) framework is legislated but not yet operational, so any consumer data access from a bank of this size is voluntary and today would be aggregator/screen-scraping based rather than through a documented first-party API. No Interac, Real-Time Rail (RTR), FDX, or consumer-driven-banking API participation is publicly documented by the institution.

providers.name: Citibank Canada
providers.description: Citibank Canada (Citi Canada) is the Canadian arm of Citigroup, chartered under Canada's Bank Act as a Schedule II (foreign bank subsidiary) deposit-taking institution, established in 1919 in Toronto and headquartered at Citigroup Place, 123 Front Street West. It is a member of the Canadian Bankers Association and the Canada Deposit Insurance Corporation (CDIC). Citi Canada is an institutional and corporate bank only — securities trading, cash management, treasury, trade finance, custody, clearing, securities financing and private banking — having exited Canadian consumer retail banking years ago (its MasterCard portfolio was sold to CIBC in 2010 and CitiFinancial Canada, now Fairstone, was divested in 2017). It runs no Canada-specific developer portal; its corporate and institutional clients integrate through Citigroup's group-level Citi Developer Experience and CitiConnect API platform for payments, statements/reporting, balance inquiry and FX. Canada has no operational open-banking mandate — the federal Consumer-Driven Banking framework (Budget 2024 / FES 2024, overseen by the FCAC) is legislated but not yet live — and because Citi Canada holds no retail consumer accounts here, consumer data-aggregation access is not applicable to this entity.

providers.name: KreditBee
providers.description: KreditBee is a Bengaluru, India digital lending platform founded in 2017 by Madhusudan Ekambaram, Vivek Veda and Karthikeyan Krishnaswamy, operated by Finnovation Tech Solutions Private Limited (CIN U74900KA2016PTC086953) and lending through its in-house RBI-registered NBFC KrazyBee Services Limited alongside partner banks and NBFCs. Its consumer products are instant personal loans from Rs 6,000 to Rs 10 lakh, business loans up to Rs 1 crore, two-wheeler loans up to Rs 5 lakh, loan against property, a flexi personal loan line, 24K digital gold, and free credit score reports, delivered through an Android and iOS app and a single-page web application that the company says serves over 7 crore registered Indian users. KreditBee publishes no public developer portal, no API documentation, no API reference, no SDKs and no machine-readable API description of any kind. Its only API host, api.kreditbee.in, is an AWS API Gateway behind Cloudflare that answers HTTP 403 ForbiddenException to every anonymous request and exists to serve the company's own mobile and web clients. Partner and lending-partner integrations are transacted through the /partner-with-us and /digital-lending-partners business pages rather than through any self-serve technical surface.

providers.name: PNC
providers.description: PNC Financial Services Group is a Pittsburgh-based money-center bank and Fortune 500 diversified financial services company offering retail banking, corporate and institutional banking, treasury management, asset management, and residential mortgage banking across the United States. PNC operates a real first-party developer portal at developer.pnc.com ("PNC Developer Tools: Open APIs for Banking & Payments") that publishes a catalog of treasury and payments API products — including Account Verification Services, ePayments, Real-Time Payments (RTP), Direct-to-Debit-Card (push-to-card) disbursement, and information reporting — surfaced through its PINACLE commercial banking platform and PINACLE Connect embedded-banking integrations. Full API reference documentation, sandbox/testing environments, and call codes are gated behind credentialed onboarding arranged through a PNC Relationship Manager or Treasury Management Officer; no OpenAPI/Swagger specifications are publicly downloadable. On the consumer open-finance side, PNC exposes account data through an Akoya-provided tokenized data-access API and signed a bilateral data-access agreement with Plaid in September 2024, positioning PNC ahead of CFPB Section 1033 personal-financial-data-rights requirements.

providers.name: Policygenius
providers.description: Policygenius is an independent online insurance marketplace and licensed brokerage founded in 2014 by Jennifer Fitzgerald and Francois de Lame and headquartered in New York City. The platform lets consumers compare quotes, get unbiased expert advice, and buy life, disability, homeowners, auto, and renters insurance across dozens of carriers, and it operates Policygenius Pro, a turnkey life-insurance fulfillment platform for financial advisors, agents, banks, and credit unions. Policygenius was acquired by Zinnia (an Eldridge company) in 2023. It was surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Norwest Venture Partners. As of this enrichment pass Policygenius publishes no public developer API, developer portal, or SDK; its GitHub organization hosts internal tooling and forks only.

providers.name: PrecisionLender
providers.description: PrecisionLender is a relationship pricing and profitability platform for commercial banks, now part of Q2 Holdings (acquired 2019). It equips relationship managers, treasury officers, and credit teams to price and structure optimal commercial deals with total relationship visibility, in-deal collaboration, and "Andi", an AI coaching engine that surfaces in-the-moment pricing guidance. The product draws market-competitive intelligence from 150+ financial institutions and integrates into a bank's technology stack to reduce manual data entry. The standalone precisionlender.com site now redirects to the Q2 "Relationship Pricing and Profitability" product; there is no independent public PrecisionLender API, and Q2's developer surface (Q2 Innovation Studio) requires authentication.

providers.name: Simplii Financial
providers.description: Simplii Financial is the no-fee direct banking brand of the Canadian Imperial Bank of Commerce (CIBC), one of Canada's Big Six Schedule I domestic banks. Launched November 1, 2017, Simplii succeeded CIBC's two-decade President's Choice Financial (PC Financial) co-venture with Loblaws, migrating roughly two million accounts to the new brand. Simplii is not a separately chartered bank; it operates as a division and trade name of CIBC under CIBC's Schedule I federal charter, offering no-fee daily chequing and savings, mortgages, personal loans, lines of credit, GICs, mutual funds, and USD accounts through online, mobile, and telephone channels only (no branches), with CDIC deposit insurance provided through CIBC. On open finance, Simplii exposes no first-party public developer API or developer portal; consumer financial-data access today is aggregator- and screen-scraping-based via Plaid, Finicity, and MX (CIBC signed a data-access agreement with MX), consistent with Canada's voluntary, pre-mandate posture while the federal Consumer-Driven Banking framework (Budget 2024 / FES 2024, overseen by the FCAC) is legislated but not yet operational.

providers.name: Vestwell
providers.description: Vestwell is a New York City-based digital savings and retirement platform (founded 2016) that powers workplace savings programs for employers, financial advisors, financial institutions, TPAs, PEOs, payroll and benefit partners, and government agencies. Its recordkeeping and administration engine supports traditional and Safe Harbor 401(k), Solo-k, Starter-k, pooled/PEP plans, 403(b), 529 education savings, ABLE, emergency savings, student-loan repayment, and tuition reimbursement, as well as state-facilitated ("government savings") retirement programs. Vestwell emphasizes payroll and HR integrations (auto-sync across 190+ payroll providers) rather than a public developer API; onboarding, servicing, and saver access run through its web platform. Surfaced as a Lightspeed Venture Partners portfolio company and profiled here for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Affinity Credit Union
providers.description: Affinity Credit Union is a member-owned financial cooperative headquartered in Saskatoon, Saskatchewan, Canada. Formed in 2005 through the amalgamation of several Saskatchewan credit unions, it is the largest credit union in Saskatchewan and among the ten largest in Canada, with roughly CAD 9.6 billion in managed assets and a province-wide branch and advice-centre network serving personal and business members. As a provincially regulated cooperative under its "Banking on Values" mandate, members democratically own and govern the institution. Affinity exposes NO first-party public developer API or developer portal; digital and core banking are delivered through banking-technology providers (the credit-union system's Central 1 rails), and third-party consumer data access today is aggregator/screen-scraping based. Affinity is a stated supporter of the credit-union-system "Open Banking Solution" delivered by Caspian One under the Large Credit Union Coalition, positioning it for Canada's legislated-but-not-yet-operational Consumer-Driven Banking framework (FCAC).

providers.name: Deutsche Bank
providers.description: Deutsche Bank is a global financial institution that offers a wide range of banking services to individuals, businesses, and institutions. The bank provides services such as retail banking, investment banking, asset management, and wealth management. Deutsche Bank is known for its expertise in international markets and has a strong presence in Europe, the Americas, and Asia. The Deutsche Bank Developer Portal publishes Open Banking and Beyond-PSD2 APIs for partners and developers.

providers.name: Frost Bank
providers.description: Frost Bank is the banking subsidiary of Cullen/Frost Bankers, Inc. (NYSE: CFR), a San Antonio, Texas-based financial holding company and one of the largest Texas-headquartered banks. Founded in 1868, Frost operates as a Texas state-chartered commercial bank (regulated by the Texas Department of Banking and the Federal Reserve after converting from a national charter to a state charter in 2012), serving consumer, commercial, wealth-management, and insurance customers through financial centers across Texas. On open finance, Frost runs NO first-party public developer portal or documented public API: the host developer.frostbank.com does not resolve and no developers/API page exists on frostbank.com. Consumer-permissioned account and transaction data is made available only through third-party aggregators — Frost's own digital banking uses Plaid for account aggregation — rather than a direct API. Frost publishes no FDX (Financial Data Exchange) participation and no stated CFPB Section 1033 data-access posture. This is an honest identity-only record for a regional US bank whose external data access is aggregator-mediated.

providers.name: LearnVest
providers.description: LearnVest was a New York personal-finance company founded in 2009 by Alexa von Tobel and backed by Accel, selling subscription financial planning that paired consumers with CFP professionals alongside budgeting, spending-tracking and goal tools. Northwestern Mutual acquired LearnVest in 2015 for a reported $250 million and terminated the subscription planning service on June 5, 2018, closing all client accounts. The brand was relaunched as a consumer financial-education content site, and learnvest.com today is an archived article library on budgeting, saving, paying off debt and career growth, operated under the Northwestern Mutual brand. LearnVest never published a public API, developer portal, SDK or sandbox, and no developer surface exists today.

providers.name: Levocred AI
providers.description: Levocred AI builds an AI operating system for structured credit operations, serving both credit funds (lenders) and loan originators from a single platform. Its product, Levo, ingests loan tapes, credit agreements, servicer reports and bank feeds, then automates analytical work a credit team would otherwise do by hand: generating lender-ready borrowing base reports, monitoring covenants for breaches in real time rather than at month-end, drafting credit analyses and investment committee memos, assembling lender packages, consolidating treasury and cash visibility across facilities, and maintaining a centralized facility workspace as a single source of truth. The company is a Y Combinator Summer 2026 company based in San Francisco and reports monitoring $500M in capital across 10+ facilities. As of this profile Levocred publishes no public API, developer portal, or API documentation; the product is delivered as a hosted web application.

providers.name: Bank OZK
providers.description: Bank OZK is a regional bank headquartered in Little Rock, Arkansas, tracing its charter to 1903 and today operating roughly 265 offices across Arkansas, Georgia, Florida, North Carolina, Texas, and New York. It is a state-chartered commercial bank and the wholly owned subsidiary of Bank OZK holding company, publicly traded on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under the symbol OZK, with about $40.8 billion in total assets as of year-end 2025 and a national reputation in commercial real estate lending. Bank OZK runs no first-party public developer portal and publishes no downloadable OpenAPI/Swagger specifications; it is not a documented Financial Data Exchange (FDX) participant and has not published a specific CFPB Section 1033 data-access posture. Consumer-permissioned account data is reached only indirectly through third-party aggregators, with Plaid documented as the supporting aggregator. This is an honest identity-only profile with no public API surface.

providers.name: BECU
providers.description: BECU (Boeing Employees' Credit Union) is a member-owned, not-for-profit state-chartered credit union founded in 1935 and headquartered in Tukwila, Washington (NMLS ID 490518). Originally serving Boeing employees, it is today one of the largest credit unions in the United States, offering consumer and business deposit accounts, lending, mortgages, and investment services across the Pacific Northwest and nationally through digital channels. Like the vast majority of US credit unions, BECU exposes no public first-party developer API or developer portal; its digital banking runs on established core and fintech vendors (FIS, LPL/Client Point, ICE/Ellie Mae for mortgage), and consumer-permissioned data access for third-party fintech apps is intermediated through data aggregators rather than a documented, self-serve BECU API. US open finance is voluntary and fragmented, and no mandated open-banking API contract applies here; the CFPB Section 1033 Personal Financial Data Rights rule is the emerging framework that will shape BECU's future data-access posture.

providers.name: Joko
providers.description: Joko is a French fintech company operating a consumer cashback, rewards, and savings application that connects shoppers with more than 3,500 partner brands online and in physical stores. Users earn cashback and automatically apply promo codes through the Joko iOS and Android apps and browser extensions (Chrome, Firefox, Safari), while also managing budgets, loyalty cards, gift cards, and split (3x installment) payments. Joko also runs a business solution offering brand partnerships and consumer market research. Backed by Partech, Joko is tracked in the API Evangelist network as a company profile; it publishes no public developer API, developer portal, or API documentation at this time.

providers.name: KlariVis
providers.description: KlariVis is an enterprise data analytics platform built for community banks and credit unions by former community bankers. It ingests data nightly from a financial institution's core and ancillary systems into a secure Microsoft Azure data warehouse, then aggregates and visualizes it through role-based interactive dashboards covering deposits, loans, transactional intelligence, profitability and funds transfer pricing, plus a Report Builder for bespoke charts and reports. The company was founded in 2019 in Roanoke, Virginia by Kim Snyder, raised an $11M Series B led by Blueprint Equity in January 2024, and serves 100+ financial institutions. KlariVis is a consumer of core banking APIs rather than a publisher of one: it operates no public developer program, publishes no API documentation or machine-readable contract, and integration work is handled through its implementation team.

providers.name: Popular (Banco Popular)
providers.description: Popular, Inc. (NASDAQ: BPOP), operating as Banco Popular, is a publicly traded financial holding company founded in 1893 and headquartered in Hato Rey, San Juan, Puerto Rico. It is the largest bank in Puerto Rico and operates through two chartered depository segments: Banco Popular de Puerto Rico (BPPR), serving Puerto Rico and the U.S. Virgin Islands, and Popular Bank (formerly Banco Popular North America), a New York state-chartered commercial bank serving mainland U.S. markets including New York, New Jersey, and Florida. Popular is FDIC-insured and regulated as a U.S. bank holding company. On its open-finance and API posture, Popular does not publish a first-party public developer portal or downloadable API specifications for its U.S. institutions (popular.com); consumer-permissioned account and transaction data is made available indirectly through third-party data aggregators such as Plaid, Tink, and Finicity rather than a direct bank API. This identity record reflects that honest reality — an aggregator-only access model with no documented first-party API surface, FDX membership, or published CFPB Section 1033 data-access program. (Note: the separate apiportal.popularenlinea.com open-banking portal belongs to Banco Popular Dominicano / Grupo Popular, a distinct Dominican Republic company, not to Popular, Inc.)

providers.name: RockFi
providers.description: RockFi is a French private wealth management firm positioning itself as a modern family office, pairing experienced private-banking advisors with technology to serve high-net-worth entrepreneurs, executives, athletes, and independent professionals. Its fixed-fee model offers life insurance (France and Luxembourg), structured funds, private equity, SCPI real estate, PEA and securities accounts, customized investment mandates, and consolidated real-time portfolio monitoring, tax optimization, and wealth-transmission planning. Registered with ORIAS (23004556) under ACPR and AMF oversight. Backed by Partech. No public developer API is currently published; this profile has been enriched from the public site.

providers.name: Erudifi
providers.description: ErudiFi (ErudiFi Pte. Ltd., formerly Dana Cita Pte. Ltd., a Singapore-registered company) is an education-financing technology company on a mission to expand access to affordable financial services for students across Southeast Asia. It operates two consumer lending platforms: Bukas in the Philippines, which provides secure, integrated tuition installment plans in partnership with top colleges and universities, and Danacita in Indonesia, a peer-to-peer education-financing platform registered with the OJK that funds diploma, bachelor's, master's, and short-course programs. ErudiFi is backed by investors including 500 Global and Helicap. The company maintains a small public GitHub presence (internal tooling, a data-quality checker, and a Danacita UI kit) but publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI specification, SDK, or MCP server.

providers.name: Felix
providers.description: Félix (Félix Pago) is a US-based fintech building financial services for the Latino community in the United States. Its core product lets users send remittances to Latin America in seconds through a WhatsApp message, with no app download or physical-location visit required, covering 9+ countries including Mexico, Guatemala, Honduras, El Salvador, Nicaragua, Colombia, Dominican Republic, Ecuador and Peru with real-time exchange rates, no hidden fees, over 40,000 cash pickup and deposit locations, and Spanish-language support. Félix is expanding beyond remittances into accounts, credit building, savings and investing for immigrants. Backed by General Catalyst and QED Investors. This profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network; Félix is a consumer-facing service and does not currently publish a public developer API or documentation.

providers.name: High Mark Credit Information Services
providers.description: High Mark Credit Information Services (now operating as CRIF High Mark) is one of India's four RBI-licensed credit bureaus, headquartered in Mumbai. It maintains credit information on retail, microfinance, and commercial borrowers, and delivers credit reports, bureau scores, analytics, portfolio monitoring, fraud-detection, and origination-decisioning solutions to banks, NBFCs, microfinance institutions, insurers, and telecom providers. The bureau is best known for its microfinance credit information services and pan-India retail and commercial credit databases. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Battery Ventures and profiled in the API Evangelist network; it publishes no public developer portal or API specification, so this profile captures company identity and domain security posture only.

providers.name: Amica Mutual Insurance
providers.description: Amica Mutual Insurance, founded in 1907, is a mutual insurance company providing automobile, homeowners, condo, renters, life, marine, motorcycle, umbrella liability, flood, and small business insurance to customers across the United States. As a mutual company, Amica is owned by its policyholders and known for award-winning customer service and competitive pricing through bundling discounts.

providers.name: Atlas Card
providers.description: Atlas is a technology company (not a bank) that offers an invite-only luxury lifestyle membership built around a premium metal charge card, issued by Lead Bank. Membership pairs a CNC-milled steel Atlas Card with no preset spending limit and a concierge-driven mobile app that delivers curated restaurant reservations, luxury hotel bookings, access to sold-out concerts and sporting events, points-based travel rewards, and thousands of dollars in annual travel and lifestyle credits. Atlas Card is a consumer fintech product with a full monthly-payment charge structure and an annual membership fee; it does not publish a public developer API. Added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Kindred Ventures and enriched with the identity, well-known discovery, and domain-security surface it exposes publicly.

providers.name: Azos
providers.description: Azos is a Brazilian insurtech (founded 2021) that sells fully digital life insurance directly to consumers and through a broker (corretor) channel. Its products include life insurance, serious-illness coverage, accidental-disability coverage, and funeral assistance, all contracted online in minutes with no medical exam, transparent pricing from around R$5/month, and coverage up to R$1 million. The company positions itself as "seguro de vida sem burocracia" (life insurance without bureaucracy) and is backed by Prosus Ventures. Azos runs a consumer app and a broker portal but publishes no public developer API surface at this time.

providers.name: Copperlane
providers.description: Copperlane is an AI-native mortgage loan origination platform founded in 2025 by Brianna Lin and Athan Zhang and backed by Y Combinator (W26 batch). Its AI agent, Penny, behaves like a real loan officer: it guides borrowers through intake, pulls and reads borrower documents, verifies loan eligibility in real time, answers borrower questions live, and generates Letters of Explanation, delivering cleaner files to human loan officers so they can focus on closing loans instead of chasing paperwork. The San Francisco company raised a $4.1M seed round to modernize a mortgage origination process that remains largely manual. Copperlane is currently a demo-request business application and does not publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal.

providers.name: Coru
providers.description: Coru is an enterprise-grade AI company transforming financial services across Latin America with conversational AI agents. Its "Adi" platform lets banks, fintechs, and insurers build and customize agentic workflows for digital loan origination, 24/7 customer service, collections management, insurance quoting, claims handling, and commission reconciliation across web, app, and WhatsApp channels in Spanish, Portuguese, and English, with multimodal input (text, voice, audio, documents) and OCR-based document capture. Coru serves financial institutions including Bradesco, Banorte, and Neon, and is backed by QED Investors. Coru markets a hosted, enterprise agent product and does not currently publish a public developer API, documentation portal, or SDKs.

providers.name: Coverfox
providers.description: Coverfox is one of India's largest online insurance distribution platforms, offering retail insurance products including car, bike, health, and life insurance alongside embedded insurance solutions for lenders, NBFCs, and fintechs. The company partners with 37+ IRDAI-approved insurers to compare, purchase, and manage policies online, and has reached roughly 10 million households across India. Coverfox was backed by Accel and added to the API Evangelist network as a company profile; it publishes no public developer program or API at this time.

providers.name: Habito
providers.description: Habito is a UK-based digital mortgage broker that lets people research, compare, and apply for mortgages online across the whole of the market, pairing self-serve digital tools with human mortgage experts, alongside related home-buying services. Founded as a fintech in the consumer lending and real-estate space and backed by Ribbit Capital, Habito has since joined Monzo. The company operates a consumer web product (Webflow-hosted marketing site) and does not publish a public developer API program, developer portal, or OpenAPI at the time of this profile; this record is maintained by the API Evangelist network and reflects only publicly verifiable surfaces.

providers.name: Ryland Group
providers.description: The Ryland Group was one of the largest U.S. homebuilders and a leading mortgage finance company before merging with Standard Pacific Corp in October 2015 to form CalAtlantic Group, Inc., which was subsequently acquired by Lennar in 2018. During its operation, Ryland Homes built homes across 17 states and provided financial services including consumer mortgage loans, title, and escrow services. The company's technology stack included Akamai, Amazon CloudFront, ASP.NET, Fiserv for financial services, and Microsoft Dynamics for CRM and ERP.

providers.name: Shriram Finance
providers.description: Shriram Finance Limited is one of India's largest retail non-banking financial companies (NBFC), with roughly Rs 3.02 lakh crore in assets under management and 3,225 branches nationwide. It offers commercial-vehicle, two-wheeler, used-car, personal, business and gold loans, fixed deposits and fixed investment plans, general and life insurance distribution, Bharat BillPay (BBPS) bill payments, and UPI through its Shriram One app. The company runs consumer web and mobile products but publishes no public developer API, developer portal, or OpenAPI specification; a partner portal and a lending-service-provider program serve authorized business partners only.

providers.name: Springcoin
providers.description: Springcoin (operating as Spring Labs) is an AI-native compliance and customer-experience platform for financial services. It builds autonomous AI agents for contact centers, quality assurance, complaint handling, and dispute resolution, alongside SummerGRC, a governance, risk, and compliance product with entity intelligence and an agent builder. The platform integrates with 50+ contact-center and CRM systems and was surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company. No public developer API, OpenAPI, SDK, or open documentation surface was found during enrichment.

providers.name: Axoni
providers.description: Axoni is a New York-based financial data infrastructure company that provides real-time, automated replication of data between institutions, reducing reconciliations, data pipeline management cost, and operational risk across capital markets. Its platform lets banks, asset managers, and market infrastructure providers rapidly deploy critical financial networks and share post-trade data in real time. Axoni is used by leading institutions including JPMorgan, Deutsche Bank, BlackRock, and Citigroup, and has been recognized by Risk.net, the A-Team Group, and Forbes Fintech 50. The company is SOC 2 Type 2 certified and is backed by a16z and DCVC. Axoni does not currently publish a public developer portal, API reference, or SDKs; its documentation surface is access-gated to customers.

providers.name: Responsiv
providers.description: Responsiv is an AI-powered regulatory intelligence and compliance platform that helps organizations monitor regulatory change, translate laws and regulations into clear actionable requirements, identify compliance gaps against existing policies and controls, and track remediation through to completion. The platform continuously monitors 1,000+ regulatory sources across 50+ jurisdictions, routes alerts by business unit, topic, or jurisdiction, maintains an obligations register, and offers agentic legal research with fully cited sources. It serves compliance teams in financial services, health and P&C insurance, and consumer tech. Backed by Greylock. As of this enrichment pass the company exposes no public API, developer portal, or documentation surface.

providers.name: Signal Advisors
providers.description: Signal Advisors is a financial technology company building an integrated software platform for independent financial advisors and insurance professionals. The Signal Platform consolidates annuity, life insurance, and wealth management workflows into a single system, replacing the traditional Independent Marketing Organization (IMO) model. Product lines include Signal Annuity (quoting, design, and submission), Signal Wealth (portfolio and compliance management), and Signal Life (life-insurance workflow automation), with features such as real-time carrier status updates (TrueStatus), fast commission payouts (TruePay), AI-generated policy summaries, and integrated householding. The company operates a closed, account-based advisor portal and does not publish a public developer API surface.

providers.name: Vesta
providers.description: Vesta is an AI-native mortgage Loan Origination System (LOS) — a modern, open system-of-record platform that orchestrates the loan manufacturing process through configurable software workflows and AI agents that run real loans end to end. Founded in 2020 by former Blend employees Mike Yu and Devon Yang and headquartered in San Francisco, Vesta gives mortgage lenders a cloud, API-and-integration-friendly LOS to replace legacy origination systems, connecting to the broader mortgage technology ecosystem. The company raised an Andreessen Horowitz (a16z)-led Series A. Vesta sells to lenders through a demo/partner-signup enterprise motion and does not currently expose a public self-serve developer API, portal, or documentation surface.

providers.name: Cadence Bank
providers.description: Cadence Bank is a regional U.S. commercial bank headquartered in Tupelo, Mississippi and Houston, Texas, formed in October 2021 when legacy Cadence Bancorporation merged into BancorpSouth Bank (the surviving entity, subsequently renamed Cadence Bank; NYSE ticker CADE). It is a Mississippi state-chartered bank operating roughly 400+ branches across the U.S. South, Midwest, and Texas with about $48-50 billion in assets, offering consumer banking, mortgages, home equity, credit cards, small business and commercial banking, treasury management, and wealth/insurance services. On open finance, Cadence Bank exposes no first-party public developer API or developer portal; consumer-permissioned account data is reachable only through third-party aggregators (notably Plaid), which is the honest, prevailing posture for most U.S. regional banks. No documented direct FDX (Financial Data Exchange) membership or published CFPB Section 1033 data-access API was found as of this profile.

providers.name: Corebridge Financial
providers.description: Corebridge Financial (formerly AIG Life and Retirement) is one of the largest and most established retirement and insurance solutions providers in the United States. Spun off from AIG in September 2022 in the largest IPO of that year, Corebridge provides retirement solutions, life insurance, fixed and variable annuities, and institutional products. The company is a leading retirement plan provider for K-12 schools, healthcare, government, higher education, and other not-for-profit institutions. Corebridge Financial does not currently publish a public developer API; participant and plan sponsor access is provided through dedicated portals.

providers.name: Forwardlane
providers.description: ForwardLane Technologies builds Signal Studio, a decision intelligence platform that transforms enterprise data into auditable actions rather than dashboards. Users ask questions in natural language and receive Next Best Actions with complete audit trails in seconds, powered by a semantic data layer, multi-agent AI orchestration, a no-code signal builder, and in-database processing so data never leaves the customer environment. Validated across eight years of Fortune 500 production, Signal Studio serves financial services, private credit and private equity, real estate, energy and oil and gas, and government, with BYOK support for any LLM, cloud, or inference provider. Led by CEO Nathan Stevenson. ForwardLane exposes no public developer API surface; this profile captures the company's public identity and security posture for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Live Oak Bank
providers.description: Live Oak Bank (Live Oak Banking Company) is a digital, branchless, North Carolina state-chartered commercial bank founded in 2008 and headquartered in Wilmington, NC, operating as the primary subsidiary of Live Oak Bancshares, Inc. (NYSE: LOB). It is the largest originator of U.S. Small Business Administration (SBA) 7(a) loans in the country and serves small businesses in all 50 states with SBA and commercial lending, high-yield business and personal savings, CDs, and business checking with treasury services. Technology-forward for a bank of its size, Live Oak runs a cloud-native Finxact core (now Fiserv) with an Apiture-based digital banking platform, and in 2024 launched an in-house embedded-banking / Banking-as-a-Service (BaaS) program that lets software companies deliver Live Oak deposit and payment products to their own customers. Its API surface is real but partner-gated: a production AWS API gateway operates at api.liveoak.bank (returning MissingAuthenticationToken to unauthenticated callers, with Live-Oak-specific lob-identity-id / lob-foreign-entity-id headers), but Live Oak publishes no public self-serve developer portal, no downloadable OpenAPI/Swagger, and no public API reference. Consumer-permissioned data access is available through account aggregators rather than a first-party public API, and no FDX participation or CFPB Section 1033 data-access posture is publicly documented.

providers.name: Odessa Technologies
providers.description: Odessa is a Philadelphia-headquartered lease and loan management software company founded in 1998 that powers asset finance for banks, captive finance companies, and independent lenders. The Odessa Platform manages roughly $200B in assets across equipment finance and auto finance, covering the full asset lifecycle from origination through servicing and remarketing on a modern, API-first, Microsoft Azure-hosted SaaS stack with low-code developer tools, packaged integrations, and an Odessa AI layer for agentic asset-finance workflows. The platform's APIs and developer tooling are delivered to licensed customers (no public developer portal, no OpenAPI, no public SDK or GitHub org); profiling here captures the surface visible from the marketing site, integrations catalog, and engineering blog.

providers.name: Security Service Federal Credit Union
providers.description: Security Service Federal Credit Union (SSFCU), headquartered in San Antonio, Texas, is a member-owned, not-for-profit financial cooperative federally chartered and insured by the National Credit Union Administration (NCUA). It is one of the largest credit unions in the United States, serving members across Texas, Colorado, and Utah with consumer and business banking, deposit accounts, credit cards, auto and mortgage lending, and investment services through branches, online banking, and mobile apps. Its open-finance posture is the norm for a US credit union: there is no first-party public developer portal or downloadable API specification, and no public FDX or CFPB Section 1033 data-access API is documented. Consumer-permissioned account data is reachable only indirectly through third-party aggregators, and any API capability is delivered through its core banking provider rather than a self-serve developer program.

providers.name: Servus Credit Union
providers.description: Servus Credit Union Ltd. is a member-owned cooperative financial institution headquartered in Edmonton, Alberta, founded in 1938. It is Alberta's largest credit union and, following its 2023 member-approved merger with connectFirst Credit Union, became Canada's largest credit union by total assets (roughly $30 billion CAD), serving more than 500,000 members through about 100 branches and distributing profits back to members via its Profit Share program rather than to outside shareholders. As a provincially regulated Alberta credit union, Servus operates within a cooperative charter and offers retail and business banking, mortgages, loans, investments, and digital/mobile banking. On the open-finance front its posture is aggregator-only and honest: Servus runs no public first-party developer portal or documented public API. External data access to member accounts today is provided through third-party financial-data aggregators (Mastercard Open Banking / Finicity and Plaid) via consumer-permissioned connections, consistent with Canada's voluntary, not-yet-operational Consumer-Driven Banking framework overseen by the Financial Consumer Agency of Canada (FCAC).

providers.name: Skience (The Athene Group)
providers.description: Skience, a product of The Athene Group, is a wealth management technology company that delivers a Salesforce-based platform for firms undergoing digital transformation. Its platform serves broker-dealers, registered investment advisors (RIAs), and enterprise wealth management organizations with digital client and advisor onboarding, automated account opening, data management and aggregation, and advisor productivity tooling built natively on the Salesforce Financial Services Cloud ecosystem. Skience is backed by Insight Partners and operates as a private SaaS provider; it does not publish a public developer API, OpenAPI specification, or developer portal, but it does maintain a SafeBase-hosted trust center documenting SOC 2 Type 2 and SOC 2 + HITRUST attestations and a responsible disclosure program.

providers.name: NerdWallet
providers.description: NerdWallet is a personal finance company that helps consumers make smarter money decisions across credit cards, banking, investing, loans, mortgages, insurance, and taxes. Through its website and mobile apps it offers comparison tools, product marketplaces, educational content, and free credit-score monitoring. Founded in 2009 and headquartered in San Francisco, NerdWallet is publicly traded (NASDAQ: NRDS) and was surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of ivp. As of this enrichment pass NerdWallet publishes no public developer API, developer portal, or well-known API discovery surface; this profile captures its public identity and domain-security posture.

providers.name: PC Financial
providers.description: PC Financial (President's Choice Financial) is the financial-services brand of Canadian grocery giant Loblaw Companies Limited. Its personal banking and Mastercard credit-card products are issued by President's Choice Bank, a federally chartered Schedule I bank and CDIC member, while insurance is offered through PC Financial Insurance. The digital-first, branchless brand centers on the no-fee PC Money Account (a Mastercard-network everyday spending account launched September 2020), a line of PC Financial and PC World Elite Mastercard credit cards, and deep integration with the PC Optimum loyalty program across Loblaw's grocery, pharmacy, and retail banners. Consumer banking (chequing, savings, mortgages) was transferred to CIBC's Simplii Financial in 2017, so PC Financial today is a rewards-linked digital banking arm rather than a full-service bank. In December 2025 Equitable Bank (EQB) agreed to acquire PC Financial from Loblaw for roughly $800 million. On open finance, PC Financial runs NO public first-party developer portal or API; Canada's Consumer-Driven Banking framework is legislated but not yet operational, so consumer account access today is aggregator/screen-scraping-based via providers such as Plaid and Finicity (Mastercard). The bank supports Interac e-Transfer on the PC Money Account as shared payments-rail participation.

providers.name: Qardy
providers.description: Qardy is the first online lending aggregator marketplace in Egypt and the wider MENA region, connecting micro, small, and medium enterprises (MSMEs) with banks and financial institutions for debt financing. Its digital matchmaking platform collects and digitizes business and individual financial data, runs bank-statement and financial-statement analysis, produces credit ratings and predictive profiles, then matches eligible applicants to partner financial institutions by loan amount, industry, and risk rating. Qardy offers business loans (from EGP 50,000), micro-company financing (up to EGP 242,000), small and medium company financing (from EGP 250,000 to over EGP 10,000,000), supply chain / invoice financing, leasing, and factoring — free of charge to applicants through a fast, transparent three-step application process.

providers.name: Uhura Solutions
providers.description: Uhura Solutions is a London-based AI platform for document-driven process automation in financial services, combining fine-tuned large language models, a low-code framework, and a visual workflow engine to deliver intelligent data capture, intelligent document processing, and intelligent process automation for banks and financial institutions including Barclays, Raiffeisen, and Erste Bank. A Techstars portfolio company, Uhura publishes no public developer portal or self-serve API surface; platform access is arranged through sales contact.

providers.name: Apollo Agriculture
providers.description: Apollo Agriculture is an agricultural technology company founded in 2016 and headquartered in Nairobi, Kenya, that helps small-scale farmers across Africa maximize their profits. Apollo delivers a full-stack service bundling quality farm inputs (seed and fertilizer), flexible input financing and credit, satellite- and machine-learning-driven agronomic advice, crop insurance, and market access, distributed through a network of local agrodealers and mobile technology. The company serves smallholder farmers in markets including Kenya and Zambia and is backed by investors including Anthemis and the SoftBank Vision Fund. This profile tracks Apollo Agriculture as a company in the API Evangelist network; no public developer API has been identified at this time.

providers.name: Go Rise
providers.description: Rise (gorise.co) is a Dubai-based fintech platform that gives migrant workers control over their finances across both their home and host countries. Through a mobile app for iOS and Android, Rise offers bank accounts, insurance, savings and investment options, "Pay Later" installment services, and remittance and money-transfer capabilities. The company partners with regulated financial institutions including United Arab Bank and insurance providers such as AXA Gulf, and is headquartered in DMCC, Jumeirah Lakes Towers, Dubai, UAE. Rise is a portfolio company of 500 Global and has raised funding led by MEVP. This is a consumer financial-services product with no public developer/API surface at the time of enrichment.

providers.name: OneConnect
providers.description: OneConnect Financial Technology (NYSE: OCFT; HKEX: 6638) is a technology-as-a-service platform for financial institutions, incorporated in 2015 as an associate of China's Ping An Group to externalize its banking and insurance technology. Its cloud-native, microservices platform spans digital banking, digital insurance, and the Gamma platform (AI voice, computer vision, blockchain and big-data analytics), serving hundreds of banks and insurers across China and Southeast Asia with ready-to-integrate financial technology components exposed through Open APIs. OneConnect raised a US$650M Series A in 2018 from investors including the SoftBank Vision Fund and SBI Group. Its APIs are delivered as enterprise B2B integrations rather than a public self-serve developer portal.

providers.name: Payna
providers.description: Payna is a compliance operating system for financial licensing that automates applications, renewals, maintenance, and monitoring across all 50 US states and jurisdictions. It tracks state statutes, NMLS procedures, and FinCEN requirements in real time, calculates filing deadlines backward from due dates, scores compliance posture against state examiner playbooks, automates document pre-fill and e-signature, and maintains a timestamped, queryable audit trail for examinations. Payna serves regulated financial sectors including money transmission, lending, mortgage, cryptocurrency/VASP, debt collection, loan origination, and insurance. It is a Y Combinator (W26) company; no public developer API is currently published.

providers.name: Tugende
providers.description: Tugende is a for-profit social enterprise founded in 2012 in Uganda that uses asset finance, technology, and a customer-centric model to help informal-sector entrepreneurs (MSMEs) own income-generating assets through lease-to-own financing — motorcycles (boda bodas), taxis, matatus, boat engines, smartphones, and small-business equipment like salon kits, fridges, and sewing machines. Operating in Uganda and Kenya with 800+ full-time staff, Tugende has served over 52,000 clients. Backed by Partech. Tugende publishes no public API or developer program as of this profile.

providers.name: WithAI
providers.description: WithAI is a San Francisco-based Y Combinator (Spring 2026) company building Multiplier, a secure AI platform for institutional investors and independent equity hedge funds. Multiplier unifies structured data, unstructured data, AI agents, human work, and firm knowledge so investment teams can research stocks and manage portfolios more efficiently, with an integration ecosystem spanning Bloomberg, FactSet, Enfusion, Snowflake, and other market data and infrastructure platforms. WithAI does not currently publish a public API, developer portal, or documentation.

providers.name: Amartha
providers.description: Amartha (PT Amartha Mikro Fintek, operating as Amartha Financial Group) is an Indonesian technology company founded in 2010 that builds digital financial infrastructure for the grassroots economy, connecting micro-entrepreneurs — predominantly women running micro and small businesses in rural villages — with affordable working capital from retail and institutional funders. Its consumer and agent brands include Amartha Prosper (investment), Celengan (savings), Modal (group loans), AmarthaLink (agent network) and the AmarthaFin mobile app for payments and bill purchase, alongside two business lines — Institutional Investments and Embedded Lending — that let banks, non-bank financial institutions, insurers and technology partners channel loans to Amartha borrowers. The company is headquartered at Amartha Village in South Jakarta, and runs its social impact programs through Amartha.org.

providers.name: Arq
providers.description: Arq (formerly DolarApp) is a Latin American cross-border fintech app that gives travelers, investors, and professionals digital dollar and digital euro accounts at real market rates without hidden fees. Founded in 2021, the mobile-first platform offers currency conversion, a borderless payment card, global accounts to send and receive international payments, bill payment, PIX transfers, stock and ETF investing, and high-yield Trade and Save accounts, plus ARQ Premium and Prestige tiers. Arq raised $70M from Sequoia Capital and Founders Fund and serves over 2 million users across the Americas. Arq is a consumer mobile product and does not publish a public API or developer portal; this profile captures its verified public identity and web surface for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Atlantic Money
providers.description: Atlantic Money is a London-based fintech, founded in 2020 by Robinhood alumni and backed by Index Ventures, offering international money transfers at a flat GBP 3 fee with the live mid-market exchange rate and no FX markup.
