The service supports transfers across ten currencies with direct bank deposits and standard or express delivery, for both consumers and businesses, and is authorized and regulated by the UK FCA as a payment institution. Atlantic Money is a consumer- and business-facing mobile and web application; it publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI, or SDK surface, so this network profile is limited to company identity, website property links, and probed domain-security posture.

providers.name: First Circle
providers.description: First Circle is a Philippine fintech offering digital business banking and non-collateral financing to small and medium enterprises. Its products include free online business bank accounts, business credit lines up to PHP 20M, same/next-day express business loans, longer-term Business Credit Plus, future salary access for employees, and solar financing. The company is 100% online with five-minute account opening and no branch visits, serves over 5,000 Filipino businesses, and has disbursed roughly PHP 16 billion in loans. It is licensed by the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC), with banking delivered through partner rural banks regulated by the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas (BSP). It was surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company. No public developer API surface is currently published.

providers.name: Klaim
providers.description: Klaim (Klaim Kapital Technologies Limited / Klaim Holdings Limited) is an Abu Dhabi-founded, UAE-based healthcare fintech that advances working capital against receivables. Healthcare providers, real estate brokers and SMEs submit unpaid insurance claims or invoices, Klaim's AI evaluates and prices the risk in real time, and Klaim advances up to 90% of face value within 24 hours, collecting only when the payer or client settles. Products span Klaim Health (insurance claim advances plus AI denial prediction), Klaim Flow (SME receivables purchasing with an escrow model), Klaim Estate (real estate commission advances) and Klaim Eligible (insurance eligibility verification). Founded in December 2019 by Karim Dakki and Ahmad Ghafour, backed by Techstars, and operating across the GCC, North Africa and Turkey. Klaim publishes no public developer portal, API documentation or machine-readable API description at this time.

providers.name: Moneyfellows
providers.description: Money Fellows is an Egyptian fintech, founded in 2018 and regulated by the Central Bank of Egypt, that digitizes the traditional rotating savings and credit association (ROSCA / "gam'eya") model as a mobile app. Members join Money Circles to save together and access interest-free funds on flexible 6, 10, or 12-month plans of up to 1.2M EGP, and can spend and save through a prepaid Money Fellows Mastercard. The service is Sharia-compliant (Official Fatwa No. 46205 from the Egyptian Dar Al Iftaa) and has served millions of users while raising roughly $60M across its funding rounds, including a 2025 Series B first close backed by investors such as Partech. Money Fellows is a consumer mobile application and does not publish a public developer API, developer portal, or programmatic integration surface.

providers.name: Payall
providers.description: Payall Payment Systems provides purpose-built banking infrastructure that automates cross-border payments for regulated financial institutions. The platform orchestrates the full international money-movement lifecycle across originating banks, correspondent and clearing institutions, central banks, and payment channels, automating sanctions screening, KYC/AML compliance, fraud and risk management, FX, and settlement. Payall markets a lightweight, backward- compatible technical integration and business-friendly APIs (plus bulk/Excel upload) so banks, credit unions, EMIs, and other regulated institutions can offer safe, profitable international transfers. Public developer documentation and an open API specification are not published; the API surface at api.payall.com is authentication-gated.

providers.name: Personetics
providers.description: Personetics is a Cognitive Banking platform that helps banks and financial institutions deliver AI-driven, financial-data-personalized customer engagement and money management. Its products analyze customer transaction data in real time to surface personalized insights, proactive financial guidance, automated savings and cash-flow programs, and self-driving finance experiences embedded inside a bank's own mobile and web channels. Personetics serves hundreds of banks and financial institutions across roughly 30 global markets, reaching an estimated 150 million banking customers, and positions itself as a way for banks to deepen and monetize customer relationships. The platform is delivered as enterprise software integrated into a bank's digital banking stack rather than as a public self-serve developer API; developer and integration material lives in a gated Personetics Documentation Hub.

providers.name: Sav Technologies Limited
providers.description: Sav Technologies Limited operates Sav (sav.money), a UAE-based intelligent financial platform that lets users track, save, invest, and grow their wealth across accounts. Sav offers a suite of consumer products including Gold (physical gold investment from AED 10), MyMoney (financial management and savings), Card (a prepaid card with cashback), Wealth (investing), Sav Pro (premium membership), and an upcoming Credit product. Sav describes itself as extending the APIs and technology components of licensed financial services providers to its users. It is a 500 Global portfolio company. As of this enrichment pass, Sav publishes a consumer app and marketing site but no public developer API, API documentation, developer portal, or SDKs.

providers.name: SendWave
providers.description: Sendwave is an international money-transfer service operated by Zepz (the fintech group behind WorldRemit) that lets people send money abroad directly from a mobile app, with a focus on low or no transfer fees and fast delivery to recipients across Africa, Asia and Latin America. Funds can be sent to mobile-money wallets, bank accounts and cash pickup in supported corridors. Sendwave is a consumer-facing app (iOS and Android) and is regulated as a money transmitter in the jurisdictions where it operates (NMLS No. 1179663). As of this profile it publishes no public developer API, SDKs, or developer portal; enrichment therefore captures its public identity, security posture, and support surface only.

providers.name: Vridhi Home Finance
providers.description: Vridhi Home Finance (Vridhi Finserv Home Finance Limited) is an affordable housing finance company (HFC) headquartered in Bengaluru, India, founded in 2022. Operating as a tech-enabled brick-and-mortar lender across tier-2 and tier-3 cities, it provides home purchase loans, home construction loans, plot-and-construction loans, balance-transfer and top-up loans, and loans against property to salaried and self-employed customers. The company is backed by Norwest Venture Partners and Elevation Capital. It operates a public marketing website, a customer service portal, a refer-and-earn portal, and an Android mobile app, but publishes no public developer API, documentation, or machine-readable API surface.

providers.name: Yonder
providers.description: Yonder is a UK-based financial technology company offering rewards credit and debit cards — a "financial membership" that earns points on everyday spending, redeemable across 300+ dining, travel, shopping, entertainment and wellness partners. Cards run on the Mastercard network with no foreign-exchange fees, and Yonder is authorised and regulated by the UK Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) with FSCS-protected accounts held via partner banks. Yonder ships a consumer mobile app and a help centre but does not expose a public developer API or portal. Added to the API Evangelist network as a VC-portfolio lead (backers include Northzone, Seedcamp and Techstars).

providers.name: Neo Financial
providers.description: Neo Financial is a Calgary- and Winnipeg-based Canadian fintech (neobank) founded in 2019 by the founders of SkipTheDishes, offering credit cards, savings, money, investing, and mortgage products to consumers. Neo is not a chartered bank and holds no Canadian banking licence; it delivers CDIC-eligible deposits and card issuance through regulated partner institutions — Peoples Bank of Canada for everyday accounts, ATB Financial as Mastercard credit-card issuer, and formerly Concentra Bank (now part of Equitable Bank) for savings. Neo operates a consumer mobile and web platform only and publishes no first-party public developer API or developer portal; third-party access to Neo accounts today is available solely through data aggregators such as Flinks (a National Bank-owned Canadian aggregator) and Plaid via credential/screen-scraping access, not a documented first-party API. Canada's federal Consumer-Driven Banking (open banking) framework, legislated in Budget 2024 and overseen by the Financial Consumer Agency of Canada, is not yet operational, so no first-party FDX or CDB data API exists. Neo maintains a public GitHub organization of internal engineering tooling and an engineering blog, but ships no public API products.

providers.name: Old National Bank
providers.description: Old National Bank is a nationally chartered, FDIC-insured regional commercial bank and the primary subsidiary of Old National Bancorp (NASDAQ: ONB), headquartered in Evansville, Indiana and Chicago, Illinois. With roughly $73 billion in assets and nearly 200 retail branches across Illinois, Indiana, Iowa, Kentucky, Michigan, Minnesota, Tennessee, and Wisconsin, it is one of the largest commercial banks headquartered in the U.S. Midwest, offering consumer, small business, commercial, treasury management, and wealth banking. Old National does not operate a first-party public developer portal or publish any downloadable OpenAPI/Swagger specifications; probes of developer., api., and apis.oldnational.com do not resolve and /developers returns HTTP 404. Consumer-permissioned account and transaction data is instead reached through third-party financial data aggregators (Finicity by Mastercard is documented), which is the honest, aggregator-only open-finance posture typical of U.S. regional banks. No documented first-party FDX-conformant data-access API or published CFPB Section 1033 developer surface was found at review time.

providers.name: Sea Group (Sea Limited)
providers.description: Sea Limited is a Singapore-headquartered consumer internet holding company that operates three core businesses across Southeast Asia, Taiwan, and Latin America: Shopee (e-commerce), Garena (digital entertainment and game publishing), and SeaMoney / Monee (digital financial services including SeaBank, ShopeePay, and SPayLater). Sea Limited is publicly listed on the NYSE (ticker: SE). Sea does not publish a unified group-level developer API — each operating subsidiary maintains its own developer platform: Shopee Open Platform (open.shopee.com) for marketplace integrations, Garena for game-platform partners, and SeaMoney / ShopeePay for in-region payment integrations.

providers.name: Tallyman
providers.description: Tallyman is Experian's collections and recoveries management software platform, acquired from Talgentra. It provides an end-to-end collections management system for financial services, utilities, telecommunications, and public sector organizations. The platform manages customer segmentation, contact strategies, decision automation, and analytics for debt collection operations. Tallyman integrates with Experian Decision Analytics, CRM systems, billing platforms, and external data sources via web services. It is available as a hosted service managed through Experian's data centres.

providers.name: TechProcess Payment Services
providers.description: TechProcess Payment Services is an Indian digital-payments pioneer that has been building and operating cloud-based electronic-payment platforms since 2000, when it launched BillJunction.com, India's first electronic bill presentment and payment service. Its payment gateway supports card payments, Net-banking, NACH, NEFT/RTGS, IMPS, UPI and e-wallets for merchants across India. The business is now part of Worldline India (ePayments India), whose merchant checkout product is Paynimo, offering hosted and embeddable checkout, native mobile SDKs, and 20+ e-commerce platform plugins so developers can accept digital payments with a few lines of code. Originally a Battery Ventures portfolio company, it was acquired by Ingenico Group and folded into Worldline.

providers.name: Valley National Bank
providers.description: Valley National Bank is a nationally chartered commercial bank (OCC-regulated) and the principal banking subsidiary of Valley National Bancorp (NASDAQ: VLY), a regional financial holding company founded in 1927 with roughly $64 billion in assets and more than 200 offices serving consumers, families, and businesses across New Jersey, New York, Florida, Alabama, California, and Illinois. Its business spans consumer banking, commercial banking, and treasury services. As of this profile Valley National Bank operates no first-party public developer portal and publishes no downloadable API specifications; consumer-permissioned account and transaction data is reached only through third-party open-finance aggregators (Finicity by Mastercard is documented, alongside general Plaid/Tink connectivity) rather than a directly exposed FDX-conformant or first-party API.

providers.name: Amalan
providers.description: Amalan (amalan International) is an Indonesian financial-services technology company headquartered in Jakarta and registered with Indonesia's Financial Services Authority (OJK). It helps distressed consumers and small-business owners restructure and refinance credit-card debt, personal loans (KTA), online loans (pinjol), and mortgages back toward creditworthiness. Its consumer platform provides a debt-relief negotiation program, amalanPROTECT protection against unethical debt collectors, Credit Score by amalan credit-score checks and history reports, and Credit Checkup loan-rejection consultation. Amalan is not a lender and does not take deposits or originate loans. It is backed by 500 Global. The company runs a consumer web app and marketing/blog site but publishes no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal.

providers.name: Arteria AI
providers.description: Arteria AI is an enterprise AI company for financial services that positions itself as the agentic backbone of financial services operations. Its platform automates document-intensive workflows across the institutional client lifecycle for tier-one global financial institutions: OTC derivatives and ISDA onboarding, prime brokerage, securities services and custody, corporate and commercial lending, trade confirmations, securities lending and repo, regulatory reporting, and post-transaction loan compliance. The platform spans four layers (data, component, agentic, and workflow), combining no-code configuration, automated document generation, intelligent extraction with zero-shot models, clause comparison and decisioning, and controlled agentic orchestration. Arteria AI is SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 certified. It does not publish a public API or developer portal; this profile captures the company identity, domain-security posture, and published compliance certifications.

providers.name: Hilltop Holdings
providers.description: Hilltop Holdings is a major US corporation and Fortune 1000 company. The Hilltop Holdings API provides programmatic access to its platform services, data, and integrations for enterprise customers and partners.

providers.name: Hoptroff
providers.description: Hoptroff is a London-based precision timing company that delivers Traceable Time as a Service (TTaaS), providing enterprise-grade, traceable UTC time with guaranteed SLA accuracy to any data center or cloud environment. Founded in 2015 by Richard Hoptroff, the company operates a global network of atomic timing hubs in London, New York, and Tokyo, delivering microsecond-level precision over IEEE 1588 Precision Time Protocol (PTP) and NTP. Its Certified Time and Terrestrial Time Feed products let organizations timestamp and audit automated events without a satellite dependency, using resilient multi-source feeds (three satellite feeds plus a terrestrial feed from the RISE Institute of Sweden) that are hardened against GPS spoofing and network failure. Hoptroff is certified to ISO 27001 and ISO 9001, and its time synchronization is licensed as an API so a consistent, compliant timescale can be applied across an enterprise for use cases in financial services (MiFID II timestamping and high-frequency trading), content streaming, gaming, IoT, and distributed ledger technology.

providers.name: Mundi
providers.description: Mundi is a digital cross-border trade finance platform for exporters, primarily connecting Mexican exporters with US importers. It provides non-recourse international factoring (invoice advances up to $10M USD / $200M MXN with rates from 0.9% per month), foreign-exchange spot and hedging across 100+ currencies, purchase-order and revolving-line financing, multi-currency virtual US accounts and international payments/collections, and digital cargo insurance. Backed by Speedinvest and Union Square Ventures, Mundi operates a customer web application but publishes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface at this time.

providers.name: Prosperity Bank
providers.description: Prosperity Bank is a Texas-chartered commercial bank (member FDIC, NMLS ID 466414) and the banking subsidiary of Prosperity Bancshares, Inc. (NYSE: PB), a Houston, Texas based regional financial holding company with roughly $37-43 billion in total assets and 300-plus full-service branches across Texas and central Oklahoma. It offers consumer and commercial banking, treasury management, mortgage, and wealth services, and has grown largely through acquisitions (LegacyTexas, Lone Star State Bancshares, American Bank Holding, Southwest Bancshares, Stellar Bancorp). On open finance, Prosperity Bank operates no first-party public developer portal or documented API: developer. and api. subdomains do not resolve, and no /developers or /api pages exist. Consumer-permissioned account and transaction data is reachable only through third-party aggregators (Finicity/Mastercard Open Banking, Plaid, and similar), not a directly published bank API. No FDX-conformant data-access API or CFPB Section 1033 posture is publicly documented by the bank as of this review.

providers.name: Qwil
providers.description: Qwil (qwil.co) is a financial-technology company and a 500 Global portfolio company. It operates a consumer-facing web and mobile application ("Qwil WebApp" at app.qwil.com) backed by a private, authenticated REST API at api.qwil.co. The platform connects to users' bank accounts through Plaid and uses Firebase Authentication (Google Identity Platform) for identity, with bearer tokens presented to a Django REST Framework API. Qwil does not publish a public API specification, developer portal, or SDK documentation; the API is private and partner-gated. Note that qwil.co is distinct from Qwil Messenger (qwil.io), an unrelated secure client-collaboration platform. This profile was enriched by live probing of Qwil's public network surface; most standard developer artifacts are unavailable because Qwil exposes no public developer program.

providers.name: SouthState Bank
providers.description: SouthState Bank, National Association is an OCC-chartered national commercial bank headquartered in Winter Haven, Florida, and the principal subsidiary of SouthState Bank Corporation (NASDAQ: SSB). Formed through the 2020 merger of South State Corporation and CenterState Bank and redomiciled to Florida in 2025, it holds roughly $67 billion in assets and operates across the Southeast, Texas, Colorado, and Virginia. Like most US regional banks, SouthState runs no public first-party developer portal and publishes no downloadable OpenAPI or Swagger definitions. Consumer-permissioned data access is delivered through third-party aggregators rather than a direct API: the Open Banking Tracker records SouthState reachable via Plaid only, with no documented Financial Data Exchange (FDX) endpoint and no published CFPB Section 1033 data-access surface. Its open-finance posture is therefore aggregator-mediated, not a self-serve developer program.

providers.name: Beesafe Ai
providers.description: Beesafe AI is a fraud-prevention and anti-scam platform whose tagline is "Stopping Scams Before They Reach Your Customers." Its AI-powered anti-scam agents proactively engage scammers to uncover the fraudulent accounts, money-mule networks, and criminal financial infrastructure behind trust-based scams such as romance scams, pig-butchering, and investment fraud, which bypass traditional detection by convincing victims to authorize transactions themselves. Beesafe serves financial-services firms, cryptocurrency companies, telecommunications providers, and government agencies. It was founded by AI and security PhDs from Carnegie Mellon and UC San Diego and is backed by Y Combinator, Obvious Ventures, and SBIR/STTR funding. The platform is currently in early access with no public self-service API, developer documentation, or pricing published.

providers.name: Finaccess
providers.description: Finaccess Mexico, S.A. de C.V., Sociedad Operadora de Fondos de Inversion, is an independent Mexican investment-fund operator (asset manager) authorized by the CNBV and the SHCP and regulated by Banco de Mexico. Founded in 2000 and headquartered in Mexico City, it is part of Grupo Finaccess and operates under the tagline "Acceso financiero para todos" (financial access for everyone). Finaccess manages the AXES family of mutual funds spanning short/medium/long-term local debt (AXES CP, MP, LP), domestic and international equity (AXES BMV, GLO, GSP, USA), dollar-denominated debt (AXES COB), and ESG equity (AXES ESG), and it distributes third-party funds from Franklin Templeton, Santander, and Scotiabank. It provides model portfolios, published rate-of-return tracking, and Morningstar-rated fund evaluation for retail and institutional clients. Finaccess publishes no public developer API; this profile carries company identity and domain-security enrichment only.

providers.name: MISMO
providers.description: MISMO — the Mortgage Industry Standards Maintenance Organization — is the standards development body for US real estate finance, founded in 1999 and a not-for-profit wholly owned subsidiary of the Mortgage Bankers Association since 2004. Its Reference Model defines the data of a loan from application through closing, servicing and the secondary market, and version 3.6 ships an XML schema, a Logical Data Dictionary, a Unique ID Matrix and a YAML file set that conforms to the OpenAPI Specification, alongside a MISMO API Toolkit and services such as a FIPS Code API. Around the Reference Model sit sixteen dataset specifications — iLAD, the Mortgage Compliance Dataset, the IRS 4506-C, the VA forms, adverse action, closing instructions — plus SMART Doc and the eMortgage and eNote work, and certification programmes for RON, eClosing, eVault and SMART Doc systems. MISMO standards are accepted and deployed by every type of entity involved in creating mortgages and are required by most regulators, housing agencies and the GSEs. It governs in the open — fourteen bodies and their rosters are published — and distributes behind a $3,500 annual membership and a licence agreement, which is the exact inverse of the specifications-as-code posture CAMARA and NMFTA took.

providers.name: Stockbit
providers.description: Stockbit (PT Stockbit Sekuritas Digital) is an Indonesian retail-investing platform and social community for the Indonesia Stock Exchange (IDX), letting members discuss, analyze, and trade stocks with real-time market data, fundamentals, trading ideas, news, and sentiment. The product is delivered as consumer iOS and Android apps plus a web experience, with a separate crypto brand (Stockbit Crypto). It was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global. As of this enrichment pass Stockbit publishes no public developer API, developer portal, OpenAPI/Swagger definition, SDK, or .well-known discovery surface — the profile is maintained as a consumer-app company record rather than an API provider.

providers.name: Thndr
providers.description: Thndr is an Egyptian investment and brokerage mobile app that lets retail users open a regulated brokerage account and invest in Egyptian Exchange (EGX) stocks, US equities, mutual funds, ETFs, and IPOs from their phone. Founded in 2019 and headquartered in Cairo, Thndr is licensed by Egypt's Financial Regulatory Authority (FRA) and registered with the Egyptian Exchange as a brokerage, positioning itself as a low-cost, mobile-first gateway to the capital markets across Egypt and the wider MENA region. The company raised a $20M Series A in 2022 led by Tiger Global with participation from Prosus Ventures and others, and has been recognized among Forbes Middle East's top fintech companies. Thndr's product surface is a consumer investing app (iOS, Android, and a web account-access portal) with an educational Learn hub and a customer support center; as of this profile it publishes no public developer program, API documentation, or machine-readable API artifacts.

providers.name: Alogent
providers.description: Alogent is a banking and financial technology provider that delivers cloud-native software to banks and credit unions across three product families: payments and deposit automation (Unify omni-channel check capture across branch, mobile, and ATM/ITM), intelligent check fraud detection and mitigation (Alogent Shield and Shield+), and enterprise content and loan document management (FASTdocs, AccuAccount, and the Alogent Document Portal). The platform emphasizes workflow automation, compliance controls, real-time transaction processing, and AI-assisted fraud prevention for financial institutions of all sizes. Alogent is a portfolio company of Battery Ventures. No public developer portal or API documentation surface was found during enrichment.

providers.name: Barclays US
providers.description: Barclays US is the United States consumer banking arm of Barclays PLC, operated through Barclays Bank Delaware, a Delaware state-chartered bank headquartered in Wilmington. Doing business as Barclays US (barclaysus.com redirects to cards.barclaycardus.com), it is one of the largest co-branded credit card issuers in the country, running highly customized card programs for major travel, airline, retail, and affinity partners (JetBlue, American Airlines, Wyndham, AARP, Gap, and others), alongside small-business cards, installment loans, point-of-sale financing, and a direct-to-consumer online savings and CD franchise. Unlike Barclays UK — which operates a mandated PSD2 Open Banking API Exchange at developer.barclays.com — the US consumer entity publishes no first-party public developer portal or downloadable API specification. US open finance is voluntary and fragmented, so consumer- permissioned account and card data from Barclays US is reached in practice through third-party data aggregators rather than a documented first-party API. No FDX-conformant data-access endpoint or formally stated CFPB Section 1033 posture is published on the US site as of this profile.

providers.name: CohnReznick
providers.description: CohnReznick is a top-25 US accounting, tax, and advisory firm formed in 2012 by the merger of J.H. Cohn LLP and Reznick Group, P.C. The firm serves clients across more than 30 industries from offices throughout the United States and four offshore subsidiaries, with its global reach extended through membership in the Nexia International network (operating in more than 128 countries). In May 2024 CohnReznick became the first US accounting firm of its scale to receive a strategic growth investment from a private equity sponsor when funds advised by Apax Partners acquired a majority stake. As part of that transaction the firm operates under an alternative-practice structure: audit and attest services are delivered by CohnReznick LLP (a licensed CPA firm) while tax and advisory services are delivered through CohnReznick Advisory LLC. Largest practice areas include Real Estate, Renewable Energy, Government Contracting, Asset Management (private equity, hedge funds, private credit, REITs), Financial Services, Healthcare, Life Sciences, Consumer & Industrial, Technology & Media, Public Sector, and Private Clients (family offices, high net worth individuals, professional sports). CohnReznick does not publish a public software developer API; this repository documents the firm's organizational profile, practice taxonomy, and linked-data context for API catalog purposes.

providers.name: First Nations Bank of Canada
providers.description: First Nations Bank of Canada (FNBC) is a Schedule I federally regulated chartered bank under the Bank Act, chartered on 19 November 1996 and headquartered in Saskatoon, Saskatchewan. It is the first Canadian chartered bank to be independently controlled by Indigenous shareholders — roughly 88% Indigenous owned and controlled by 78 Indigenous shareholder groups from Nunavut, Northwest Territories, Yukon, Saskatchewan, Manitoba, Alberta and Quebec — and focuses on serving the Indigenous marketplace, with over 90% of its loans going directly to Indigenous communities, many of its branches on reserve, and CDIC-insured deposits. On the open-finance and API front, FNBC runs no first-party developer portal and publishes no public API: probes of developer.fnbc.ca, api.fnbc.ca and developers.fnbc.ca all fail to resolve, and the fnbc.ca site exposes only retail online-banking and a mobile app, not a documented API surface. Canada's federal Consumer-Driven Banking framework (legislated via Budget 2024 / Fall Economic Statement 2024, with FCAC as overseer) is not yet operational, so third-party access to FNBC account data today is voluntary and effectively aggregator-mediated (Flinks, Plaid and similar), not a first-party open-banking API.

providers.name: Happy Money
providers.description: Happy Money is a consumer finance company offering fully digital unsecured personal loans, best known for The Payoff Loan, aimed at helping members consolidate and pay off high-interest credit card debt. Loans are funded through a network of community-focused credit unions, banks, and asset managers rather than by Happy Money itself. The company has served over 350,000 customers and facilitated more than $7 billion in personal loans, and operates the industry's first end-to-end API for unsecured lending, offered to lending partners through a gated partner portal rather than as a public self-serve developer product. This API Evangelist profile was seeded as a portfolio-company lead (Anthemis) and enriched from Happy Money's public web presence; its lending API surface is partner-gated and not publicly documented.

providers.name: Jingle Pay
providers.description: Jingle Pay is a DFSA-regulated (Dubai Financial Services Authority) digital financial services fintech headquartered in the UAE, offering an all-in-one mobile money account for cross-border remittances, peer-to-peer payments, real-time multi-currency exchange, and Mastercard-powered card payments. Founded and led by CEO Amir Fardghassemi, the company serves the UAE, Pakistan, Bahrain, and Canada, and reports having processed over $3.5 billion across 8M+ transactions to 150 countries for 1.5M+ unique senders. It is backed by strategic partners and investors including Bank Alfalah, MoneyGram, Mastercard, and 500 Global. Jingle Pay operates as a consumer mobile app (iOS and Android) and does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal.

providers.name: Stablecore
providers.description: Stablecore provides digital-asset banking infrastructure that lets banks and credit unions offer stablecoins, tokenized deposits, digital-asset accounts and exchange, and digital-asset-based lending inside their existing core, digital-banking and compliance stacks. The platform targets cross-border payments, treasury management, digital-asset investing, crypto on/off-ramps and stablecoin sponsor banking, with a multi-provider design intended to avoid vendor lock-in and built-in compliance tooling. Stablecore is SOC 2 compliant and an ABA Partner Network member; investors include Coinbase Ventures, Norwest Venture Partners and Bank of Utah. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes a marketing and product site plus a blog, but no public developer portal, API documentation, OpenAPI, SDKs or GitHub organization.

providers.name: Texas Capital Bank
providers.description: Texas Capital Bank, National Association is the banking subsidiary of Texas Capital Bancshares, Inc. (NASDAQ: TCBI), a Dallas-headquartered full-service financial services firm founded in 1998 with roughly $31.5 billion in assets (FYE 2025). As a nationally chartered commercial bank it serves businesses, entrepreneurs, and institutions across Texas and the United States with commercial and business banking, treasury management, mortgage/warehouse finance, and investment banking. On the open-finance dimension the bank is relationship-first rather than developer-first: it markets treasury and ERP API integrations (including its ConnectNow embedded banking for Sage and NetSuite, direct platform integrations, and SFTP/XChange file transfer) but exposes them through partner onboarding with dedicated bankers, not a public self-serve developer portal. There is no public first-party developer portal, no downloadable OpenAPI/Swagger, and no self-serve API signup. Consumer account and transaction data is made available to permissioned third parties through the Finicity (Mastercard) aggregator rather than a first-party API, which is the honest posture for most US regional banks under the voluntary, fragmented US open-banking landscape (CFPB Section 1033 and the industry FDX standard).

providers.name: Warren
providers.description: Warren (Warren Investimentos e Gestao Patrimonial) is a Brazilian digital wealth-management and investment platform founded in 2017 and based in Porto Alegre. Regulated by Brazil's Central Bank, the CVM securities commission, and ANBIMA, Warren offers a goals-based, fee-only model spanning managed portfolios, ETFs, fixed income, global stocks, gold and crypto, private pension plans, life insurance, currency exchange, and business (PJ) accounts, plus a Warren for Business platform for investment professionals. It is backed by QED Investors, Ribbit Capital, and Citi Ventures. As of this enrichment pass Warren exposes no public developer API, documentation portal, or first-party SDK; its GitHub organization (warrenbrasil) contains internal engineering tooling and courseware rather than a consumer-facing API surface.

providers.name: Cholamandalam
providers.description: Cholamandalam Investment and Finance Company (Chola) is an Indian non-banking financial company (NBFC) headquartered in Chennai and part of the Murugappa Group (CIN L65993TN1978PLC007576). It provides lending across vehicle finance (commercial vehicles, cars, two-wheelers, three-wheelers, tractors and construction equipment), home loans and loan against property, SME/MSME and business loans, supply chain finance, gold loans, and consumer and personal loans through a branch network across India. No public developer portal, API documentation, or SDKs were found during enrichment; the company operates consumer/branch and mobile-app (Chola One) channels rather than a published developer program. Group affiliates include Chola Securities and the Gaadi Bazaar vehicle marketplace.

providers.name: ExpressSteuer (fka Express Group)
providers.description: ExpressSteuer (formerly Express Group) is a German tax-technology company, originally a Hamburg-based fintech backed by Insight Partners that offered an app-based, largely automated income-tax-return (Steuererklärung) service aimed at consumers and employees. The expresssteuer.de domain currently presents a German-language tax-information and guidance website (built on WordPress) covering income tax, self-employment, and everyday financial topics. No public developer program, API, SDK, or /.well-known/ discovery surface is published. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Insight Partners and added to the API Evangelist network as a company lead for enrichment.

providers.name: Fivestargroup
providers.description: Five Star Group (Five Star Business Finance) is an India-based non-banking financial company (NBFC) that provides small-business and mortgage loans to self-employed and underserved borrowers, primarily across southern India. Its public web presence is an investor-relations and customer-service portal covering board and management disclosures, financials, annual reports, NCD and SEBI (LODR) compliances, RBI policies, credit ratings, and investor grievance redressal, alongside customer tools such as a loan mobile app, online EMI payments, and NACH mandate cancellation. It is listed in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Norwest Venture Partners. No public developer program, API, or SDK was found during enrichment.

providers.name: SALARY HERO PTE. LTD
providers.description: Salary Hero is a Singapore-headquartered financial wellness and earned wage access (EWA) platform offered to employees through their employers. Its products include Salary on Demand (accessing earned wages before payday), budgeting and spending-tracking tools, savings accounts (a partnership with Dime offering 3% interest), and financial-literacy education covering debt management and investing. The service is delivered via iOS and Android apps and is provisioned by employers, integrating with existing payroll and HR systems. Salary Hero is a portfolio company of 500 Global. This profile was enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline; no public developer API, portal, or documentation surface was found.

providers.name: Veritasfin
providers.description: Veritas Finance Limited is a non-banking finance company (NBFC) in India focused on retail and micro, small and medium enterprise (MSME) lending to underserved and self-employed customers. Its lending products include MSME and business loans, loan against property, home loans, mortgage and working-capital finance, and used commercial vehicle loans, supported by an EMI calculator, branch network, online payment portals and an investor-relations and corporate-governance section. It was surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Norwest Venture Partners. Public probing of veritasfin.in finds a corporate financial-services website with no developer portal, documentation, or public API surface at this time.

providers.name: Columbia Bank
providers.description: Columbia Bank is an Oregon state-chartered commercial bank and the principal banking subsidiary of Columbia Banking System, Inc. (NASDAQ: COLB), a West Coast regional bank holding company headquartered in Tacoma, Washington with more than $50 billion in assets. The bank took the legal name "Columbia Bank" effective July 1, 2025, having previously operated as Umpqua Bank following the 2023 merger of Columbia Banking System and Umpqua Holdings Corporation. On the open-finance front, Columbia is one of the relatively few US regional banks to run a first-party developer surface: Columbia API Banking, a commercial and treasury-management integration product exposing capabilities such as book transfers, ACH file imports, positive pay, stop-payment and NSF management, lockbox management, transaction and statement search, check images, and real-time account balances in JSON and XML, backed by a production-ready SDK and the gated Columbia API Portal. That surface is commercial/ERP-oriented rather than a self-serve public developer portal, and consumer-permissioned data access is instead delivered through the Plaid aggregator. No documented FDX participation or published CFPB Section 1033 posture was found.

providers.name: FGL Holdings
providers.description: FGL Holdings is a major US corporation and Fortune 1000 company. The FGL Holdings API provides programmatic access to its platform services, data, and integrations for enterprise customers and partners.

providers.name: FT Cash
providers.description: FTCash (ftcash) is a Mumbai, India based financial services / fintech company focused on financial inclusion for micro-merchants and small and medium enterprises (SMEs). It provides digital payment acceptance and working-capital business loans to small offline retailers and merchants who are typically underserved by traditional banking, enabling them to accept digital payments and access short-term credit. FTCash was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global (500 Startups) and added to the API Evangelist network. At this time FTCash operates a public marketing website but publishes no public developer program, API documentation, or machine-readable API artifacts, so this profile is limited to verified company identity plus a live domain-security probe.

providers.name: LIMRA
providers.description: LIMRA is a member-based research and trade association for the life insurance and financial services industry, operating alongside LOMA under the LL Global umbrella. It provides industry research, sales and market data, benchmarking, experience studies, and professional development to member companies - primarily life insurers, annuity providers, and workplace benefits carriers. LIMRA does not operate a public developer API or developer portal. Its research, benchmarking, and experience-study data are delivered through the member-gated LIMRA.com portal, reports, and consortium programs rather than a programmatic interface. LIMRA's most API-relevant offering is the LIMRA Data Exchange (LDEx) Standards - free, industry-developed data exchange standards for workplace benefits (benefits enrollment management, benefits configuration management, and evidence of insurability) that define payloads in XML and JSON and, in recent releases, REST endpoints specified in OpenAPI 3.1. LDEx is a specification that insurance carriers and benefits administration platforms implement between themselves; LIMRA publishes the standard (registration required to download, membership not required) but does not host any live endpoints. This entry is an honest documentation stub kept for catalog completeness; it will be updated if LIMRA ever ships a hosted public API.

providers.name: SchoolsFirst FCU
providers.description: SchoolsFirst Federal Credit Union is a federally chartered, member-owned credit union headquartered in Tustin, California, serving educators and their families. Founded in 1934 as Orange County Teachers Credit Union, it is the largest credit union in California and one of the largest in the United States, with roughly $31.9 billion in assets, over 1.4 million members, and about 70 branches. It offers savings, checking, loans, mortgages, credit cards, and investment services. Like most US credit unions, SchoolsFirst runs no first-party public developer program: probes of developer.schoolsfirstfcu.org fail to resolve and /developers returns 404, and its api.schoolsfirstfcu.org host is the member online-banking login backend, not a documented API. Consumer-permissioned data access is available only through open-finance aggregators (Plaid, Finicity, MX, Akoya) rather than a direct API. No public FDX participation or CFPB Section 1033 data-access posture is documented at this time.

providers.name: Tweezr
providers.description: Tweezr is a system-intelligence platform for safe legacy change, helping banks and insurers understand and incrementally evolve legacy core systems without risky big-bang modernization. The platform maps mainframe and heritage codebases (COBOL, PL/I, CICS, IMS, DB2 z/OS, VSAM, IBM i RPG, Adabas/Natural) into a deterministic, queryable, cited model that grounds engineering teams and AI tools in what the code actually does before anything is changed. Tweezr deploys on-premise by default, is a member of the Banking Industry Architecture Network (BIAN), partners with 10x Banking, is distributed through AWS Marketplace and Microsoft AppSource, and is a Techstars portfolio company. Tweezr publishes no public API or developer program as of July 2026.

providers.name: SCENARIO-X GLOBAL HOLDING PTE. LTD.
providers.description: SCENARIO-X GLOBAL HOLDING PTE. LTD. (Scenario X) is a financial-technology company building an AI- and quantum-computing-powered platform for financial risk analysis, stress testing, and regulatory reporting. The integrated platform is organized into four modules — Scenario (adverse market-condition design), PPNR (Pre-Provision Net Revenue projection), Risk (market, counterparty, credit, and operational risk), and Console (financial-data aggregation) — plus a quantum-computing offering for predictive financial modeling. It serves banks, insurers, family offices, independent wealth managers, and commodity traders. Surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and tracked in the API Evangelist network; no public API or developer surface has been found to date.

providers.name: Amex Bank of Canada
providers.description: Amex Bank of Canada is the Canadian banking subsidiary of the American Express Company (United States), incorporated in 1990 and headquartered in the Toronto area (Markham, Ontario). It is a Schedule II bank under Canada's Bank Act — a foreign-bank subsidiary regulated by the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) and treated as a Category II small-and-medium-sized deposit-taking institution — and it issues American Express charge and credit cards to Canadian consumers and businesses. As a card-centric Schedule II bank, Amex Bank of Canada runs no first-party developer portal of its own; the global American Express developer platform at developer.americanexpress.com is operated by the U.S. parent (a separate profile), not by this Canadian entity. Canada's federal Consumer-Driven Banking (open-banking) framework, legislated in Budget 2024 and the 2024 Fall Economic Statement with the Financial Consumer Agency of Canada (FCAC) as overseer, is not yet operational, so consumer data access to Amex-Canada accounts today is voluntary and largely aggregator-based rather than served by a public first-party API. This is an identity/provider record; no public Canadian API surface is documented.

providers.name: CIBC Bank USA
providers.description: CIBC Bank USA is an Illinois state-chartered, FDIC-insured commercial bank (FDIC Cert #33306) headquartered at 120 South LaSalle Street in Chicago, Illinois. Formerly The PrivateBank and Trust Company, it was acquired in 2017 and rebranded, and today operates as a wholly owned US subsidiary of Canadian Imperial Bank of Commerce (CIBC) through the intermediate holding company CIBC Bancorp USA Inc. The bank focuses on commercial banking, capital markets, wealth management, trust services, private banking, and cross-border services for clients with North American operations, rather than mass-market retail. As a US regional institution, CIBC Bank USA publishes no first-party public developer portal or open API program; consumer-permissioned account and balance data is reached only through third-party aggregators such as Plaid, and the CIBC group has a data-access agreement with MX. It is not a documented direct Financial Data Exchange (FDX) participant and has published no explicit CFPB Section 1033 data-access posture, making its honest API surface aggregator-mediated only.

providers.name: Close Brothers
providers.description: Close Brothers Group plc (LSE: CBG) is a UK merchant banking group founded in 1878 and a constituent of the FTSE 250 Index, headquartered at 10 Crown Place, London EC2A 4FT. The group provides specialist lending across motor, premium, asset, invoice, and property finance; takes personal and business deposits through Close Brothers Savings; manages wealth through Close Brothers Asset Management; and trades securities through Winterflood. Its banking entity, Close Brothers Limited, is authorised by the Prudential Regulation Authority and regulated by the Financial Conduct Authority and the PRA. Close Brothers is not one of the CMA9 mandated banks; it offers savings and deposit products rather than online payment (current) accounts, and therefore carries no UK Open Banking (OBIE / PSD2) Read/Write or Open Data publishing obligation. As of this profile no public developer portal, Open Banking Open Data endpoint, or documented API surface could be confirmed for the group.

providers.name: Santander US
providers.description: Santander Bank, N.A. (santanderbank.com) is the US retail and commercial banking subsidiary of Spain's Banco Santander S.A., headquartered in Boston, Massachusetts. It is a nationally chartered bank (National Association, regulated by the OCC) operating a branch network across the Northeast US (Massachusetts, New Hampshire, Rhode Island, Connecticut, New York, New Jersey, Pennsylvania and Delaware), which positions it as a super-regional bank. Unlike UK and Australian institutions bound by mandated open-banking contracts, and unlike US banks such as Capital One or Chase that publish first-party developer portals, Santander Bank N.A. exposes no public, first-party developer API for its US retail franchise: developer.santanderbank.com does not resolve, and the site publishes no developers/API/open-banking pages. Consumer-permissioned data access in the US is available today through aggregators rather than a direct API — Plaid supports "Santander - Personal" (Assets, Auth, Balance and Transactions). Santander's UK developer portal (developer.santander.co.uk) and the group's Corporate & Investment Banking API marketplace (apimarket.santandercib.com) are operated by separate legal entities and are not the US retail bank's surface. This record is an honest identity profile of a super-regional bank whose US open-finance posture is aggregator-mediated, with no documented first-party developer program.

providers.name: Juvo
providers.description: Juvo is a San Francisco based fintech company, founded in 2014, that provides Financial Identity as a Service (FiDaaS). In partnership with mobile network operators, Juvo uses data science, machine learning, and game mechanics to analyze anonymous prepaid mobile subscriber behavior and build proprietary Identity Scores for the roughly 68% of adults worldwide who lack a formal credit history. Its Identity Stack exposes an API for carriers to derive customer analytics and insights, and powers airtime lending and cash-loan products. Juvo has built over 150 million financial profiles and works with operators and partners including Mastercard, Claro, T-Mobile, Vivo, and TIM across Latin America and beyond. Developer documentation is published on a Stoplight-hosted portal at developers.juvo.com.

providers.name: Petal
providers.description: Petal is a New York-based consumer fintech that issues Visa credit cards aimed at people with limited or no credit history, underwriting applicants from their bank-account cash flow (its proprietary CashScore metric) rather than a traditional credit score alone. Its Petal 1, Petal 1 Rise and Petal 2 cards are issued by WebBank, and the business is now part of the Tilt family of consumer finance brands (Tilt Card, Inc., NMLS #2295169). Petal reaches customers through iOS and Android apps plus a web dashboard and help center. It is a direct-to-consumer card issuer: as of this profile it operates no developer program, publishes no API documentation, and exposes no machine-readable API contract on any of its public hosts.

providers.name: Axiom Trust
providers.description: Axiom Trust Company is a vertically integrated trust company and technology platform serving investment advisors, attorneys, trustees, and private families. Founded in 2025 by David Meister and headquartered in Las Vegas, Nevada, Axiom pairs a regulated corporate trustee with a proprietary data-driven administration platform, using technology to remove the administrative bottleneck of traditional trust administration so named trust officers can focus on fiduciary judgment and family relationships. The company positions itself as infrastructure rather than a competitor for the client relationship: it acts as independent or directed trustee, handles bill pay, notices, distributions, approvals and principal & income accounting, and takes on complex mandates other institutions avoid — closely held entities, private investments, contested situations, and special needs trusts. Axiom raised $11.8M in pre-seed and seed funding led by Lightspeed Venture Partners, with Wischoff Ventures, Runa Capital, SNR, Primetime Partners, and Mercury founder Immad Akhund participating. As of this profile Axiom Trust publishes no public developer program, API documentation, or machine-readable API artifacts; its client-facing application is a private authenticated web app.

providers.name: COUNTRY Financial
providers.description: COUNTRY Financial is the marketing name for an Illinois-headquartered family of affiliated insurance and financial services companies that includes COUNTRY Life Insurance Company, COUNTRY Mutual Insurance Company, COUNTRY Casualty Insurance Company, COUNTRY Preferred Insurance Company, and related subsidiaries based in Bloomington, IL. Founded in 1925 by Illinois Agricultural Association members, COUNTRY today offers auto, home, life, farm, crop, and commercial insurance along with investment, retirement planning, and trust services through a captive agent network in 19 U.S. states. COUNTRY does not publish a public developer API; partner and agency integrations occur through internal agency systems.

providers.name: First Data (Fiserv)
providers.description: First Data was a global payment technology solutions company providing merchant transaction processing, financial institution services, and prepaid services before merging with Fiserv in 2019. Legacy First Data API products including Payeezy, Bolt, and Commerce Hub are now part of the Fiserv developer portal.

providers.name: Heartland Financial USA
providers.description: Heartland Financial USA is a major US corporation and Fortune 1000 company. The Heartland Financial USA API provides programmatic access to its platform services, data, and integrations for enterprise customers and partners.

providers.name: Jenfi
providers.description: Jenfi is a Singapore-headquartered SME credit platform for digitally-enabled businesses in Southeast Asia, operating principally in Singapore and Vietnam. Founded in 2019 by Jeffrey Liu and Justin Louie and backed by Y Combinator, Monk's Hill Ventures and Headline, it started with revenue-based financing — non-dilutive growth capital repaid as a percentage of monthly revenue rather than on a fixed schedule — and has since broadened into growth financing, working capital and supply-chain financing, alongside a B2B buy-now-pay-later product marketed as PaidFi ("b2b BNPL by Jenfi"). In May 2026 the company reported passing US$100 million in cumulative originations across more than 2,400 financings, from over 30,000 evaluated enquiries. Jenfi publishes no public developer portal, API reference, or machine-readable contract: its only integration surface is a login-gated partner console at partners.jenfi.com and a contact-sales "Embedded Financing" offer on its partner page.

providers.name: Bread Financial
providers.description: Bread Financial is a technology-driven financial services company offering white-label buy now pay later (BNPL), installment financing, and branded credit card products for merchants. The platform processes $27 billion in annual sales volume for 35.6 million active customers. Bread Pay enables merchants to embed financing options directly into their checkout flow for both online and in-store purchases, including installment plans (Bread Pay) and short-term split payment options (SplitPay).

providers.name: Jefferies Financial Group
providers.description: Jefferies Financial Group is a leading global, full-service investment banking and capital markets firm providing advisory, capital raising, sales, trading, research, wealth management, and alternative asset management services to clients across the Americas, Europe, the Middle East, and the Asia-Pacific.

providers.name: LTSE
providers.description: The Long-Term Stock Exchange (LTSE) is a U.S. national securities exchange, approved by the SEC, built to help companies and investors focus on long-term value creation over short-term results. LTSE operates a stock exchange and trading platform with listing standards organized around five long-term principles covering stakeholders, strategy, executive compensation, board governance, and investor engagement. The company also publishes market and governance insights and produces The Eric Ries Show podcast. LTSE previously offered a cap-table management product (LTSE Equity, formerly Captable.io) which has since been sunset and transitioned to Astrella. LTSE exposes no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; this profile captures its public web and security posture.

providers.name: Primerica
providers.description: Primerica is a major US corporation and Fortune 1000 company. The Primerica API provides programmatic access to its platform services, data, and integrations for enterprise customers and partners.

providers.name: IKF Finance
providers.description: IKF Finance Limited is an India-based non-banking financial company (NBFC) that has provided asset financing for more than 35 years through a network of 300+ branches pan-India, serving over one lakh customers. Its lending products include commercial vehicle loans, construction equipment loans, tractor loans, car and MUV loans, and MSME and business loans, with home loans offered through the affiliated IKF Home Finance entity. Operating under the tagline "Powering Progress with Prompt Financing," the company focuses on prompt, accessible credit for transport operators, small businesses, and individuals across India. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio lead and enriched with public identity, legal, and domain-security signals; IKF Finance publishes no public developer/API surface.

providers.name: Plumery
providers.description: Plumery is an Amsterdam, Netherlands-based fintech that provides a headless, mobile-first digital banking engagement platform it markets as the "Digital Success Fabric" — a "Digital Engagement Platform for Banks." It lets banks, credit unions, and financial institutions build and launch branded mobile and web banking experiences on top of their existing core banking systems, delivered to engineering teams as an API-first, composable platform with SDKs and developer documentation (built on the Stainless docs/SDK toolchain). Plumery maintains a public GitHub organization of supporting engineering tooling and publishes a security & compliance program (SOC 2, ISO 27001). The company is backed by QED Investors and Seedcamp.

providers.name: Voya Financial
providers.description: Voya Financial (NYSE: VOYA) is a leading health, wealth, and investment company serving approximately 14.7 million individual, workplace, and institutional clients. Voya specializes in retirement plans, group employee benefits, health savings accounts (HSAs), and investment management. Their myVoyage platform integrates financial wellness tools to help participants plan, invest, and protect their financial futures. Voya does not offer a public developer API but provides account connectivity through open banking aggregators such as Plaid.

providers.name: Core10
providers.description: Core10, Inc. is a U.S.-based fintech software development and API integration firm founded in 2016 by Lee Farabaugh and Jeff Martin, headquartered in Franklin, Tennessee with delivery centers in Martin, Tennessee and Huntington, West Virginia, built on a domestic-outsourcing model it trademarked as Hereshore(R). Core10 wrote custom software, core-banking integrations and API layers for community banks, credit unions and fintechs, and acquired Accrue Technologies in 2021 to add a Salesforce-based digital lending, account opening and treasury onboarding platform. In January 2024 it spun its implementation practice out as Monarch, and the Core10 brand has since been retired: core10.io now 301-redirects to monarchfts.com, where Monarch operates as an Intapp DealCloud implementation, configuration and managed-services consultancy for private capital firms, while the Accrue platform trades independently at getaccrue.com under its own leadership. Core10 built API integrations for other companies for nearly a decade but never published a developer program, public API, SDK or machine-readable contract of its own, and as of 2026-08-11 neither successor brand does either.

providers.name: Home Trust
providers.description: Home Trust Company is a federally regulated Canadian trust company founded in 1977 and headquartered in Toronto, and the principal operating subsidiary of Home Capital Group. Home Capital was taken private by Smith Financial Corporation (Stephen Smith) in 2023, and the group now spans Home Trust, Home Bank (a Schedule I bank), Fairstone Bank, and the Oaken Financial deposit brand, positioning itself as one of Canada's leading alternative (non-prime) lenders. Its products include residential and commercial mortgages, reverse mortgages, Equityline, Preferred and Secured Visa credit cards, and Oaken GIC and high-interest savings deposits. Home Trust operates no public developer portal or first-party API: developer.hometrust.ca and api.hometrust.ca do not resolve (DNS NXDOMAIN), no downloadable OpenAPI/Swagger is published, and no Interac e-Transfer or Payments Canada Real-Time Rail (RTR) API surface is documented. Canada's federal Consumer-Driven Banking (open-banking) framework is legislated (Budget 2024 / Fall Economic Statement 2024, FCAC as overseer) but not yet operational, and Home Trust publishes no stated CDB or FDX position; any consumer data access today would be via screen-scraping aggregators such as Flinks or Plaid rather than a first-party API. This is an identity-only record: no public API exists as of July 2026.

providers.name: Spring Labs
providers.description: Spring Labs is an AI-native compliance and customer-experience platform for financial institutions, deploying autonomous AI agents that complete operational work rather than only surfacing insights. Its agents score customer-service calls, run 100% QA/QC review coverage, identify and file complaints, and (soon) automate the dispute lifecycle, alongside SummerGRC, an AI-driven governance, risk, and compliance product. Spring Labs targets sponsor banks, fintech lenders, enterprise banks, BaaS platforms, and debt-collection (ARM) organizations. Originally a blockchain-based data and identity company backed by Multicoin Capital, the firm has repositioned around applied AI for regulated financial operations. This profile was surfaced from a VC portfolio and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline; the company publishes a marketing/product site but no public API, developer portal, or SDKs at this time.

providers.name: Arro
providers.description: Arro is a consumer fintech company that helps people build or rebuild credit without traditional barriers. Its flagship product is the Arro Card, a Mastercard with no deposit and no hard credit check that starts at up to $300 and grows to $2,500, issued by Community Federal Savings Bank (member FDIC). The Arro app pairs the card with financial-education lessons, credit tracking, personalized guidance, and Artie, an AI money coach. Arro is a mobile-first consumer product and does not publish a public developer API, OpenAPI, or developer portal at this time.

providers.name: Diametric Capital
providers.description: Diametric Capital is an equity long/short, multi-manager investment fund firm headquartered in Boston and New York. The firm builds customizable funds that isolate what it calls "True Alpha" — returns uncorrelated to the broader market — by removing beta and factor risk exposure to deliver performance with below-average volatility. Alongside its funds it offers aligned fee structures, capital partnerships, and business development support to entrepreneurs and emerging managers. Diametric Capital is a private financial firm and does not publish a public developer program, API, or SDK surface; it operates a secure client data room for investors and partners.

providers.name: East West Bancorp
providers.description: East West Bancorp is a major US corporation and Fortune 1000 company. The East West Bancorp API provides programmatic access to its platform services, data, and integrations for enterprise customers and partners.

providers.name: ELV8
providers.description: ELV8 Inc. operates Scout, a financial platform built for college athletes and athletic departments navigating Name, Image, and Likeness (NIL) income. Scout provides NIL income tracking and management, financial education with one-on-one coaching, payment processing for schools (per diems, bonuses, and NIL payments), roster cap-management and compliance tooling, and business-setup assistance such as LLC formation and tax filing. ELV8 Inc. is an SEC-registered investment adviser and works with 30-plus college athletic programs serving thousands of athletes. It was surfaced as a Techstars-backed portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network. Scout is a consumer/institutional fintech product and does not currently publish a public developer API, SDKs, or API documentation.

providers.name: Glacier Bancorp
providers.description: Glacier Bancorp is a major US corporation and Fortune 1000 company. The Glacier Bancorp API provides programmatic access to its platform services, data, and integrations for enterprise customers and partners.

providers.name: KKR
providers.description: KKR & Co. Inc. is a leading global investment firm offering solutions in alternative assets spanning real estate, private credit, private equity, and infrastructure, as well as liquid credit, capital markets and insurance. KKR does not currently publish a public developer portal or open API program; this repository tracks the company in the API Evangelist Network for context, common properties, and future developer resource discovery.

providers.name: MouseCat
providers.description: MouseCat is an agentic AI infrastructure company for risk operations, founded in 2026 and a graduate of the Y Combinator Winter 2026 batch. The platform runs human-quality fraud investigations to help risk teams automatically detect, investigate, and mitigate emerging fraud, scale investigations, build better models, and make faster decisions. MouseCat deploys entirely within customer-owned cloud environments, integrating with the data, vendors, and APIs a risk team already relies on so companies retain complete control of sensitive data. The company was founded by Nicholas Aldridge (CEO) and Joseph McAllister (CTO) and is backed by Y Combinator, Imagination Capital, and SurgePoint Capital. As of this profile MouseCat is an early-stage startup with a public marketing site and a private application; it publishes no public API, SDK, developer documentation, or MCP server yet.

providers.name: Palus Finance
providers.description: Palus Finance is a Y Combinator (Winter 2026) financial-advisory startup that acts as a startup's outsourced financial advisor and Registered Investment Advisor (RIA) with a fiduciary duty to its clients. Palus automatically manages a company's reserve cash and treasury, sweeping idle balances into NVCA-compliant bond portfolios built from U.S. government securities and T-Bills to optimize yield (targeting roughly a SOFR + 1% spread) while preserving safety and liquidity. It connects to a company's existing bank accounts (via Plaid) rather than requiring an account switch, sizes allocations against runway and burn rate, and can be set up in under ten minutes with no minimums or lockups. Palus is a managed, human-plus-software advisory product delivered through its web application; it does not currently publish a public developer API, SDKs, or developer documentation.

providers.name: South State Corporation
providers.description: South State Corporation is a major US corporation and Fortune 1000 company. The South State Corporation API provides programmatic access to its platform services, data, and integrations for enterprise customers and partners.

providers.name: Synovus Financial
providers.description: Synovus Financial is a major US corporation and Fortune 1000 company. The Synovus Financial API provides programmatic access to its platform services, data, and integrations for enterprise customers and partners.

providers.name: Tilt
providers.description: Tilt is a consumer fintech mobile app for building and rebuilding credit. It offers cash advances of up to $400, a line of credit with potential limit increases, and three credit cards (Essentials, Motion, and Engage), evaluating applicants from real-time bank-linked financial data rather than credit history alone. The app adds credit-score monitoring with personalized tips, customizable budgeting and spend tracking, AI-assisted automatic savings, and on-time-payment rewards, for an $8/month subscription after a 14-day trial. Tilt is a consumer application with no public developer API surface at this time.

providers.name: Titan Invest
providers.description: Titan (titan.com), operating the brand Titan Invest, is a wealth management firm founded in 2017 and headquartered in New York City that serves high-performing technology professionals. Titan combines AI-assisted technology with dedicated human wealth teams to deliver actively managed portfolios, direct indexing and equity-diversification strategies, tax planning, and financial advisory for pre- and post-IPO tech employees, charging a 0.4% annual advisory fee. The company reports managing roughly $1.2B in assets for more than 10,000 clients and is backed by General Catalyst. Titan delivers its service through consumer web and mobile applications and advisor relationships; it does not publish a public developer API, SDKs, or a developer portal, so this profile captures the company identity and domain-security posture rather than an API surface.

providers.name: TomoCredit
providers.description: TomoCredit is a consumer fintech that helps people build credit without requiring a credit score or prior credit history. Its flagship products are the Tomo Card, a credit-building card marketed as an all-new black card, and TomoBoost, an AI-powered credit-building tool. The company positions itself around fast approval (apply in minutes), no credit-history requirement, and cardmember benefits and coverage it values at over $1,300, aiming to help thin-file consumers such as newcomers and students establish and grow their credit. TomoCredit was surfaced through the Techstars portfolio and added to the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Tongdun
providers.description: Tongdun (同盾科技 / Tongdun Technology) is a Hangzhou-based intelligent risk-control and anti-fraud analytics company whose public product presence now operates under the 小盾未来 (Xiaodun Future) brand at xiaodun.com. It uses AI and intelligent-analysis techniques to predict and score fraud and credit risk across consumer lending, banking, insurance, and e-commerce, delivering decisioning, anti-fraud, and risk-management capabilities to financial institutions, small-loan and consumer-finance lenders, auto finance, and internet businesses. Its risk-control services are consumed as enterprise interfaces (风控接口) provisioned behind account registration and sales onboarding; there is no public self-serve developer portal, OpenAPI, or SDK registry surface exposed at this time. This record was surfaced as a portfolio company of Qiming Venture Partners and enriched from the company's live public web presence.

providers.name: TransFS
providers.description: TransFS (Transparent Financial Services, LLC) is the Chicago fintech that operated FeeFighters, a marketplace helping small and medium-sized businesses compare credit-card processors and reduce merchant-account fees. It also built the Samurai payment gateway, a developer-facing API for tokenizing cards and processing payments. FeeFighters was acquired by Groupon in March 2012 and folded into Groupon Payments / the Merchant Operating System, after which the Samurai gateway API was retired. The feefighters.com domain today operates as a credit-card fee-negotiation and chargeback-management consultancy under the FeeFighters name, promising fee reductions without switching processors; it publishes no public API, developer portal, or machine-readable API definition.

providers.name: Umpqua Holdings
providers.description: Umpqua Holdings is a major US corporation and Fortune 1000 company. The Umpqua Holdings API provides programmatic access to its platform services, data, and integrations for enterprise customers and partners.

providers.name: Western Alliance Bancorporation
providers.description: Western Alliance Bancorporation is a major US corporation and Fortune 1000 company. The Western Alliance Bancorporation API provides programmatic access to its platform services, data, and integrations for enterprise customers and partners.

providers.name: Globe Life
providers.description: Globe Life is a major US corporation and Fortune 1000 company. The Globe Life API provides programmatic access to its platform services, data, and integrations for enterprise customers and partners.

providers.name: Porters
providers.description: Porters is an AI-native outsourcing partner for European banking operations. Its platform uses AI agents with human oversight to automate high-volume back-office banking processes — account seizure processing (private and public account seizures), insolvency case management from intake to resolution, and chargeback dispute data collection, triage, and resolution. Documents are ingested, extracted, and classified; decisions are made with a human in the loop; and banking actions plus audit reports are generated automatically. Porters hosts data in the EU in line with GDPR, maintains 24/7 audit trails, and does not use customer data for model training. It was founded by veterans of McKinsey, Qonto, Upvest, Solaris, and Roland Berger, and is backed by Earlybird and Seedcamp. No public developer API is currently published.

providers.name: AXA
providers.description: AXA is a French multinational insurance firm and one of the world's largest providers of life, health, property & casualty, and asset management services. AXA does not publish a single global developer portal; technology integration is delivered through country-specific broker and partner portals, AXA Partners B2B2C distribution channels, AXA XL specialty insurance APIs for commercial brokers, and ACORD / EDI standards used across the insurance industry.

providers.name: Principly
providers.description: Principly, Inc. is an SEC-registered investment adviser that operates the consumer fintech product Backer (backer.com), a mobile-first platform for opening and managing 529 education savings plans. Backer lets parents open a 529 plan in minutes, automate contributions, and share custom gifting links so family and friends can contribute to a child's college fund. The service helps families choose among more than 100 U.S. 529 plans, reporting 250K+ users and $70M+ saved. It is a consumer-facing mobile and web application and does not publish a public developer API, documentation, or SDKs. Principly is backed by 500 Global and was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company.

providers.name: Syscap
providers.description: Syscap is a Monterrey-based Mexican financial technology company that provides a private-credit and funding-management platform for non-bank financial intermediaries (SOFOMs and financieras). Its software helps loan originators manage funding lines, organize documentation, automate tax compliance, generate amortization tables and electronic signatures, and give funders a 24/7 transparency portal with balance reports and transaction tracking. More than 140 financial institutions across Mexico use Syscap to manage private debt. The company operates a web application and a mobile app; it does not publish a public API, developer portal, or API documentation.

providers.name: Equator Principles
providers.description: The Equator Principles is a risk management framework adopted by financial institutions for determining, assessing, and managing environmental and social risk in project finance transactions. It provides a minimum standard for due diligence and monitoring to support responsible risk decision-making and is primarily intended to provide a minimum standard for due diligence and monitoring in project finance and related advisory activities.

providers.name: Willow Wealth
providers.description: Willow Wealth Inc. - formerly Yieldstreet - is a New York City financial technology company that operates an online private-markets investing platform, giving accredited and retail investors access to alternative asset classes including real estate, private credit, private equity, art, legal finance, and third-party evergreen funds from institutional managers. Founded in 2015 by Milind Mehere and Michael Weisz, the platform reports more than 500,000 members and over $6 billion in cumulative investments, and renamed itself Willow Wealth in late 2025. Investors reach it through a web portal and iOS/Android apps; the company publishes no public developer program, API reference, or machine-readable specification.

providers.name: Alpharank
providers.description: Alpharank is a no-code sales guidance and digital-origination analytics platform for banks and credit unions. It analyzes funded loan and deposit applications to reveal which marketing tactics, channels, and campaigns actually drive funded dollars, then guides institutions to optimize their online branch, curb funnel abandonment, and turn ad spend into higher-quality leads. Its products include Optimizer, AdSync, and CRMSync, and it serves roughly 200 financial institutions nationwide. Originally recognized for turning payment transaction data into customer influence graphs, Alpharank is a 500 Startups / 500 Global portfolio company. As of this enrichment pass Alpharank publishes a marketing and client-login presence but no public developer portal, API reference, or OpenAPI surface.

providers.name: Arca
providers.description: Arca (Arca Financial, Inc.) is an AI-native wealth management company founded by former Plaid product leader Rron Rexha and headquartered in New York. It pairs human financial advisors with a fully integrated, agentic platform in which AI agents are the primary operational users: monitoring emails, calls, documents, market data, and news, coordinating with one another, generating dynamic user interfaces, and executing multi-step advisory workflows so advisors can focus on client relationships. Arca is an SEC-registered investment adviser managing over $1 billion in client assets, and raised $64M across a seed round (led by Venrock) and a Series A (led by General Catalyst, with Index Ventures and Venrock).
