It has no public developer API surface at this time; this profile captures its public identity and security posture.

providers.name: Fairbanc
providers.description: Fairbanc (PT Fairbanc Technologies Indonesia) is a Jakarta-based digital finance platform that uses AI/ML-powered credit scoring to deliver embedded, revolving supply-chain financing and buy-now-pay-later "terms of payment" to micro, small, and medium enterprises (MSMEs) across Indonesia. Working with trusted financial institutions and distributor/supply-chain ecosystems, Fairbanc provides merchants with an instant digital facility limit and short-term working-capital liquidity at the point of purchase — with no formal loan application, smartphone, or app required — plus data intelligence and consulting that help distributors reduce bad-debt risk and grow transaction value. The company reports its terms-of-payment product drove roughly 35% distributor sales growth. This is a company profile in the API Evangelist network; Fairbanc publishes a consumer-facing marketing and onboarding site but no public developer/API program at this time.

providers.name: Lexyom
providers.description: Lexyom (Lexyom LLP) is a law firm operating at lexyom.com, which redirects to lexyomlaw.com. The firm markets legal services to financial-services companies: financial institution setup, company registration, broker licensing, proprietary-trading ("prop firm") licensing, trademark registration and IP protection, retainer representation, and contract drafting and review. Published offices are New York (450 Park Avenue) and Dubai (DIFC Gate Village), with stated emphasis on US and MENA cross-border regulation. The public web property is a client-rendered single-page application with a marketing site, a blog, a news section, a "Become a Client" intake flow, and an authenticated client portal (matters, contracts, documents, invoices, trademarks). Lexyom publishes no public API, developer portal, API documentation, SDKs, or machine-readable specifications as of this enrichment pass.

providers.name: MeridianLink
providers.description: MeridianLink provides a powerful web service enabling software applications to retrieve consumer credit data in XML format. It offers lending and credit platform solutions for financial institutions.

providers.name: Randolph-Brooks FCU
providers.description: Randolph-Brooks Federal Credit Union (RBFCU) is a member-owned, not-for-profit federal credit union headquartered in Live Oak, Texas, federally insured by the NCUA and serving more than one million members across Texas and beyond. Chartered as a federal credit union rather than a state or national bank, RBFCU is one of the largest credit unions in the United States by membership and assets, offering retail banking, mortgages, auto loans, credit cards, and deposit products through branches and digital channels. As a member-focused retail institution, RBFCU publishes no first-party public developer program, API documentation, or downloadable OpenAPI/Swagger specifications; consumer-permissioned account data is reached through third-party aggregators (such as Plaid, MX, Finicity, or Akoya) rather than a directly documented open-finance API, and it publishes no stated CFPB Section 1033 data-access posture or documented FDX participation.

providers.name: SoLo Funds
providers.description: SoLo Funds is a Techstars-backed, Los Angeles fintech that operates a community-driven peer-to-peer lending marketplace delivered as a consumer mobile app for iOS and Android. Members request small, short-term loans that other members choose to fund, with borrowers offering an optional tip and donation rather than mandated interest, positioning the platform as a member-to-member alternative to payday and overdraft borrowing. SoLo Funds is a consumer financial-services product and does not publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; its only publicly reachable operational surface is a hosted status page.

providers.name: Silvur
providers.description: Silvur (Silvur Technology Services, Inc.) is a white-label financial-wellness platform that helps credit unions and financial institutions deliver personalized retirement education and planning tools to their members and customers. Its patent-pending Retirement Score answers "how long will their money last in retirement?" and its SmartDraw technology generates personalized recommendations across Social Security, Medicare, retirement savings, and state-specific planning. Institutions launch a fully branded retirement website in weeks and use it to educate members and market financial products such as loans, mortgages, and insurance against the multi-trillion-dollar retirement wallet. Silvur is a venture-backed fintech (Anthemis portfolio). As of this enrichment pass Silvur publishes only a marketing site with legal and support pages and exposes no public developer portal, API reference, SDKs, or webhooks.

providers.name: Apollo Global Management
providers.description: Apollo Global Management is a global alternative investment manager providing private equity, credit, and real assets strategies to institutional and individual investors. With over $840 billion in assets under management, Apollo focuses on delivering excess returns through its private equity, credit, and real assets business segments. Apollo does not have a public developer API program.

providers.name: Dayforward
providers.description: Dayforward is a New York-based life insurance technology and services group founded in 2019 by Aaron Shapiro. It owns Commercial Travelers Life Insurance Company (NY-domiciled carrier) and Dayforward Insurance Agency LLC (licensed in all 50 states), and sells income-replacement term life insurance direct to consumers at dayforward.com. Since pivoting to B2B at dayforward.io it licenses Workbench — a SaaS platform covering the full life insurance lifecycle from agent selling and automated underwriting through policy administration and service — plus managed distribution, underwriting and administration services to other carriers and distributors. Workbench is marketed as including "APIs, plug-and-play widgets, single sign-on support, and robust administration tools", but Dayforward publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, OpenAPI definition or SDKs.

providers.name: ATB Financial
providers.description: ATB Financial (formerly Alberta Treasury Branches) is a financial institution and Crown corporation wholly owned by the Government of Alberta, established in 1938 and operating under the provincial ATB Financial Act rather than the federal Bank Act. Headquartered in Edmonton, it is Alberta's largest home-grown financial institution and the largest public bank in North America, with roughly C$64 billion in assets, more than 800,000 customers, about 5,000 team members, and 300+ branches and agencies across the province; deposits are guaranteed by the Province of Alberta rather than covered by CDIC. On the open-finance front, ATB does NOT operate a public first-party developer portal or documented public API surface (developer.atb.com returns HTTP 404), and Canada's federal Consumer-Driven Banking framework (legislated in Budget 2024 and the Fall Economic Statement 2024, with the FCAC as overseer) is not yet operational. Consumer financial-data access to ATB today is therefore voluntary and aggregator-mediated — reached through third-party aggregators such as Finicity (by Mastercard) and Flinks rather than a direct bank API.

providers.name: First Tech Federal Credit Union
providers.description: First Tech Federal Credit Union is a federally chartered, member-owned, not-for-profit financial cooperative headquartered in San Jose, California, and one of the largest credit unions in the United States. It was founded to serve employees of the technology industry and their families, and its membership is drawn heavily from workers at major technology employers. As an NCUA-insured credit union, First Tech offers consumer and business deposit accounts, lending, mortgages, credit cards, and wealth services delivered primarily through its website and mobile apps. Like the vast majority of US credit unions, First Tech publishes no first-party public developer portal or documented open API; consumer-permissioned financial data sharing is handled through third-party data aggregators (such as Plaid, MX, Finicity, and Akoya) rather than a directly documented first-party API surface. US open finance is voluntary and fragmented — the Financial Data Exchange (FDX) standard and the CFPB Section 1033 Personal Financial Data Rights rule are still emerging — and no first-party FDX-conformant data-access API or published Section 1033 posture was found for First Tech during this review.

providers.name: Proximitty
providers.description: Proximitty is a Y Combinator-backed company building an AI operating system for commercial lending. Its platform deploys regulator-grade AI agents that ingest and parse borrower documents, spread financials, generate credit memos, automate loan operations, and continuously track covenants and closing obligations for FDIC-insured banks, credit unions, and non-bank lenders originating C&I, CRE, and SBA loans. The system is designed to align with SR 11-7 and OCC guidance on AI governance and third-party risk, and claims to compress underwriting from weeks to minutes while enabling loan closures in under ten days. Proximitty publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI specification, SDK, or developer portal; it is delivered as a hosted SaaS product, and its public surface is limited to a marketing site, blog, security/compliance page, and a hosted Trust Center.

providers.name: Fidelity National Information Services (FIS)
providers.description: Fidelity National Information Services (FIS) is a global provider of financial services technology offering solutions across retail and institutional banking, payments, asset and wealth management, risk and compliance, and outsourcing. FIS exposes APIs to financial institutions, fintechs, and corporates through its Code Connect API marketplace.

providers.name: MultiLynq
providers.description: MultiLynq is a fixed income trading technology company founded in 2018 by Patrick Scheideler and Scott Collins and based in Shrewsbury, New Jersey. It sells market integration as a service: a single high-performance API that normalizes the messaging and trading protocols of every major and emerging electronic U.S. fixed income trading venue — including MarketAxess, Tradeweb, Trumid, Bloomberg, ICE Bonds, LTX by Broadridge, Liquidnet, Octaura, TMC Bonds and Bonds.com — into one interface for credit, municipal bond and loan trading. The platform covers pre- and post-trade workflows including price dissemination, market data aggregation, RFQ negotiation, portfolio trading, auction mechanisms, quoting conventions, smart order routing, and post-trade reporting and reconciliation, delivered as a fully hosted solution in which clients establish a single physical connection to a MultiLynq data center while MultiLynq maintains all upstream venue connectivity. The company has raised funding from Citadel Securities and Jane Street. The API is the entire product, but it is sold and onboarded through a sales conversation: MultiLynq publishes no public developer portal, documentation, specification, SDK or pricing.

providers.name: BOK Financial
providers.description: BOK Financial Corporation (NASDAQ: BOKF) is a regional financial-services holding company headquartered in Tulsa, Oklahoma, delivering banking under the Bank of Oklahoma, Bank of Texas, and BOK Financial brands across the Southwest and Midwest, along with wealth management and commercial treasury services. As of July 2026 it does not publish a first-party public developer portal or any documented API products — developer.bokfinancial.com does not resolve and /developer and /api return 404. Its public, machine-accessible surface is consumer-permissioned account data access delivered through third-party aggregators (Plaid coverage confirmed), while commercial treasury and ERP connectivity is offered privately to clients under contract rather than through a self-serve documented developer program.

providers.name: Comerica
providers.description: Comerica Incorporated is a Texas-headquartered super-regional financial services holding company providing retail, small-business, commercial, and wealth-management banking across the United States, with market concentrations in Texas, California, Michigan, Arizona, and Florida. As of July 2026 Comerica publishes NO first-party developer API portal: developer.comerica.com, api.comerica.com, and related developer subdomains do not resolve, and directory trackers (Open Banking Tracker, API Tracker) list no documented API products, OpenAPI/Swagger specs, SDKs, or Postman collections. Consumer and small-business account data is reached indirectly through US open-finance aggregators (Plaid, MX, Finicity, Akoya) and through Financial Data Exchange (FDX) APIs — the CFPB-recognized standard-setting body for the Section 1033 Personal Financial Data Rights rule — rather than a Comerica-published endpoint. Commercial treasury, cash-positioning, ACH/wire initiation, and reporting are delivered through Comerica's Cash Management and Commercial Information Management platforms under direct customer contract (host-to-host files, portal, and BAI/ISO 20022 feeds), not a public REST API. Note: Fifth Third Bancorp completed its all-stock acquisition of Comerica in February 2026, so Comerica's future digital and API surface is being integrated into Fifth Third's platform.

providers.name: Cullen/Frost Bankers
providers.description: Cullen/Frost Bankers is a major US corporation and Fortune 1000 company. The Cullen/Frost Bankers API provides programmatic access to its platform services, data, and integrations for enterprise customers and partners.

providers.name: Fintech Farm
providers.description: Fintech Farm is a London-based fintech company that builds and operates credit-led digital banks (neobanks) in emerging markets in partnership with licensed local banks. Founded in 2020 by Dmytro Dubilet (co-founder of Monobank), Nick Bezkrovnyy and Oleksandr Vityaz, the company supplies an end-to-end stack — mobile banking apps, an AI-driven credit engine and credit-risk models, customer acquisition and retention programs, and customer service operations — and is compensated on the performance of the resulting bank. Its launches include Leobank in Azerbaijan, Liobank in Vietnam, Simbank with DosCredoBank in Kyrgyzstan, Roarbank with Unity Bank in India, Tez with Hamkorbank in Uzbekistan, and Credit+ in Morocco. Fintech Farm is a business-to-business bank-partnership provider and publishes no public developer program, API documentation or machine-readable API contract; its integration surface is delivered privately to partner banks.

providers.name: Nexu
providers.description: Nexu is a Mexico City fintech that provides automotive financing at the point of sale. Founded in 2014 by Abdon Nacif and Fernando Gomez Arriola, the company began as an auto price and comparison site and now operates a digital lending platform used by car dealerships across Mexico to originate credit and leasing offers in real time. Nexu underwrites and funds two consumer products - credito automotriz (auto credit) and arrendamiento (leasing with a purchase option and no residual), distributed through partnerships with more than ten OEM dealer networks including Nissan, Volkswagen, Kia, Hyundai, Mazda, Honda, Ford, Chevrolet, BMW and Audi. Applicants complete an onboarding and identity flow in a browser application at nexu.mx and receive a decision without visiting a branch. The company has raised roughly $73M across five equity rounds, plus debt facilities, from Valor Capital Group, Altos Ventures, Wollef, Architect Capital, Clocktower, Tresalia Capital, FJ Labs, Gilgamesh Ventures and others. As of this profiling pass Nexu publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK or machine-readable contract of any kind - see x-coverage below.

providers.name: Amparo
providers.description: Amparo is a Brazilian fintech that supports bereaved families in the days after a funeral. Its Central de Cadastros uses automated document reading and data extraction to register a family once and share that data across partner systems, while a WhatsApp assistant delivers personalized financial guidance covering INSS pension advances, life-insurance payouts, credit, repatriation reimbursements, and debt and inventory organization. Amparo exposes integration APIs so its Central de Cadastros can connect with funeral-home and insurer client systems. Backed by QED Investors.

providers.name: CNO Financial Group
providers.description: CNO Financial Group is an Indiana-based insurance holding company that develops, markets, and administers life and health insurance, annuities, and workforce benefits solutions through brands including Bankers Life, Colonial Penn, Washington National, Optavise, and PMA USA. CNO does not publish a public-facing developer portal or API; integrations are run via partner channels (CRM, Pega Cloud platform, and brand-specific producer portals).

providers.name: Oxyzo
providers.description: Oxyzo Financial Services is an RBI-registered Non-Banking Financial Company (NBFC) providing customized SME and corporate financing across India. Founded as the lending arm of the OfBusiness group, Oxyzo offers purchase finance, work order finance, invoice discounting, vendor finance, business loans, machinery finance, and loan against property, serving industries such as auto manufacturing, capital goods, e-mobility, logistics, pharmaceuticals, and textiles. The company operates 145+ branches, has powered 10,000+ businesses, disbursed over Rs 77,000 crore, and holds A+ ratings from CRISIL and ICRA. Oxyzo publishes no public developer/API surface; this profile captures its identity and domain-security posture for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Zypl
providers.description: Zypl (zypl.ai) is an AI company building synthetic-data and machine-learning technology for financial services and government. Its core is proprietary zGAN generative synthetic-data technology, delivered through Lucid, a no-code platform for developing and deploying robust scoring models. Products include zScore for credit decisioning, plus fraud detection, collection scoring, and IFRS-9/GAAP-compliant provisioning for credit-loss estimation. Zypl serves banks, financial institutions, and public-sector entities, and operates an R&D lab (zehnlab.ai). It is backed by Prosus Ventures. Zypl publishes no public developer/API surface at this time; this profile carries verified identity and a live domain-security probe.

providers.name: Gain Credit
providers.description: GAIN Credit is a market-leading fintech providing responsible, AI-powered credit solutions for people underserved by traditional banks and lenders. The company combines deep financial expertise with advanced, AI-enabled credit-decisioning technology to offer affordable consumer lending, with funds disbursed within roughly 90 seconds of approval. GAIN Credit operates three consumer lending brands — Lending Stream, Drafty, and Afforda — serving the underserved credit market primarily in the UK, with operations across the US and India. Backed by QED Investors, Crosslink Capital, and Mohr Davidow. This corporate profile publishes no public developer API surface; it was surfaced as a QED Investors portfolio company and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline.

providers.name: Raymond James Financial
providers.description: Raymond James Financial is a diversified financial services holding company headquartered in St. Petersburg, Florida, providing investment banking, wealth management, capital markets, asset management, and banking services to individuals, corporations, and municipalities. With more than 7,100 financial advisors serving approximately 3 million client accounts and total client assets exceeding $637 billion, Raymond James is a Fortune 500 firm and one of the largest independent broker-dealers in the United States. The company offers client-facing portals and mobile apps for account management and reporting but does not publish a general-purpose public developer API or machine-readable specification at this time.

providers.name: State Employees' Credit Union
providers.description: State Employees' Credit Union (SECU / NCSECU) is a member-owned, not-for-profit financial cooperative headquartered in Raleigh, North Carolina. Founded in 1937 with 17 members and $437 in deposits, it is a state-chartered credit union regulated by the Credit Union Division of the North Carolina Department of Commerce and federally insured by the NCUA (NMLS #430055). SECU is the second-largest natural-person credit union in the United States by both assets and membership, serving nearly 2.9 million member-owners with roughly $56 billion in assets across 275 branches in all 100 North Carolina counties. Membership is primarily limited to North Carolina state employees and their families. On the open-finance front, SECU operates no public first-party developer portal and publishes no downloadable OpenAPI/Swagger specifications; its consumer digital banking (Member Access) supports connecting external accounts for aggregation, and outbound consumer-permissioned data sharing is handled through data aggregators rather than a documented first-party API. No public FDX-conformant data-access endpoint or CFPB Section 1033 data-rights posture is published as of July 2026.

providers.name: Dwight Capital
providers.description: Dwight Capital LLC is a leading commercial real estate finance company in the United States, with a loan servicing portfolio exceeding $15 billion across all affiliates. The firm originates Balance-Sheet Bridge and New Construction Loans, FHA/HUD Insured Loans, C-PACE Financing, Mezzanine Financing, and Preferred Equity for multifamily, healthcare, and mixed-use commercial real estate. Headquartered in New York City with an additional office in Sunny Isles Beach, Florida, Dwight is consistently ranked among the top FHA/HUD multifamily lenders in the country and operates as a privately held business specializing in bridge-to-HUD execution for commercial real estate sponsors.

providers.name: Fannie Mae
providers.description: Fannie Mae, officially known as the Federal National Mortgage Association, is a government-sponsored enterprise that plays a critical role in the American housing market. Established in 1938, Fannie Mae operates as a secondary mortgage lender, purchasing mortgages from banks and other financial institutions. By buying these loans, Fannie Mae helps to provide liquidity to the mortgage market, enabling banks to lend more money to homebuyers. Fannie Mae operates a developer portal that hosts API integrations for mortgage industry partners; access typically requires authenticated business relationships.

providers.name: Lendtable
providers.description: Lendtable was a US consumer fintech that extended a line of credit so individuals could afford to max out employer-sponsored benefits they would otherwise leave on the table — primarily the employer 401(k) match and Employee Stock Purchase Plans (ESPP). In its own words: "Lendtable gives a line of credit to help individuals get their employer 401(k) match and ESPP." The product advanced cash against a user's paycheck contributions and took a share of the resulting gains, and was distributed direct-to-consumer and through employers via a Lendtable for Business offering, alongside an iOS app and a Zendesk help center. Lendtable was backed by Partech among others. The company now appears defunct: lendtable.com, the blog, and all product paths return HTTP 402 DEPLOYMENT_DISABLED (probed 2026-07-19), the iOS App Store listing is delisted, and the last successful Internet Archive capture of the live site is 2024-12-06. DNS, Google Workspace mail (MX/SPF/DMARC) and the GitHub organization remain registered. No public API, developer portal, or machine-readable API artifacts were ever published by this company.

providers.name: Maywood
providers.description: Maywood is a Y Combinator (W26) artificial-intelligence startup building a finance-compliant, proactive AI platform that automates deal execution for investment banks. The product runs continuously across a banker's network, pipeline, and active M&A processes, generating client-ready CIMs, pitch decks, and financial models, drafting outreach in the banker's voice, and managing due-diligence workflows through a connected data layer that updates automatically. Maywood is built to FINRA and SEC requirements: autonomous within scope, human-approved at every external boundary, and fully reconstructable in between. Founded in 2026 and based in New York City, it is an early-stage SaaS company with no public developer API at this time; this profile tracks its public web, security, and trust surfaces so the network can detect an API program when one appears.

providers.name: Rabobank
providers.description: Rabobank is a Dutch multinational banking and financial services company organized as a cooperative with a strong focus on the food and agriculture sector. It serves retail, business, corporate, and wholesale customers in the Netherlands and operates a global Food & Agribusiness practice through Rabobank Wholesale & Rural and the Rabobank Group internationally. Rabobank publishes a developer portal at docs.developer.rabobank.com (legacy URL developer.rabobank.nl redirects there) exposing PSD2-mandated open banking APIs (Account Information, Payment Initiation, Funds Confirmation) as well as Premium / Beyond-PSD2 commercial APIs for corporate cash management and notifications, with sandbox endpoints for development and a regulated production tier under PSD2 Strong Customer Authentication. Underlying schemes are aligned with the Berlin Group NextGenPSD2 XS2A Framework.

providers.name: Western & Southern Financial Group
providers.description: Western & Southern Financial Group is a Fortune 500 diversified family of financial services companies headquartered in Cincinnati, Ohio. Founded in 1888, the group offers life insurance, annuities, mutual funds, asset management, retirement planning, and investment management through a family of subsidiaries including Western & Southern Life, Columbus Life, Gerber Life, Integrity Life, Lafayette Life, Fort Washington Investment Advisors, Touchstone Investments, and W&S Financial Group Distributors, with over $112 billion in assets under management.

providers.name: Fig
providers.description: Fig (Fig Loans) is a socially conscious, CDFI-certified fintech lender founded in 2015 and based in Texas that offers small-dollar installment loans as a responsible alternative to payday loans, along with credit-builder loans that help underserved borrowers establish and improve their credit. Loans typically range from a few hundred dollars over four-to-six-month terms, and Fig reports repayment to the three major consumer credit bureaus so on-time payments build credit history. Fig operates across a growing set of U.S. states including Texas, Missouri, Ohio, Utah, Florida, Illinois, and California, and partners with CDFIs and nonprofits on community-lending programs. Backed by General Catalyst and Techstars, Fig is profiled in the API Evangelist network as a company; it is a consumer-facing lender and does not publish a public developer API.

providers.name: Fnality International
providers.description: Fnality International is a London-headquartered financial market infrastructure company that builds and operates distributed-ledger wholesale payment systems settling in tokenised central bank money. Backed by a consortium of 24 global financial institutions — including Banco Santander, BNY, Barclays, BNP Paribas, Citi, Goldman Sachs, State Street and UBS — Fnality launched the Sterling Fnality Payment System (£FnPS) in 2024 as the first regulated DLT-based payment system supervised by the Bank of England, with US Dollar and Euro payment systems in development. The systems run on private Ethereum networks, giving participant banks 24/7 availability, real-time atomic and PvP settlement, programmable money and T+0 cross-border liquidity movement. Fnality Services is the operational and product-delivery arm that licenses software to participants and runs inter-system arrangements. Technical documentation for participants is hosted in a credential-gated Archbee space at docs.fnality.com; Fnality publishes no public developer portal, API reference or machine-readable specification.

providers.name: Pinnacle Financial
providers.description: Pinnacle Financial Partners, Inc. (NASDAQ: PNFP) is a Nashville, Tennessee based regional bank holding company whose principal subsidiary, Pinnacle Bank, is a Tennessee state-chartered, FDIC-insured commercial bank (FDIC Cert #35583) originally founded in 2000 as Pinnacle National Bank and renamed in 2012. Pinnacle operates across the Southeast — Tennessee, the Carolinas, Virginia, Georgia and Alabama — serving consumer, small-business, commercial and wealth clients. On the open-finance side Pinnacle runs NO public first-party developer API portal; its consumer digital and mobile banking is delivered on a third-party core/digital platform (Apiture), and consumer-permissioned account and transaction data is made available to fintechs only through data aggregators (Plaid and Finicity/Mastercard) rather than through a documented bank-operated API. No direct Financial Data Exchange (FDX) membership or published CFPB Section 1033 data-access posture was found; open-finance participation is aggregator-mediated.

providers.name: Raseedi
providers.description: Raseedi is an Egyptian financial technology platform that helps underbanked users manage their spending and save money. Through its mobile app it offers free and discounted calls, mobile top-ups and bill payments, cash loans, and a smart dialer, building a community for financial control and savings. Surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network, Raseedi runs a Wix-hosted marketing site with no first-party developer API; its only machine-readable surface is a published llms.txt and the generic Wix Site MCP endpoint.

providers.name: Tala
providers.description: Tala is an AI-native digital financial services company providing instant credit, digital wallets, money transfers, and cash-out services to underserved consumers in informal economies. Built on a proprietary, patent-pending credit-decisioning model trained on billions of dollars of lending data, Tala has delivered more than $7B in credit access to over 13 million customers across Kenya, Mexico, the Philippines, India, Vietnam, Guatemala, Panama, and the Dominican Republic. The company also offers Embedded Credit infrastructure for partners. Tala reaches customers primarily through consumer mobile apps; no public developer API or documentation portal is currently published.

providers.name: Tammwel
providers.description: Tammwel (Tamawal) is a Saudi Arabian digital financing intermediary that connects consumers with licensed financial institutions to compare and obtain Sharia-compliant financing. Its consumer platform and iOS/Android apps let users apply once and receive multiple offers across four products - personal loans, credit cards, auto financing, and mortgage financing (each up to 150,000 SAR) - emphasizing transparent pricing with no hidden fees. The company is a portfolio company of 500 Global. As of this enrichment pass Tammwel publishes no public API, developer portal, documentation, SDK, or /.well-known discovery surface; this profile captures its identity and infrastructure security posture.

providers.name: Alliant Credit Union
providers.description: Alliant Credit Union is a federally chartered, member-owned credit union headquartered in Chicago, Illinois, regulated by the National Credit Union Administration (NCUA). Founded in 1935 as the United Airlines Employees' Credit Union and rebranded Alliant in 2003, it is one of the largest credit unions in the United States, with more than 800,000 members and over $19 billion in assets. Alliant operates as a digital-first, branchless institution offering consumer and commercial deposit accounts, high-yield savings and checking, credit cards, auto and home loans, and business banking. Like nearly all U.S. credit unions, Alliant publishes no public first-party developer API or developer portal; consumer-permissioned data access is available to members only through third-party aggregators (Plaid, MX, Finicity, Akoya) rather than a directly documented open-finance API.

providers.name: Aven
providers.description: Aven is a consumer fintech that issues a home-equity-backed Visa credit card, letting homeowners tap their home equity (a HELOC) through a card with credit-card convenience at lower, home-equity-secured rates. Its product line spans the Aven HELOC card, a Bitcoin-backed Visa card, and educational tooling such as a payment calculator, positioning itself as an AI-driven "machine bank." Founded in the fintech sector and backed by Electric Capital, Founders Fund, General Catalyst, GGV Capital, and Khosla Ventures, Aven operates a consumer marketing and account-servicing web presence at aven.com. As of this enrichment pass Aven publishes no public developer API, developer portal, OpenAPI/AsyncAPI specification, SDKs, or MCP server; this profile captures its verifiable public identity and domain-security posture.

providers.name: HSBC
providers.description: One of the world's largest banking and financial services organizations headquartered in London. Serves over 40 million customers globally with a strong presence in Asia, Europe, and the Americas. Operates a public Developer Portal (develop.hsbc.com) exposing Open Banking, payments, accounts, and global payments solutions APIs for partners and third-party providers.

providers.name: Zest AI
providers.description: Zest AI is an AI-powered lending technology company that provides credit underwriting, fraud detection, and lending intelligence software to credit unions, banks, and specialty lenders. Its machine-learning models automate credit decisioning and risk assessment, and the company reports operating over 600 active lending models in production. Zest AI operates as a B2B SaaS platform delivered to financial institutions rather than as a public developer API; no public developer portal, API documentation, OpenAPI specification, SDKs, or self-service developer surface were found during enrichment.

providers.name: AA Audience
providers.description: AA Audience is an adtech and data company that estimates a mobile user's credit score from their online activity using proprietary machine learning models. It collects data from partner mobile apps and ad networks, analyzes it, and connects with popular DSPs and DMPs so its clients - banks, credit card companies, and financial services firms - can target audiences interested in credit cards, loans, and financial services with guaranteed ROI. Publishers integrate a JavaScript header-bidding tag to enrich their bid stream; advertisers buy segments into their own DMP or as a DealID for their DSP, from a stated floor of $1 CPM. Surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network. No public API, developer portal, documentation, specification, SDK, or public repository was found during enrichment - the site is five static HTML pages served from an S3 bucket whose homepage has not changed since March 2018, and the Login link in the navigation is a dead button on a page with no form.

providers.name: Erad
providers.description: Erad is a licensed, Sharia-compliant fintech lender providing fast, flexible working capital to small and medium-sized businesses across Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates. Founded in 2022 (Y Combinator S22) and headquartered in Riyadh, Erad offers revenue-based financing, invoice financing (advancing up to 90% of B2B/B2G invoices in as little as 48 hours), and supplier financing to revenue-generating SMEs. The company embeds working-capital products into supplier networks and business platforms, and is backed by investors including Y Combinator, 500 Global, Nuwa Capital, Khwarizmi Ventures, Aljazira Capital, VentureSouq, Oraseya Capital and Joa Capital, alongside debt facilities from Stride Ventures and a $125M asset-backed facility led by Jefferies with Channel Capital.

providers.name: Finiata
providers.description: Finiata was a Berlin-founded fintech providing working-capital and invoice financing to small businesses, freelancers and micro-enterprises, operating principally in Germany and Poland and backed by investors including Point Nine. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of point-nine and added to the API Evangelist network as a lead for enrichment. As of the 2026-07-20 enrichment pass Finiata has no live public surface: finiata.com is registered but fully undelegated (no NS, SOA, A, MX or TXT records) and does not resolve; the former developer portal developer.finiata.com, archived as live in 2019, no longer resolves; and finiata.de has been taken over by unrelated third-party gambling-affiliate content. The only live first-party assets found are the company's GitHub organization (github.com/debitech) and one unmaintained internal npm tooling package. No API, OpenAPI or other machine-readable specification, documentation, or well-known surface exists to catalog.

providers.name: Flagstar
providers.description: Flagstar Bank, N.A. is the OCC-chartered national bank subsidiary of Flagstar Financial, Inc. (NYSE: FLG), the Hicksville, New York holding company formerly known as New York Community Bancorp (NYCB). It is one of the largest regional (super-regional) banks in the United States, formed when NYCB acquired Flagstar Bancorp in December 2022, converted Flagstar Bank, FSB into a national bank (Flagstar Bank, N.A.), and subsequently acquired certain assets and liabilities of Signature Bridge Bank from the FDIC in March 2023; the holding company rebranded to Flagstar Financial in October 2024. Flagstar operates in retail and commercial banking, mortgage origination and servicing, and warehouse lending. On the API front, Flagstar runs a first-party developer portal at developer.flagstar.com (a Broadcom/Layer7 "LivePortal" API Developer Portal), but as of this review it publishes no public, self-serve API products, API documentation, or downloadable OpenAPI/Swagger to anonymous visitors — all products are sign-in gated behind partner/consumer-team access. Flagstar has no publicly documented FDX (Financial Data Exchange) participation or CFPB Section 1033 data-access posture; consumer-permissioned data sharing appears to be available only through third-party aggregators (e.g. Plaid, Tink, TrueLayer) rather than a first-party public API.

providers.name: New Residential Investment Corp (Rithm Capital)
providers.description: New Residential Investment Corp (NYSE: NRZ) was a mortgage real estate investment trust (REIT) that **rebranded as Rithm Capital Corp (NYSE: RITM) in August 2022** to reflect its evolution from a pure mortgage REIT into a diversified global asset manager focused on real estate, credit, and financial services. Rithm Capital is headquartered in New York City, led by Chairman & CEO Michael Nierenberg, and as of 2024 reported approximately $46 billion in assets under management, ~$5.2 billion in revenue, and ~6,045 employees across its operating businesses (Newrez mortgage origination/servicing, Genesis Capital business-purpose lending, Sculptor Capital Management alternatives platform, Rithm Property Trust REIT [formerly Great Ajax], Adoor single-family rental, Crestline credit, and Elecor Properties [formerly Paramount Group] office real estate). This profile carries forward the legacy `new-residential-investment` repo identity under the API Evangelist network. The active corporate identity, public filings, and investor communications are at rithmcap.com. Rithm Capital and its subsidiaries operate as financial-services businesses serving institutional investors, mortgage borrowers, and real-estate sponsors. None of the public-facing Rithm Capital, Newrez, Genesis Capital, Sculptor, Rithm Property Trust, Adoor, Crestline, or Elecor Properties websites expose a public developer portal, OpenAPI specification, REST/GraphQL API, SDK, CLI, webhook system, status page, or RSS feed. There are no public GitHub organizations of substance for any of the brand surfaces (the `newrez` GitHub org exists with zero public repositories; `rithmcap` does not exist). Integration with these businesses occurs through traditional B2B mortgage / capital-markets channels, not a public API surface.

providers.name: SigFig
providers.description: SigFig is a San Francisco-based wealth management technology (fintech) company. It operates two lines: "Tandems," an enterprise platform that helps financial institutions deliver intelligent, personalized financial advice, and "SigFig Wealth Management," a consumer robo-advisory service that builds and manages tax-efficient, diversified investment portfolios tailored to each client's goals. SigFig is backed by Bain Capital Ventures, DCM Ventures, and Union Square Ventures. As of the 2026-07-21 enrichment pass, SigFig publishes no public developer API, SDK, MCP server, or developer portal; its site is served behind a WAF and the developer/docs/api subdomains do not resolve.

providers.name: Zeen
providers.description: Zeen is an AI-powered autonomous personal finance platform — a money copilot that connects to your financial accounts and uses background AI agents to manage money on your behalf. Its features include an interactive AI financial copilot that answers questions in real time, Guard (loss prevention that avoids overdraft fees and cancels unused subscriptions), Grow (yield optimization that moves idle balances to higher-interest accounts), and Guide (spending insights). As of mid-2026 Zeen is in pre-launch with a public waitlist. Zeen is backed by Cowboy Ventures and is tracked in the API Evangelist network as a company profile.

providers.name: Knight Fintech
providers.description: Knight Fintech is a Mumbai-based banking technology company that sells digital lending infrastructure to Indian banks and NBFCs. It positions itself as "India's leading digital lending infrastructure platform", stating it powers 500+ financial institutions across co-lending, digital lending, treasury management, supply chain finance, embedded finance and credit line on UPI, alongside a Knight Aurix product line. The company describes its approach as cloud-first, API-driven middleware that integrates with legacy core banking systems without displacing them. It is enterprise sales-led: there is no public developer portal, no published API documentation, no SDKs and no self-service signup — evaluation runs through a scheduled demo.

providers.name: TD Bank Group
providers.description: TD Bank Group (The Toronto-Dominion Bank) is one of Canada's Big Six chartered banks — a federally regulated Schedule I bank headquartered in Toronto and listed on the TSX and NYSE under the ticker TD. It is among North America's largest banks by assets, serving roughly 27 million customers worldwide across Canadian Personal & Commercial Banking (TD Canada Trust), U.S. Retail (TD Bank, N.A. — America's Most Convenient Bank, a separately profiled entity), and Wholesale Banking (TD Securities). Like the rest of Canada's banking sector, TD's open-finance posture is voluntary: Canada's Consumer-Driven Banking framework was legislated in 2024 (Consumer-Driven Banking Act) but is not yet operational, so the Canadian parent exposes no first-party public developer API. Consumer financial-data access today is aggregator-based — TD signed a North American data-access agreement with Plaid in December 2023 — while payments run over the shared Canadian rails (Interac e-Transfer and Payments Canada's Real-Time Rail, with Interac as the RTR exchange solution provider). The FDX-aligned, Akoya-based open-banking API suite published at developer.td.com belongs to the U.S. subsidiary TD Bank, N.A., not this Canadian entity.

providers.name: Inyad
providers.description: Inyad is an all-in-one business management and payments platform for small and medium businesses across Morocco, the Middle East, and Africa. Its mobile-first apps let merchants sell, get paid, and run their operations from one place — including a smart point-of-sale (POS Mahaal), automatic invoicing, an online store builder, employee attendance and payroll (Staff), a digital credit book (Konnash), in-store card terminals and terminal-free digital collection (Collect), professional business accounts, and money-transfer services. The company reports 250,000+ professionals on the platform and is backed by investors including Partech, Al Mada Ventures, CDG Invest, and FJ Labs. Inyad exposes an internal application backend (api.inyad.com) but publishes no public developer API, documentation, or SDKs at this time.

providers.name: PennyMac Financial Services
providers.description: PennyMac Financial Services, Inc. is a specialty financial services firm focused on the production and servicing of U.S. residential mortgage loans. The company is one of the largest mortgage lenders and servicers in the United States, providing financing to homebuyers and refinancing to existing homeowners. PennyMac operates through correspondent, consumer direct, and broker channels.

providers.name: Vymo
providers.description: Vymo is a sales-engagement and distribution-management platform for financial institutions — banks, insurers, and asset managers — helping field sales and collections teams manage leads, allocate and prioritize activities, and capture engagement in a mobile-first app. It layers AI-driven nudges, activity capture, and analytics on top of CRM and core systems, and integrates with existing enterprise ecosystems. Vymo does not publish a self-serve public developer API or documentation portal; its integrations are delivered through enterprise/partner connections. Backed by Emergence Capital and headquartered in Sunnyvale, California.

providers.name: Cambridge Blockchain
providers.description: Cambridge Blockchain, Inc. was a blockchain-based digital identity and compliance software company founded in 2015 and headquartered in Cambridge / Boston, Massachusetts. Its enterprise platform let financial institutions deliver strong digital identities to end users while meeting KYC/AML and data privacy obligations (including European GDPR), giving individuals control over their own personal identity data shared across institutions. The company was backed by investors including Partech and PayPal, and was acquired by Blockchains, Inc. in December 2020, after which its team and identity technology were folded into Blockchains' digital identity product. The former company website (cambridge-blockchain.com) is no longer served; the surviving public developer surface is its GitHub organization and two first-party npm cryptographic libraries. No public HTTP API, OpenAPI specification, developer portal, or hosted documentation was ever published.

providers.name: McGraw Hill Financial
providers.description: McGraw Hill Financial was a financial information and analytics company providing credit ratings, benchmarks, and analytics to global capital and commodity markets. The company was renamed S&P Global in 2016. No public developer APIs are currently documented under the McGraw Hill Financial brand.

providers.name: Monedo
providers.description: Monedo, founded in Hamburg in 2012 as Kreditech and renamed Monedo in March 2020, was a German online consumer lender that underwrote short-term and installment credit in Poland, Spain, Russia, Romania, India and Mexico using a self-learning machine-learning scoring engine over thousands of alternative data points instead of traditional bureau scores. Backed by Peter Thiel, J.C. Flowers and Naspers, it was valued above EUR 230m in 2017. It marketed a business-facing Lending-as-a-Service / Credit-as-a-Service partner API that let retailers, telcos, banks and payment providers embed its credit products and point-of-sale financing, but that surface was sales-gated for its whole life: the company never operated a public developer portal, never published a reference, and never published a machine-readable contract. Monedo filed for insolvency in a Hamburg court in September 2020 and ceased operations in December 2020. Both monedo.com and kreditech.com lapsed and were re-registered by unrelated parties in 2022 - monedo.com is now a GoDaddy aftermarket listing offered for sale - so no company-controlled web or API surface remains.

providers.name: Prospera Credit Union
providers.description: Prospera Credit Union is a member-owned cooperative financial institution headquartered in British Columbia, Canada, formed on January 1, 2020 through the merger of the original Prospera Credit Union and Westminster Savings Credit Union — the largest credit-union merger in Canadian history. With roughly CA$9 billion in assets under management, about 120,000 members, and some 900 employees across branches in Metro Vancouver, the Fraser Valley, and the Okanagan, it is the third largest credit union in British Columbia and among the six largest in Canada. As a provincially regulated cooperative (credit unions in BC are overseen by BC Financial Services Authority and deposits are protected by the Credit Union Deposit Insurance Corporation of BC), Prospera serves personal and business members with chequing and savings accounts, credit cards, mortgages, loans, and Interac e-Transfer. On the open-finance side, Prospera runs NO public first-party developer portal or documented API — none of developer/api/developers.prospera.ca resolve — and Canada's federal Consumer-Driven Banking (open-banking) framework, legislated in Budget 2024 and overseen by the FCAC, is not yet operational. Like most Canadian credit unions, Prospera reaches national payment rails and consumer data-sharing through shared credit-union-system infrastructure rather than a proprietary API, and third-party data access today is aggregator/screen-scraping based (e.g. Flinks, Plaid). This is an honest identity-only profile with no public API surface to catalog.

providers.name: Ramre
providers.description: Ramre (RamRe) is the brand associated with Ram Reinsurance, now operating as American Overseas Group Limited (AOG) — a Bermuda-based insurance holding company that is tax resident in the United Kingdom. Through its U.S. subsidiaries the group writes non-standard automobile insurance and provides related management services, and it operates as a reinsurer through a subsidiary based in Barbados. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of Canaan Partners and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. An enrichment pass found no public developer program, API, documentation, or SDK surface: this is a financial-services holding company whose public web presence (ramre.com now redirects to aoreltd.com) is corporate and investor-relations oriented, with no machine-readable API artifacts to catalog.

providers.name: wefox
providers.description: wefox is a Berlin-headquartered digital insurance distribution platform that connects insurance carriers, brokers, and end customers through a single technology stack. Founded in 2014 and originally known as FinanceFox, the company operates across Germany, Austria, Switzerland, Italy, the Netherlands, Spain, and France, selling personal-lines products such as motor, home, liability, life, and commercial insurance via its in-house carrier (wefox Insurance) and a network of independent brokers. wefox positions itself as an "indirect" insurtech — meaning it distributes through human advisors augmented by software rather than selling direct-to-consumer — and has historically been one of Europe's most highly funded insurtech companies, with backing from Mubadala, Target Global, Salesforce Ventures, OMERS Ventures, Eurazeo, Mountain Partners, and others. The platform itself is a multi-tenant SaaS used by brokers and agents to manage customer relationships, quote and bind policies across multiple carriers, handle claims, and trigger commissions. wefox does not publish a public developer portal, OpenAPI specifications, SDKs, or a github.com/wefox organization; integration with the wefox platform is carrier-, broker-, and partner-mediated rather than self-service, and there is no Tier-1 developer surface to document. This repo profiles wefox as an insurance distribution business and tracks any future move toward a public API program.

providers.name: PenFed Credit Union
providers.description: PenFed Credit Union (Pentagon Federal Credit Union), founded in 1935 and headquartered in McLean, Virginia, is a federally chartered credit union regulated by the National Credit Union Administration (NCUA) and one of the largest credit unions in the United States, with roughly 2.9 million members and tens of billions of dollars in assets. It is a not-for-profit, member-owned financial cooperative that originally served the U.S. military and defense community and now offers open membership, providing mortgages, auto loans, credit cards, personal loans, and deposit accounts. On the open-finance front, PenFed runs an internal API-management practice — MuleSoft/Anypoint is the backbone of its digital-banking platform and an Apigee-backed developer portal host exists at developer.penfed.org (with an api.penfed.org gateway) — but neither surface is publicly documented or openly reachable: there is no public developer program, no published OpenAPI, and consumer account data is made available to members through permissioned third-party aggregators such as Plaid rather than a directly documented FDX or CFPB Section 1033 data-access API.

providers.name: Adjoint
providers.description: Adjoint Inc. is a Boston, Massachusetts fintech (founded 2016) that built distributed-ledger and smart-contract software for corporate treasury and insurance. Its flagship platform, Uplink, let financial firms onboard assets onto a permissioned ledger, manage balances, and author self-executing agreements in Adjoint's Financial Core Language (FCL), with SDKs to bridge to traditional systems. The company raised roughly $10.4M and competed with Kyriba, Trovata, and Modern Treasury. As of this enrichment pass the company appears dormant: its adjoint.io domain now resolves to a parked/expired Namecheap page, its GitHub organization returns 404, and no first-party client SDKs are published to public registries. This profile is a VC-portfolio enrichment stub; see the data-quality note below regarding the originally-attached website.

providers.name: Alassio
providers.description: Alassio is a French financial-technology company building a next-generation payroll software platform (logiciel de paie nouvelle generation) for businesses. Alassio positions itself as offering the functional depth expected of a specialist payroll and HR tool, with added transparency and control for finance and people teams. The company is backed by venture-capital firm Partech and operates from France, serving the French and European payroll, compensation, and human-resources market. As of this profile the company publishes only a marketing landing page and a legal notice; no public API, developer documentation, SDK, or integration surface has been located. This profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-lead stub awaiting a public developer surface to enrich.

providers.name: Alongside
providers.description: Alongside is an a16z-backed crypto company (alongside.xyz) founded in 2022. It originally launched the Alongside Crypto Market Index (AMKT), the first on-chain broad crypto market index token with a 0% annual fee, backed by Andreessen Horowitz, Coinbase Ventures, and Franklin Templeton. The company has since pivoted to AI-native compliance automation for scaling crypto firms, unifying fragmented KYC/AML/KYT tooling into a single system and reducing manual analyst burden for autonomous financial agents. As of this enrichment pass Alongside publishes no public API, developer portal, SDKs, MCP server, or developer documentation; this profile captures its identity and probed domain security only.

providers.name: Alterya
providers.description: Alterya is an AI-powered fraud-prevention company founded in 2022 (Y Combinator; seed round led by Battery Ventures, ~$9.8M) that detects authorized-fraud scams — authorized push-payment (APP) scams, pig-butchering and romance scams, money-mule and synthetic accounts, and social-engineering-driven withdrawals — before victims send funds. It connects fraud signals across crypto rails and traditional fiat/bank rails, and prior to acquisition monitored more than $8B in transactions per month for exchanges and fintechs including Binance, Coinbase, and Block, protecting roughly 100M end users. Chainalysis acquired Alterya in January 2025 for a reported ~$150M; it now ships as the "Alterya by Chainalysis" fraud-prevention product. The standalone alterya.com domain is parked and the company operates entirely inside Chainalysis, with no independent public developer portal, API, or OpenAPI surface.

providers.name: Artivest
providers.description: Artivest was a New York-based alternative investments technology company founded in 2012 that gave financial advisors and high-net-worth investors a curated digital experience for discovering, evaluating, and subscribing to private investment funds, including its "Open Network" platform serving roughly 1,800 advisors and management of 28 proprietary alternative investment funds. iCapital Network announced the acquisition of substantially all of Artivest's assets — technology, operating platform, fund management, and enterprise relationships — on 2020-05-13 and closed the transaction in August 2020. The Artivest brand, platform, and public web presence were fully absorbed into iCapital; as of this enrichment pass artivest.co does not resolve and artivest.com is registered to an unrelated third party. Artivest never published a public developer portal, API documentation, or machine-readable API artifacts, and there is no live surface remaining to enrich.

providers.name: Ayannah
providers.description: Ayannah (Ayannah Information Systems, Inc.) is a Philippines-based fintech company providing digital finance and digital commerce services to the emerging middle class across emerging markets, many of whom are migrants and/or unbanked. It operates a market-proven stack of digital financial services spanning payments, commerce, and analytics, reporting 10K+ touchpoints and 50M+ transactions processed. Marquee products include Sendah Direct (a B2B SaaS payment platform for retailers offering mobile top-ups, game credits, and domestic remittance, adopted in 7,000+ outlets), Sendah Remit (bank-grade interoperable international and domestic remittance), Sendah (a B2C gift-remittance service for Overseas Filipinos), and Asira (Indonesian B2B2C/B2C lending, insurance, and investment apps). Ayannah is backed by 500 Global. This profile is maintained by the API Evangelist network; the company publishes a corporate marketing site but no public developer portal, API documentation, or machine-readable API specification at this time.

providers.name: Babel Finance
providers.description: Babel Finance was a Hong Kong-based crypto financial services provider offering crypto asset lending and borrowing, asset management, brokerage and derivatives trading, and mining-related financing to institutional and high-net-worth clients. It reached a USD 2B valuation on an USD 80M Series B in May 2022 with backing that included Multicoin Capital, then froze customer redemptions and withdrawals weeks later in June 2022 amid the Three Arrows Capital and Celsius contagion. The company disclosed roughly USD 766M in losses, pursued a Singapore court moratorium and a scheme of arrangement, and floated a crypto-backed stablecoin to repay creditors. As of this enrichment pass the company is listed as permanently closed and its primary domain babel.finance no longer resolves (no NS delegation), so there is no live developer portal, documentation, or API surface to catalog. This profile is retained as a historical record of a defunct crypto-lending provider.

providers.name: BankOns
providers.description: BankOns was a San Mateo, California mobile savings startup founded in the summer of 2010 by Joshua Greenough, a former VP of Operations at PowerReviews. Launched in May 2011, the app connected a user's bank transaction history to their location, analyzing spending habits to surface the nearby merchant deals and rewards best suited to them, drawing on Foursquare and other local deals data. The name was a contraction of "bank" and "coupons". BankOns was seed funded by 500 Startups (now 500 Global) plus a friends-and-family round. In May 2012 Capital One acquired select BankOns software through a limited asset purchase agreement, and several team members including Greenough joined Capital One Labs. The product was wound down and the company no longer operates a consumer service or a developer platform. The bankons.com domain resolves to a GoDaddy parking lander with no content, and no API, documentation, SDK, or developer surface exists.

providers.name: Benny
providers.description: Benny is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of matrix-partners and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Sector: fintech. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Bumped
providers.description: Bumped was a Portland, Oregon-based fintech that rewarded consumers with fractional shares of publicly traded stock in the brands and companies they shop with, turning everyday spending and loyalty into equity ownership. Backed by Canaan Partners, the company operated a consumer investing and rewards application before winding down its consumer product. It was surfaced through the Canaan Partners portfolio and added to the API Evangelist network. During enrichment no live public developer surface, API, documentation, package, or well-known discovery endpoint could be located -- the primary domain (bumped.com) no longer resolves and related domains are parked -- so this remains an identity-only profile with no active API artifacts.

providers.name: Carr, Riggs & Ingram (CRI)
providers.description: Carr, Riggs & Ingram (CRI) is a top-25 nationally ranked accounting and advisory firm headquartered in Alabama, operating 70+ locations across 13 states plus Mexico. The firm delivers audit and attest, tax, and advisory services (cybersecurity, fraud and forensics, valuations, and transaction advisory) to more than 18 industries, alongside value add-on subsidiaries including CRI Advanced Analytics, CRI CFO Hub, and CRI M&A Advisors, and is a member of PrimeGlobal. It was surfaced via the VC-portfolio pipeline and enriched here; note that criadv.com is a professional-services accounting firm, not a Bessemer-backed fintech startup, so the portfolio-lead tagging is a domain false-positive. No public API, developer portal, or documentation surface exists.

providers.name: cashbus
providers.description: CashBus (现金巴士), operated by Micro-Credit Speed Express (Group) Co., Ltd. (微额速达集团有限公司) of Shanghai, is a Chinese mobile financial-technology platform providing quick microloans to underserved consumers who lack access to traditional banking. The company runs an automated, AI-driven credit decision engine that scores applicants in seconds using thousands of risk factors and big-data analysis, with risk management spanning pre-loan, in-loan, and post-loan stages. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Qiming Venture Partners and added to the API Evangelist network. The public presence is a corporate marketing site (company vision, team, careers, contact) with no published developer portal, API documentation, or machine-readable API surface at this time.

providers.name: Cashforce
providers.description: Cashforce is a fintech platform focused on cash flow forecasting and working-capital analytics for corporate treasury and finance teams, connecting ERP systems, bank accounts, and financial data to give companies real-time visibility into cash positions, liquidity, and forecasting scenarios. Originally a Techstars-backed portfolio company, Cashforce was acquired by Billtrust and its standalone product surface is no longer independently operated; this API Evangelist profile tracks the company's public footprint. No public developer portal, API documentation, or machine-readable API definitions are currently reachable at the cashforce.com origin (the site returns HTTP 522), so this record carries identity and domain-security signals only.

providers.name: Circa Labs
providers.description: Circa Labs (Circa) was a fintech and proptech startup that operated a rental wealth platform helping renters build financial assets and accelerate their wealth. Backed by Techstars, Circa has since merged with Stake to continue its mission of accelerating renter wealth, and the wearecirca.com site now points to the combined company. No public API, developer platform, SDKs, or developer documentation are published by Circa Labs at this time.

providers.name: ConnectCapital
providers.description: ConnectCapital is a private equity investment firm, established in 2000, that made investments in early and expansion stage companies providing enterprise application and infrastructure software and solutions. It was surfaced as a portfolio entry of Insight Partners and added to the API Evangelist network as a lead for enrichment. Enrichment probing on 2026-07-20 found no operating web presence - the connectcapital.com domain is parked on GoDaddy nameservers and redirects every path to a lander, and connect-capital.com is listed for sale. ConnectCapital is an investor, not an API producer, and has no developer portal, documentation, or API surface to catalog.

providers.name: Cyota, Inc
providers.description: Cyota, Inc was a cybersecurity company founded in 1999 in New York City by Naftali Bennett, Lior Golan, Michal Tzur, and Amir Orad, focused on online banking fraud, e-commerce fraud, and anti-phishing protection. Cyota pioneered token-less consumer authentication and risk-based fraud detection for financial institutions, reportedly holding a majority share of the US and UK e-commerce authentication markets. Backed by Bessemer Venture Partners, the company was acquired by RSA Security on December 30, 2005 for approximately $145 million, after which its technology was folded into RSA's Identity and Fraud portfolio (RSA Adaptive Authentication / FraudAction). Cyota no longer operates as an independent entity and publishes no live developer surface, API, or documentation. This profile is retained for historical/network provenance only.

providers.name: Dealflo
providers.description: Dealflo was a UK-based financial-technology company that provided an automated agreement, identity-verification, and e-signature platform used by lenders and financial institutions to capture, verify, and legally bind financial agreements end to end. It was acquired by OneSpan (formerly VASCO Data Security) in September 2018 for roughly USD 55 million and folded into OneSpan's Digital Agreements / electronic-signature product line. The dealflo.com domain now 301-redirects to onespan.com and Dealflo no longer operates an independent developer program, public documentation, or API. This record is retained in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio/company lead surfaced from the HV Capital portfolio; no independent API artifacts exist to enrich because the product surface has been absorbed by OneSpan.

providers.name: eCredit.com
providers.description: eCredit.com was an online trade-credit and credit-decisioning company, surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a Battery Ventures portfolio company. It no longer operates independently. The ecredit.com domain is delegated to Moody's nameservers and 301-redirects in full to Moody's trade-credit offering, where "Moody's eCredit" now exists as a platform within Moody's Trade Credit product line. Enrichment probes confirm no independent developer portal, documentation, API specification, or /.well-known surface remains on ecredit.com. Any live API capability for this product is delivered through Moody's, which is profiled separately in the network as the successor company.

providers.name: Equitable Bank
providers.description: Equitable Bank is Canada's seventh largest independent Schedule I bank by assets and a wholly owned subsidiary of EQB Inc. (TSX: EQB), a Toronto-based Canadian financial services company with over CAD $144 billion in combined assets under management and administration. Federally chartered and Canadian owned, Equitable Bank markets itself as "Canada's Challenger Bank" and, in 2016, launched EQ Bank, its digital-only banking platform offering high interest savings accounts, GICs, and payments alongside the parent bank's single-family residential and commercial lending. Equitable Bank and Equitable Trust are members of the Canada Deposit Insurance Corporation (CDIC). On the open-finance front, Equitable Bank does not operate a public first-party developer portal or publish downloadable API specifications; consumer permissioned data sharing is delivered through the Canadian aggregator Flinks (Flinks Outbound) rather than a first-party API. Canada's federal Consumer-Driven Banking framework (legislated in Budget 2024 with the Financial Consumer Agency of Canada as overseer) is not yet operational, so the bank's data-access posture today is voluntary and aggregator-mediated.

providers.name: Fluidly
providers.description: Fluidly was a London-based intelligent cashflow forecasting fintech founded in 2016 by Caroline Plumb, providing SME cash-flow prediction, scenario planning, and working-capital tools used by roughly 1,300 UK accountancy firms. OakNorth Bank acquired Fluidly in December 2021 and folded the product into its Credit Intelligence Suite; the independent Fluidly brand has since been retired and fluidly.com now redirects to OakNorth's partnerships page. This profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as an acquired-company record — no independent Fluidly developer portal, OpenAPI, or public API surface remains.

providers.name: Fortune Technology (China FIF)
providers.description: Fortune Technology, listed by Qiming Venture Partners as one of the largest commercial factoring companies in China, historically operating at china-fif.com. Commercial factoring is a trade-finance business: purchasing accounts receivable from suppliers at a discount to provide working capital. As of the 2026-07-20 enrichment probe the company publishes no developer surface of any kind — no public API, no documentation portal, no OpenAPI or other machine-readable specification, and no /.well-known/ discovery documents. The china-fif.com domain no longer serves the company: HTTPS is refused outright (port 443 closed) and plain HTTP returns an unrelated Chinese Premier League sports-streaming site running EmpireCMS. This record is retained as an honest negative result for the API Evangelist network rather than deleted.

providers.name: Futureadvisor
providers.description: FutureAdvisor was a Y Combinator-backed robo-advisor that provided automated, algorithm-driven investment management and portfolio recommendations to retail investors. It was acquired by BlackRock and folded into the firm's digital wealth offerings; the consumer FutureAdvisor product has since been wound down. As of this enrichment pass the domain futureadvisor.com is controlled by BlackRock (its nameservers resolve to blackrock.com) but publishes no live website, developer portal, API documentation, SDKs, or any public developer surface. No API artifacts could be searched, fetched, or derived — this remains an identity-only record for a defunct/absorbed provider.

providers.name: Hedgeye
providers.description: Hedgeye Risk Management is an independent investment-research and financial-media firm founded in 2008 by Keith McCullough and headquartered in Stamford, Connecticut. Hedgeye sells subscription research and market analysis to investors across macroeconomics, sector/vertical coverage, and individual securities, delivered through daily notes, models, and its Hedgeye TV video platform, newsletters, and live events. The company is best known for its data-driven, process-oriented "GIP" (growth, inflation, policy) macro framework and its independent, no-conflicts positioning relative to traditional Wall Street sell-side research. As surfaced in the API Evangelist network, Hedgeye operates a consumer/subscriber web application at app.hedgeye.com but does not publish a public developer program, API, SDK, or machine-readable discovery surface; this profile captures the identity and domain-security posture that could be verified without authenticated access.

providers.name: Home Account
providers.description: Home-Account (Home Account) was a consumer financial-services startup focused on mortgage management and consumer credit-risk analytics, backed by Uncork Capital (formerly SoftTech VC). Per its LinkedIn profile, the company built patent-worthy consumer risk-analytic tooling to help homeowners manage mortgages and understand consumer credit risk, operating in the Consumer Services sector with roughly 11-50 employees and a base in the Fort Mill, South Carolina (ZIP 29708) area. Its original website, home-account.com, no longer resolves, and Uncork Capital's portfolio record associates the company with Bills.com. No public API, developer portal, OpenAPI, or other machine-readable API artifacts were found during enrichment; this record remains an identity-only profile of a legacy/defunct portfolio company added to the API Evangelist network as a VC-portfolio lead.

providers.name: Legg Mason
providers.description: Legg Mason was a global asset management firm offering investment products and services through a network of investment affiliates before being acquired by Franklin Resources (Franklin Templeton) in 2020. Investor resources and product information are now consolidated under Franklin Templeton, and no public REST APIs or developer portal have been identified.

providers.name: LendUp Global
providers.description: LendUp Global, Inc. was a San Francisco consumer-lending fintech backed by a16z, operating through LendUp Loans, LLC (formerly Flurish, Inc.) to offer short-term and installment credit to subprime borrowers. The company is DEFUNCT — LendUp Loans, LLC ceased loan operations in January 2022. It has no live developer surface, no public API, no documentation host, and no maintained code repositories. The lendup.com domain is now operated by an unrelated entity (LendUp LLC, Dover, DE) that publicly disclaims any corporate relationship to LendUp Global, Inc.; its properties must NOT be attributed to this company profile. Retained in the network as a historical a16z portfolio record.

providers.name: Lu Pu Investment (陆浦投资)
providers.description: Lu Pu Investment (陆浦投资), operating through Shanghai Luxiang Fund Sales Co., Ltd. (上海陆享基金销售有限公司), is a China-based wealth-management and public mutual-fund distribution business serving retail investors. It offers fund subscription and purchase (认/申购), automatic investment plans (定投), and wealth-advisory services through dedicated financial advisors, delivered via its website and mobile app. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Qiming Venture Partners. No public developer, API, or technical integration surface was found during enrichment.

providers.name: Magnetis
providers.description: Magnetis is a Brazilian digital wealth management and automated investment (robo-advisor) platform, backed by 500 Global, that offered goal-based portfolio recommendations and managed investment accounts to retail investors in Brazil. The company was acquired by BTG Pactual, and the magnetis.com.br domain now redirects to BTG Pactual's investimentos platform; no independent public developer program or API surface is currently published.

providers.name: Merklebase, Inc.
providers.description: Merklebase provides data-driven infrastructure for institutional digital-asset finance, spanning enterprise data management, a core portfolio management system, reporting and accounting, risk management, a trade capture system, and a digital-asset loan management system. It advertises connectivity to 220+ custodians, trading venues, and data providers, and is used by hedge funds, asset managers, and financial institutions to streamline front-to-back operations across fiat, crypto, derivatives, and stablecoins. A developer API and connectivity layer is referenced by customers, but the public developer surface (docs.merklebase.io on Theneo) is currently unpublished and the API (api.merklebase.io, AWS API Gateway) is gated, so no public OpenAPI/SDK artifacts are harvestable yet.

providers.name: Noah
providers.description: Noah (originally founded as Patch Homes in 2016 and rebranded to Noah in 2020) was a US-based home-equity investment fintech backed by Union Square Ventures. It offered homeowners up-front financing in exchange for a share of their home's future appreciation, as an interest-free, no-monthly-payment alternative to a HELOC or cash-out refinance. The company raised roughly $156M across five rounds from seven investors before ceasing operations in 2024. This record is retained in the API Evangelist network as a historical VC-portfolio lead; no live public API, developer portal, or documentation surface was found during enrichment.

providers.name: O11
providers.description: O11 is a Y Combinator (Winter 2026) startup building custom AI software for financial services firms. Rather than forcing teams onto a new external platform, O11 embeds AI-driven automation directly into the tools finance teams already use every day — Excel, PowerPoint, Word, and other enterprise applications — so users can generate presentations, spreadsheets, and documents and automate workflows without switching contexts. The company positions itself against the observation that a majority of firms still rely on legacy software where generic bolt-on AI features fail to deliver real value. As of this profile O11 publishes a marketing site (o11.ai) but no public developer API, OpenAPI specification, SDKs, or developer documentation could be found; this remains an early-stage identity profile in the API Evangelist network awaiting a public API surface.

providers.name: Rasyonet
providers.description: Rasyonet is a Turkish fintech company providing integrated financial software solutions and capital markets data platforms for institutional clients, asset managers, and financial analysts. Founded in 2000 and headquartered at ITU ARI Teknopark in Istanbul, Rasyonet offers tools for analyzing global equity markets, economic indicators, mutual and pension funds, fixed-income securities, portfolio analytics, and automated financial reporting. Their flagship EquityRT platform delivers equity research, company valuation, and peer benchmarking capabilities via desktop and Excel integration. No public developer API or machine-readable specification has been documented at this time.

providers.name: Rowspace
