providers.description: Rowspace builds AI infrastructure for major asset managers, converting fragmented institutional knowledge into clean, structured data that AI can reliably operate on. Founded in 2024 by Michael Manapat (former CTO of Notion and Head of Applied ML at Stripe) and Yibo Ling (former Chief Business Officer of Binance), the company operates under Emergence Capital's "Agentic Software" thesis with the positioning "You built your firm's edge. Compound it with AI." As of this enrichment pass Rowspace publishes only a marketing website (www.rowspace.ai) and has no public developer portal, API documentation, or machine-readable API surface; this profile captures verified company identity and a domain-security probe.

providers.name: Samastha Synergy Pte. Ltd.
providers.description: Samastha Synergy Pte. Ltd. operates Djoin (djoin.id), positioning itself as a "digital partner for sustainable scale" that helps financial institutions and organizations in Indonesia grow through an adaptive product ecosystem. Djoin's named products are Coopmax (a platform aimed at cooperatives / koperasi), Kocek, and ProofyLink. The company runs a private backend API at api.djoin.id, which sits behind Cloudflare and returns 403 to unauthenticated requests; as of this profile there is no public developer portal, OpenAPI/Swagger definition, documentation, or SDK surface published. Samastha Synergy was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment; this profile captures what is publicly verifiable from the djoin.id site and DNS/TLS probes.

providers.name: Samunnati
providers.description: Samunnati is an integrated agri-enterprise platform working to de-fragment India's agricultural value chain by connecting farmers, Farmer Producer Organizations (FPOs), and agri enterprises. It combines financial solutions (lending to farmers, FPOs, and agri businesses), trade facilitation and market linkages, and digital marketplaces (FPO Next, Trade Next, and input, output, credit, and consumer marketplaces), alongside innovation, research, and foundation-led community work. Operating across Chennai, Hyderabad, Bengaluru, Delhi, Mumbai, Kolkata, Jaipur, Odisha, Uttar Pradesh, and Bihar, it positions itself as one of India's largest agri enterprises. Samunnati runs several customer-facing digital platforms but does not publish a public developer portal or API at this time.

providers.name: SeedFi
providers.description: SeedFi was a U.S. consumer fintech that offered credit-building loans and savings products (its "Credit Builder Prime" and "Borrow & Grow" plans) aimed at helping financially underserved borrowers build credit history and cash savings simultaneously. Backed by a16z and other investors, SeedFi was acquired by Cross River Bank in 2022, and its consumer offerings were subsequently folded into Credit Karma (Intuit). The seedfi.com domain now 302-redirects to a Credit Karma support article; SeedFi operates no independent developer portal, public API, documentation, or OpenAPI surface. This profile is retained as a network company record with no API to enrich.

providers.name: Shara
providers.description: Shara (Shara Technology Management Nigeria Ltd) is a Lagos-based fintech that provides collateral-free working-capital loans of up to NGN 10 million to Nigerian small and medium-sized businesses. Sole traders, partnerships, and limited companies apply through Shara's website or Android app with basic business details and a bank statement, and receive a free loan estimate in seconds with approval typically in 48 hours to two weeks. The company reports over NGN 50 billion disbursed across 100,000+ loans to 7,000+ business customers. Shara publishes no public API, developer portal, or documentation.

providers.name: Sheroes
providers.description: Sheroes is a women-only social network and community platform based in India, founded in 2014 by Sairee Chahal. It gives women a safe, moderated space to connect, ask questions anonymously, seek support, learn, and grow across communities spanning careers, health, relationships, parenting, entrepreneurship, and personal finance. The platform operates a mobile app and website, offers helpline and expert support, and has expanded into women-focused financial services (MahilaMoney). Sheroes was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass Sheroes exposes no public developer API, OpenAPI definition, developer portal, or documented event/webhook surface; the site is a fully client-side single-page application. This profile therefore captures the company identity plus a live domain-security probe of its public host.

providers.name: Shriram City
providers.description: Shriram City (Shriram City Union Finance Ltd) was a leading Indian non-banking financial company (NBFC) in the Shriram Group, offering personal, business, two-wheeler, gold and small-enterprise loans plus fixed deposits. Founded 1986 in Chennai, it was surfaced as a portfolio company of bessemer-venture-partners. In November 2022 the company was amalgamated into Shriram Finance Ltd; its www.shriramcity.in host no longer resolves and the shriramcity.in apex now redirects to shriramfinance.in. No public developer or API program was found. This profile was enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline: web search + live domain/security/well-known probes.

providers.name: Silver Tail
providers.description: Silver Tail Systems was a website fraud and abuse detection company founded in 2008 in Menlo Park, California by Mike Eynon and Laura Mather, both formerly on the anti-fraud team at eBay/PayPal. Its product collected and analyzed real-time web traffic to deliver web session intelligence and predictive analytics that detected fraud, account takeover, and abuse on banking and commerce websites. Backed by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) among others, the company raised roughly $20M across three rounds before being acquired by RSA, the security division of EMC, in 2012 and rebranded as RSA Web Threat Detection. It no longer exists as an independent company and publishes no live developer or API surface.

providers.name: SK Finance Ltd
providers.description: SK Finance Ltd (skfin.in) is a Jaipur, India-based non-banking financial company (NBFC) providing asset-backed retail lending. Its products span commercial vehicle, car, tractor, construction-equipment and two-wheeler loans alongside secured business loans and home-renovation / mortgage finance, delivered through a physical branch network with EMI calculators, online EMI payment, a branch locator, a loan-application portal and a customer "Refer and Earn" referral program. Backed by Norwest Venture Partners. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes a corporate/marketing website (Next.js) with no public developer portal, API documentation, SDKs or other machine-readable API surface.

providers.name: Standard Economics
providers.description: Standard Economics is building an "economic computer" aimed at financial inclusion and intelligent capital allocation at global scale, describing a system with memory, judgment, and the ability to improve its own decisions to deliver economic security. Its product surface is Uno (uno.global). The company is backed by Lightspeed Venture Partners and Paradigm, and was added to the API Evangelist network from VC-portfolio discovery. As of the latest enrichment pass it publishes no public API, developer portal, documentation, SDKs, or /.well-known/ discovery surface; this profile currently carries only a domain-security posture probe.

providers.name: SwitchMe
providers.description: SwitchMe was a Mumbai, India based fintech startup founded in 2012 and backed by 500 Global that helped consumers evaluate and switch their home loans and mobile service providers, handling document collection and submission on their behalf. The company appears to be defunct: no public developer program, API, or documentation could be found, and its switchme.in domain currently resolves to unrelated content. This profile records what could be verified during the enrichment pass; there is no API surface to catalog at this time.

providers.name: Three Wheels United
providers.description: Three Wheels United is a fintech-driven electric vehicle financing company in India, founded in 2017 by Cedrick Tandong, Kevin Wervenbos, and Apurv Mehra. It works to remove the financial barriers to clean mobility by providing loans for two- and three-wheeler electric vehicles — starting with auto-rickshaws — disbursed through its RBI-registered NBFC lending partner Shabri Investments Private Limited. The company pairs credit with a mobile app that helps drivers manage their loans and connect to services, and reports over 4,000 vehicles financed, 20,000+ customers served, and thousands of tonnes of CO2 reduced across Bangalore, Mumbai, and the Delhi NCR (Noida) region. It is backed by Techstars, Delta Corp Holdings, Asian Development Bank Ventures, Microsoft, and other global investors, having raised roughly $10 million in Series A funding. It is a consumer-facing lender with no public developer program, API, or SDKs.

providers.name: Wealor
providers.description: Wealor is an AI-native platform for wealth managers, building a centralized, queryable source of truth across wealth management, tax, legal, estate, and insurance. The platform captures data from conversations, financial documents, tax returns, legal documents, and custodial systems into a single knowledge layer, then uses specialized AI agents to automate operational work — account opening, client subscriptions, tax optimization, trade rebalancing, and billable client-plan generation — directly across legacy partner portals and internal systems via APIs and browser automation. Founded in 2026 by Karim Bouri and Pierre Depuydt and backed by Y Combinator (P26 batch), Wealor is based in San Francisco. As of this profile it is an API consumer with no public developer API, documentation, or specification surface.

providers.name: whatiseven
providers.description: whatiseven (Even, formerly Even Responsible Finance) was an earned-wage-access and personal-finance fintech that let workers access a portion of their pay before payday, budget with "okay to spend" guidance, and automatically save. Backed by Slow Ventures, Even was acquired by One (Walmart's fintech venture, now OnePay) and folded into the OnePay @Work earned-wage-access product ("Instapay"). The whatiseven.com domain now redirects through even.com to onepay.com/atwork. Even operates no independent public developer platform, API, or documentation, and the acquirer OnePay publishes no public API surface either. This profile is retained as a network record of the company and its acquisition.

providers.name: Zeitgold
providers.description: Zeitgold was a Berlin-based fintech that automated bookkeeping, invoice and receipt processing, payments, and financial administration for small and medium-sized businesses, blending software with human back-office review. It was backed by Battery Ventures and other investors and was acquired by Deel in 2021. As of this enrichment pass the company operates no independent public developer surface: zeitgold.com does not respond on HTTP or HTTPS, and zeitgold.de resolves to a parked/reserved domain page. No public API, developer portal, documentation, OpenAPI, or other machine-readable artifact could be discovered, so this profile remains an identity-only record.

providers.name: Iman
providers.description: IMAN (mobile app IMANUM, operated by IMAN CAPITAL LTD) is a halal fintech and Islamic-finance super-app serving Muslim-majority, largely unbanked markets in Central Asia. Headquartered in Uzbekistan and expanding into Kazakhstan, Pakistan, South Asia and MENA, IMAN bundles Sharia-compliant financial products into a single consumer app: IMAN Invest, a faith-based investing platform where users and IMAN enter Mudarabah contracts to finance real trade in goods, and IMAN Pay, an interest-free buy-now-pay-later / point-of-sale installment product for the previously unbanked. All services are certified compliant with Islamic finance principles by scholars including the Muslim Board of Uzbekistan. IMAN was the first Central Asian startup backed by 500 Global and has raised over $6M from strategic and institutional investors.
